https://www.internazionale.it/ultime-not.heading: Russia steps up attacks on Ukraine’s digital infrastructure, Kyiv says - Internazionale
https://www.internazionale.it/ultime-not.body:
Oct 23 (Reuters) - Russia is attacking Ukraine’s digital infrastructure with the same intensity as its embattled power grid, Kyiv’s prime minister said on Friday, calling on government agencies to quickly form cybersecurity teams.

In a statement, Sergiy Koretskyi said Russia had struck 10 data centres in the capital Kyiv last month alone, and warned that AI-aided cyberattacks on state information systems and businesses were also on the rise.

“Russia is attacking our digital infrastructure as systematically as it is attacking our energy sector,” he said.

“Key digital agencies are already able to repel attacks using AI,” he added. “I expect the same readiness from every state agency and institution.”

Moscow’s forces have begun battering Ukrainian energy infrastructure ahead of winter, after a summer campaign of expanding Russian strikes on logistics, businesses and data centres.

Ukraine has also extended its strikes from Russia’s energy industry to include e-commerce giants.

Russia’s mounting attacks on Ukraine come as Kyiv struggles to repel the ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones used in those attacks, amid a shortage of air-defence weapons.

Some of Kyiv’s defensive and battlefield capabilities have also been hampered by recent restrictions on its use of the US-based Starshield satellite internet service.

(Reporting by Dan Peleschuk; Editing by Aidan Lewis)

https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/rus.heading: Russia, Ukraine agree on ceasefire in embattled town, to hold peace talks next month | Reuters
https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/rus.body:
Oct 23 (Reuters) - Ukraine and Russia said on Friday they had agreed on a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky, brokered through US first lady Melania Trump, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr ​Zelenskiy said peace negotiators would meet next month for new talks.

The two sides said the ceasefire would go into effect on October 27, allowing the delivery of aid and the evacuation of residents ‌through humanitarian corridors.

Get a look at the day ahead in European and global markets with the Morning Bid Europe newsletter. Sign up here.

Amid a US push to organise new talks aimed at ending the 4-1/2-year-old war, Zelenskiy said negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States had agreed to technical-level meetings in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi. A US official later said the three countries may hold their next talks in a couple weeks in Abu Dhabi or Switzerland.

Zelenskiy said he hoped a meeting of the countries' leaders would follow.

Previous rounds of talks headed by the United States stalled in February with no significant progress towards ending the bloodiest ​conflict in Europe since World War Two. Russia continues to demand Ukraine cede all of the eastern Donbas region, including territory Russia has not occupied militarily, while Kyiv rejects any notion of giving up land it ​currently holds.

The latest peace efforts follow a rift between Washington and Kyiv in recent weeks and a series of moves by US President Donald Trump seen as favouring Russia.

A major ⁠source of friction was limitations placed on SpaceX's Starlink communication system that Ukraine uses to protect against incoming attacks. Trump said on Friday that if Ukraine still faced a problem with the system, he would straighten it out and, if necessary, speak ​about the matter to SpaceX (SPCX.O), opens new tab CEO Elon Musk.

Another contentious point was Trump's announcement of a deal to allow Russia to provide diesel for the US and global markets, an agreement denounced by Ukraine and meant to keep prices down as ​the president's Republicans contest US midterm elections.

On Friday, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said the first three tankers with Russian diesel were on their way to North America.

In the town of Oleshky, occupied by Russian forces since February 2022, residents have reported that they faced a deepening food crisis.

"Both nations agreed to temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway," the White House said in a statement.

The chief of staff of Russian forces, Valery Gerasimov, ​said on the Defence Ministry's Telegram channel that Russian troops would halt fire from 4 a.m. local time (0100 GMT) on October 27 to allow for the humanitarian operation to start.

Ukraine's General Staff issued a statement agreeing to observe the ​ceasefire from the same time and pledging to "do everything possible to help Oleshky's residents." Ukraine says it has already used drones twice to send food into the town.

Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, also said the ceasefire would go into effect on October 27 and ‌told Reuters the ⁠operation would involve demining roads to the town, deliveries of food and evacuations of civilians.

Item 2 of 2 A still image taken from an undated drone video released September 12, 2026, shows a destroyed buildings in Oleshky, Kherson Region, Russian-controlled Ukraine. 34th Separate Marine Brigade "Borysfen"/Handout via REUTERS/File Photo

\[2/2\] A still image taken from an undated drone video released September 12, 2026, shows a destroyed buildings in Oleshky, Kherson Region, Russian-controlled Ukraine. 34th Separate Marine Brigade "Borysfen"/Handout via REUTERS/File Photo Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab

Both sides said Melania Trump played an important role in coordinating the agreement. The first lady has been active in trying to get Ukrainian children seized by Russia during the war returned to their families.

"Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster," she said in a statement.

"Oleshky's remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food and clean water."

Pope Leo had spoken in the past week both to Zelenskiy and to Russian President Vladimir Putin about conditions in Oleshky.

The White House said Oleshky, located across the Dnipro River from the Ukrainian-held city of Kherson, had 1,700 ​to 2,000 residents remaining, down from 24,000 before the war.

Zelenskiy's comments on resuming peace talks followed a ⁠meeting with US presidential envoy Steve Witkoff in Norway early this week and a subsequent meeting between Witkoff and Putin in St Petersburg.

Zelenskiy said he spoke on Friday with Witkoff and US envoy Jared Kushner. He said any peace agreement would need strong security guarantees for Ukraine and funding for 10 years to maintain the Ukrainian army.

"The plan is to ​meet in the first half of November, and as early as possible, of course," Zelenskiy told the Hudson Institute think tank via a video link. He said ​much would depend on Russia, noting ⁠that a similar meeting expected this month had not materialised.

Zelenskiy spoke of the importance of continued diplomatic efforts to reach a ceasefire and end the war, now in its fifth year, adding that Europe should also be involved in the talks.

Ukrainian officials said on Friday that speed restrictions on Starlink systems in Ukraine remained in place, despite Trump's previous statement that the services had been fully restored.

Trump told reporters at the White House on Friday that he had not spoken to Musk about the ⁠restrictions but would ​do so if required.

"If there is a problem, I'll get it straightened out," he said. The caps have been in place since October ​13.

Ukraine and Russia also swapped 270 servicemen each in a prisoner exchange on Friday, the Russian Defence Ministry said. Zelenskiy described the swap, the first since August, as a "very important result."

Ukraine's acting prosecutor, Anton Kovalskyi, writing on Telegram, said more than 19,000 Ukrainian civilians, including 762 children, had been killed ​since Russia launched its full-scale war more than four years ago.

https://www.politico.eu/article/ukraine-.heading: Ukraine and Russia each exchange 270 prisoners of war – POLITICO
https://www.politico.eu/article/ukraine-.body:
KYIV — Ukraine and Russia both swapped 270 prisoners of war Friday in the third stage of the process that started on Aug. 19.

Kyiv returned home 261 military personnel and nine civilians, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a statement.

“Most of those released are warriors who defended Ukraine in Mariupol. Defenders from the Donetsk, Luhansk, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Kyiv, Mykolaiv, and Chernihiv sectors are also returning. Many were illegally convicted in Russia. Among those returning are five people who were believed to have been killed in the Russian terrorist attack in Olenivka in July 2022,” Zelenskyy added. “A very important result.”

Moscow’s defense ministry also confirmed the exchange in a statement, saying Friday that the 270 exchanged Russian prisoners were in Belarus.

A prisoner exchange deal was brokered by U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration in May. The process is expected to involve 2,000 prisoners of war in total, Zelenskyy said at the time. The latest wave of exchanges took place soon after the end of another round of negotiations in Oslo and St. Petersburg.

“We express our gratitude to the United States of America and the United Arab Emirates, and in particular, we thank everyone who contributed to the release of Stephen Hubbard — a 74-year-old English teacher from Izium who was unlawfully convicted and subjected to torture by the Russians,” Ukraine’s Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War said in a statement.

Most of the military personnel handed over to Ukraine had been detained since 2022, authorities said. Some had even been captured in 2018 and 2020, during the war in Donbas.

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.heading: US and Israel are warned against launching fresh strikes on Iran | Middle East and north Africa | The Guardian
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.body:
Foreign ministers at a summit of eight European and Middle Eastern countries have urged the US and Israel not to renews their attacks on Iran, warning a fresh outbreak of fighting would spread conflict and push oil prices even higher.

The development of a new multinational “anti-war bloc” represents a challenge to the increasingly open plans by the US and Israel to relaunch strikes on Iran while talks on Tehran’s nuclear programme remain deadlocked.

The Turkish foreign minister, Hakan Fidan, joint convener of the summit in Istanbul, said: “Military intervention in Iran is not any kind of solution. We agreed that a new military attack would spread the war and the conflict in the region. All the countries around the table do not want the war to spread even more, once again.”

Ministers also demanded an end to the Houthi assaults on Saudi Arabia, and an immediate opening of the strait of Hormuz currently blockaded by Iranian ships and drones.

Jean-Noël Barrot, the French foreign minister, said another war between Iran and the US would be bad for both sides, and only worsen rising oil prices, which have hit their highest level since May. Ed Miliband, the UK foreign secretary, also urged both sides to embrace diplomacy.

The Istanbul meeting, an unprecedented gathering of regional and European leaders initiated by Turkey and Germany, represented a rare chance for European ministers to have any input into the crises afflicting the Middle East, including in Yemen, Palestine and Iran. They have largely been left as bystanders, apart from sending air force protection to Saudi Arabia as it tries to fend off Houthi drone and missile assaults on its airports and energy installations.

The Middle Eastern states were represented by Fidan, Egypt’s Badr Abdelatty, Pakistan’s Ishaq Dar and Saudi Arabia’s Faisal bin Farhan. Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia formed the Mecca defensive security pact in August, a grouping Egypt may join.

The European side was represented by Barrot, Miliband, Germany’s Johann Wadephul and Italy’s Antonio Tajani. The agenda covered the Palestinian issue, including settlement expansion, settler violence and the two-state solution, as well as security in the strait of Hormuz, Yemen and efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war and prevent spillover into the Black Sea.

Wadephul said: “We are united by the impact these deadlocked conflicts are having on the economy and security of our countries and by the will to seek new ways to bring about solutions.”

He made no criticism of the US but accused “the Houthis and Iran of blackmailing world trade and continuing to stranglehold global supplies of energy and fertiliser”.

“We are feeling the effects of the attacks on shipping routes and whether at the petrol pump or the supermarket,” he said. “Elsewhere there is threat of famine.”

Tajani said the aim of the meeting was to work for “de-escalation to guarantee freedom of navigation”.

“I do not believe the problem can be solved from a purely military standpoint,” he added. “If we want to reopen Hormuz, which is vital for our economies, we must promote dialogue and make Iran understand that this attitude cannot continue.”

https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-eas.heading: Iran has detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if war resumes, officials say | Reuters
https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-eas.body:
DUBAI, Oct 23 (Reuters) - Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to target undersea communications cables in the Gulf if the United States and Israel attack Iran again, two senior Iranian security officials ​told Reuters.

Their comments followed warnings by Iranian officials that undersea cables in the region could become targets in any renewed conflict if diplomacy with Washington ‌collapses.

The Reuters Iran Briefing newsletter keeps you informed with the latest developments and analysis of the Iran war. Sign up here.

The two Iranian security officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, gave few details and did not say how or where exactly Tehran would carry out such attacks. But one of them said Iran would aim to prevent repairs after any attacks to prolong disruptions to communications, including internet connections.

"If Iran is attacked, there will be no more red lines ... from undersea cables to military bases, including covert ones," one ​of the officials said.

The official warned Washington not to "play with fire", and said Iran had full access to the undersea cables and could easily destroy them.

Yadollah ​Javani, the deputy head of political affairs for Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC), said on Wednesday that Iran could target seven major internet cables beneath ⁠the Strait of Hormuz if Iranian infrastructure came under attack.

Undersea cables carry around 99% of global internet traffic, according to the International Telecommunication Union, a UN agency. But the ​global impact of such attacks by Iran could be limited as less than 1% of international bandwidth passes through the Strait of Hormuz, said Alan Mauldin, research director at telecommunications ​research firm TeleGeography.

The strait separates Iran and Oman, linking the Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea.

The US Department of State and Iran's Foreign Ministry did not respond to Reuters' requests for comment on the Iranian security officials' remarks. There was no immediate comment from Gulf states.

The plans for possible attacks on undersea cables reflect a conviction in Iran's leadership that a renewed US military ​campaign would have to be met with a stronger response than before.

Top security official Mohsen Rezaei warned this month that US-linked digital infrastructure across the Gulf, including data centres and ​AI facilities, could be targeted in a renewed conflict.

Item 2 of 2 Vessels at the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, October 23, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer

\[2/2\] Vessels at the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, October 23, 2026. REUTERS/Stringer Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab

Washington's Gulf allies have invested heavily in such infrastructure and they "should hold Washington, not Tehran, responsible for any damage to undersea cables," the second Iranian ‌security official ⁠said.

Alex Vatanka, director of the Iran program at the Middle East Institute in Washington, said such threats were intended to deter renewed conflict and put pressure on Washington by making Gulf governments and US companies fear for their investments in the region.

"Tehran wants Gulf states and corporate executives to press (US President Donald) Trump over the risks his policies pose to their investment plans," said Vatanka.

Cable routes are stylized and do not reflect the actual positions (Source: TeleGeography)

Multiple cable cuts could slow internet services and disrupt financial transactions, e-commerce and cloud computing, analysts said. The impact would depend on how operators rerouted traffic and ​the capacity available on alternative connections, Mauldin said.

Restoring ​connections during wartime could be difficult, ⁠experts said, and higher insurance costs and delays in obtaining permits to enter territorial waters could further complicate repairs.

The Red Sea could offer a more significant target than the Strait of Hormuz, particularly if Iran had support from its Houthi allies in Yemen, though Tehran ​has made no public statement indicating it plans to target cables there.

The Red Sea carries data between Europe, East Africa and ​Asia, with capacity routed ⁠through it accounting for about 3% of global international demand and around 10% of traffic travelling between regions, Mauldin said.

Cable routes are stylized and do not reflect the actual positions (Source: TeleGeography)

Gulf governments have been investing heavily in technology to diversify beyond oil and become global artificial intelligence hubs, deepening ties with US technology firms.

Iranian strikes directly hit two Amazon Web Services facilities in the UAE in March and damaged infrastructure near one of its ⁠facilities in Bahrain. ​The IRGC named US tech companies including Microsoft, Google, Apple and Nvidia as legitimate targets at the ​height of the war in March.

Land-based connections can provide alternative routes for internet traffic, and Gulf states and US technology companies are investing in additional infrastructure to improve resilience.

Microsoft plans to invest more than $400 million in subsea ​and terrestrial connectivity across the Middle East by 2030.

OSCE Secretary General Feridun H. Sinirlioğlu took part in the Berlin Process Leaders' Summit in Budva, Montenegro, joining leaders from across Europe, including Southeastern Europe, to discuss regional cooperation and shared challenges.

“Southeastern Europe is at a crossroads. With an important election season underway, ongoing social tensions testing the resilience of institutions, and old scars that continue to leave a deep mark, we are at a critical moment for the entire region.

The OSCE remains committed to security and stability in the region. We support national authorities on their reform paths, facilitate dialogue and reconciliation, promote confidence-building measures and counter transnational threats such as organized crime and the proliferation of small arms and light weapons,” Secretary General Sinirlioğlu said.

The Secretary General emphasized the importance of strong and resilient democratic institutions, as well as public trust, in building peaceful and stable societies. Reflecting on the OSCE's longstanding engagement in the region, he highlighted the importance of building on progress achieved, strengthening regional cooperation and preventing new crises.

During his visit, Sinirlioğlu met with leaders from across the region. He reaffirmed the OSCE's readiness to work with partners in Southeastern Europe to strengthen resilience, enhance regional cooperation and support lasting peace and security.

TIRANA, 23 October 2026 — Albania has signed a deal to join an international security force in Gaza, clearing another step towards sending up to 40 troops.

Army chief Arben Kingji signed the agreement on Friday with US Major General Jasper Jeffers, who commands the force.

Albania’s parliament approved the mission last month, allowing troops to help protect aid deliveries, military personnel and facilities, and monitor security.

The force is part of US President Donald Trump’s Gaza peace plan and will operate under American command.

No date has been announced for the Albanian troops to leave.

https://sarajevotimes.com/with-the-eu-su.heading: With the EU Support, BiH Institutions Address FATF Grey List Challenges - Sarajevo Times
https://sarajevotimes.com/with-the-eu-su.body:
Bosnia and Herzegovina’s institutions are stepping up efforts to tackle money laundering and terrorist financing, bringing together authorities from across the country to address shortcomings identified by international financial watchdogs and strengthen the integrity of the BiH financial system.

At an international conference in Sarajevo, representatives of more than 30 institutions from the state, entity, cantonal and Brčko District levels joined counterparts from Croatia and Serbia, alongside European Union representatives and international experts, to examine how Bosnia and Herzegovina can turn its commitments under the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Action Plan into measurable institutional progress.

The conference was organized in close cooperation with the Ministry of Security of Bosnia and Herzegovina, with support from the European Union Police Assistance for Bosnia and Herzegovina (EUPA4BiH) project.

The meeting comes four months after FATF placed Bosnia and Herzegovina on its so-called grey list in June 2026, subjecting the country to increased international monitoring. FATF acknowledged improvements in strategies, financial investigations, and the exchange of financial intelligence, but it also identified persistent weaknesses in supervision, risk assessment, and the effectiveness of measures against financial crime.

The Ministry of Security of Bosnia and Herzegovina has taken a central coordinating role in the BiH response, initiating the development of an inter-agency Grey List Exit Programme (GLEP) in cooperation with EUPA4BiH. The programme is intended to translate FATF recommendations into concrete institutional responsibilities, implementation priorities, and coordinated measures.

Representatives of the Ministry of Security of BiH, Ministry of Justice of BiH, Ministry of Finance and Treasury of BiH, State Investigation and Protection Agency (SIPA), Border Police of BiH, Indirect Taxation Authority, and Agency for Prevention of Corruption and Coordination of the Fight against Corruption were joined by authorities from the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Republika Srpska and Brčko District. Among them were the banking agencies and securities commissions of both entities, tax administrations, insurance regulators, police authorities, prosecutors’ offices, and professional associations.

Representatives of the European Union, the United States, and international organizations, including the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), contributed to the exchange of expertise and perspectives on strengthening BiH anti-money laundering systems.

The conference also reflected the European Union’s broader support for institutional reforms in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Through EUPA4BiH, the EU is providing technical assistance, specialist expertise and capacity-building support to help domestic institutions strengthen financial investigations, improve information exchange and advance compliance with international standards.

These efforts complement Bosnia and Herzegovina’s EU Reform agenda priorities, including the implementation of anti-money laundering legislation and the alignment of domestic practices with European and international requirements. FATF’s Action Plan, with implementation scheduled through January 2029, requires sustained institutional engagement and demonstrable improvements in areas ranging from risk-based supervision and suspicious transaction reporting to money laundering investigations, terrorist financing, and the enforcement of targeted financial sanctions.

The conference concluded with a working session dedicated to immediate implementation priorities.

The European Union Police Assistance for Bosnia and Herzegovina (EUPA4BiH) project is funded by the European Union and implemented by the Center for International Legal Cooperation (CILC), in partnership with IRZ, CIVIPOL, FIAP and CPMA. The EUPA4BIH project supports police agencies and other competent institutions in Bosnia and Herzegovina in strengthening their capacities to combat organized crime, corruption, financial crime, terrorism, and other serious security threats.

https://www.mina.news/en/article/gorcevi.heading: Gorcevic: Montenegro fulfills all requirements and final benchmarks in EU accession process
https://www.mina.news/en/article/gorcevi.body:
Podgorica, (MINA) – Montenegro has fulfilled all obligations in the EU negotiating process and submitted to the European Commission (EC) for assessment its negotiating position for the remaining open chapters, Minister of European Affairs Maida Gorcevic has announced.

Speaking at the press conference, she said that this was one of the most significant milestones in the EU accession process so far.

Gorcevic pointed out that Montenegro fulfilled the promise given to its citizens and European partners, stressing that it was the only candidate country that had met all the final benchmarks and fulfilled all its obligations.

She outlined the negotiation process path, stating that currently 21 chapters had been provisionally closed, while, as she said, the conditions had been met for closing the remaining 12 by the end of the year.

Gorcevic recalled that the European integration process involved almost 1,000 reform activities, including the adoption of strategic documents, laws and by-laws, as well as strengthening of institutions and administrative capacities.

She stressed that during the negotiations the focus was not only on improving the legislative framework, but also on modernization of existing institutions, development of information systems and strengthening of professional capacities.

Speaking about the next steps, she said that the negotiating positions were now being reviewed by the EC and EU member states, which were expected to agree on proceeding with closing the chapters.

“We expect that in the next few weeks we will certainly have another intergovernmental conference, but you will be informed about the dynamics by the EC”, stated Gorcevic.

She expressed the expectation that after closing the remaining negotiating chapters, Montenegro would address chapters 34 – Institutions and 35 – Other Issues, which are led by the EC, rather than Montenegro.

Gorcevic pointed out that the Ministry of European Affairs expected extensive amount of work in the preparation and translation of the EU legal acquis, which includes around 350,000 pages.

Speaking about the drafting of the accession treaty, Gorcevic said that an ad hoc working group had been formed this year to draft it, and that the goal was for the treaty to be signed in 2027.

She remarked that next year, in addition to the signing of the EU accession treaty, Montenegro was also expecting the start of the ratification process in the parliaments of all 27 member states.

Gorcevic noted that the elections in several member states, including France, Poland, Italy and Spain, could affect the dynamics of that process, which was why Montenegro would have to develop a strategic plan and adapt its diplomatic activities to the political circumstances in each country.

“This means that during that period, Montenegro will not be able to count on the implementation of that procedure, but we can focus on other countries until the election processes are completed”, Gorcevic explained.

She said that the EC’s report on Montenegro was expected in the first week of November and would be the last report under the current format, which, as she assessed, was a sygnal that the end of the negotiation process was approaching.

Gorcevic said that she expected the report to be the best so far, bearing in mind the results achieved by Montenegro during its EU negotiations.

Commenting on open bilateral issues with Croatia, including restitution, war crimes and missing persons, Gorcevic pointed out that it was in Montenegro’s interest to resolve bilaterally all issues that could be settled before EU membership.

She confirmed that the Government had not yet made a decision on potential compensation for the Morinj detainees, including the EUR 17 million mentioned in the public.

Asked whether Croatia could seek to have its demands addressed in the common EU negotiating position, Gorcevic explained that each member state could raise additional questions and put forward demands during the consideration of the negotiating positions, but in order for them to become part of the common negotiating position, the consent of all 27 EU members was required.

Commenting on the messages of Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic that there was sufficient time, as well as the conclusions that did not set additional deadlines, Gorcevic said that Montenegro should wait for the presentation of roadmaps for the enlargement process before putting forward additional demands or deadlines.

https://skopjediem.com/uncategorized/mic.heading: Mickoski at Berlin Process Summit: Artificial Hurdles Continue to Delay Our EU Path - SkopjeDiem
https://skopjediem.com/uncategorized/mic.body:
North Macedonia has long deserved EU membership but remains unable to begin accession negotiations for “artificial reasons”, PM Hristijan Mickoski said Thursday at the Berlin Process Summit in Montenegro.

“I expect strong messages in support of the Western Balkans’ integration into the EU, including Macedonia. My government remains strongly committed to the EU reform agenda and European integration, and we will continue working in that direction. We are living in very challenging times, perhaps among the most difficult this century. We are witnessing Russia’s war in Ukraine, the conflict involving Iran, financial market turmoil and protests across Europe. We must find a way out of these crises, particularly in Europe, and my government is firmly committed to contributing to that effort”, Mickoski said.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said that Germany strongly supports EU membership for Western Balkan countries, but accelerating integration also depends on domestic reforms and political will.

“EU membership is what we want for you. You can count on Germany’s support, as well as my personal support. As the European Union, we have done our part, but you must do yours as well. Reforms and political will must come from you”, Merz said.

Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker sent a strong message, stating that bilateral disputes must not block the enlargement process. He called for the immediate, gradual integration of all six Western Balkan nations into the EU internal market, ending roaming with the EU, and joining SEPA. He added that there is no justification for the Western Balkans to be at a disadvantage compared to Ukraine or Moldova.

https://english.republika.mk/macedonia/s.heading: Sali met with Kos in Brussels: gradual integration should bring specific benefits - Republika English
https://english.republika.mk/macedonia/s.body:
Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for European Affairs Bekim Sali met with European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos in Brussels. The discussion focused on Macedonia’s European perspective, the implementation of the Reform Agenda, and opportunities for the country to be gradually integrated into European Union policies and programs.

Sali welcomed the European Commission’s communication, “Preparing for a Wider Union,” emphasizing the importance of a more predictable enlargement process based on merit and measurable results. He stated that European integration should deliver tangible opportunities for citizens, the economy, and businesses, while reforms should progressively bring the country closer to the European Single Market.

The meeting also covered the Growth Plan for the Western Balkans, as well as reforms in the areas of the rule of law, public administration, digitalization, energy, and economic competitiveness. Specific benefits of gradual integration highlighted during the discussion included participation in the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA), the potential expansion of the “Roam Like at Home” model, and cooperation on digital transformation.

Furthermore, Sali underscored the significance of the EU’s future Multiannual Financial Framework for the 2028–2034 period, which, in his view, should provide stable and predictable support for candidate countries. During the visit, European Commissioner Kos gave an interview to media representatives from Macedonia. The Ministry of European Affairs announced that it would continue to cooperate with European institutions with the aim of accelerating reforms and delivering concrete results for the citizens.

https://www.tanjug.rs/english/politics/2.heading: Macut: Good relations with Hungary to help Serbia on EU path
https://www.tanjug.rs/english/politics/2.body:
BUDAPEST - Serbia's caretaker PM Djuro Macut said on Friday in Budapest, where he attended a ceremony that marked the 70th anniversary of the Hungarian Revolution of 1956, that Serbia-Hungary relations had been traditionally good in recent years and would help Serbia on the EU path.

In a statement to Serbian media outlets, Macut said he had briefly met with Hungarian PM Peter Magyar and that they would hold a discussion later in the evening, in what would be the first meeting between a Serbian official and the new Hungarian PM.

"I think we will have some discussion topics, and that will be my first opportunity to also meet with the new Hungarian PM and, certainly, to say that we are always here and that we should continue on already established paths: our mutual relations and all that is actually connecting our nations, and the opening of a new rail line between Belgrade and Budapest will definitely be one of them," Macut said.

He added that the rail line would be opened by the New Year, likely within a month or two.

He noted that the Serbs and Hungarians had exceptional historical ties, above all, in terms of the Serb and Hungarian communities living in Hungary and Serbia, respectively, as well as economically and in terms of transport.

"Today, we know that building mutual cooperation, mutual understanding and building bridges between nations can lead to a better future and prosperity to the benefit of both our nations. Our history tells us that, in the future, too, building our mutual relations upon mutual trust, a desire to build our future together and to forge ties, infrastructurally, economically, in education and in every other way, will help us set off for Europe together and give the region we are in a European perspective, and together be a part of the European community and make our nations a part of the great European nations," Macut noted.

He also said the ceremony had demonstrated that the universal values of freedom, independence and a desire of nations to live in peace and harmony represented a symbol of freedom and universal values.

EC: We take attempts to discredit MEP election observers very seriously
                - Vesti iz Srbije, regiona i sveta - N1 info
https://n1info.rs/english/news/ec-we-tak.body:
The European Union (EU) takes very seriously any attempts to discredit election observers drawn from the European Parliament and expects all countries to engage constructively with international election observation missions, European Commission (EC) spokesperson Christian Wigand said in Brussels on Friday.

Regarding Serbian Parliament speaker and acting Serbian President Ana Brnabic’s protest over the composition of the European Parliament observation delegation for the October 25 Serbian parliamentary elections, Wigand said that the work of international observation missions is based on clear standards, impartiality, and long-standing expertise.

“Specifically on the election observation missions, let me be clear that we take any attempts to discredit members of the European Parliament and the election observers very seriously,” Wigand said at the Friday press briefing.

He added that election observation missions deployed by well-established international organizations, including those featuring members of the European Parliament, play an important role in ensuring that democratic processes and accountability are respected.

“Their work is based on clear standards, impartiality, and long-standing expertise, so we expect all countries, including of course candidate countries and potential candidates, to engage constructively and transparently with recognized international election observation efforts,” Wigand said.

The EC spokesperson reiterated that the EU is closely following the upcoming elections in Serbia, and noted that free, fair and transparent elections are at the core of European democracy and that they “must be organized in line with European and international standards.”

“The deployment of the long-term OSCE ODIHR election observation mission at the request of the Serbian authorities, as well as the invitation to the European Parliament, are important steps toward ensuring credible election observation and supporting the contribution of domestic observers to the integrity of the electoral process,” Wigand said.

Earlier, Brnabic - who also serves as Serbia’s acting president - sent a letter to European Parliament President Roberta Metsola, protesting the makeup of the EU legislative body’s election observation mission, particularly targeting the appointment of Andreas Schieder as its head.

In the letter, Brnabic argued that the past public conduct of several mission members proves they are “politically biased,” but the European Parliament announced it has no intention of changing the lineup of the delegation set to observe Serbia’s October 25 parliamentary elections.

Alongside numerous domestic monitors, Serbia’s parliamentary elections will be monitored by several international missions deployed by ODIHR, the European Parliament, the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly, and the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe.

Brussels/Prishtina, 23 October 2026, dtt-net.com – The European Union told Kosovo Albanian lawmakers I a public statement that they have no right to change the law on special war crimes law locate in The Hague, without its prior consent, thus welcoming the decision of the newly elected Kosovan President to return to the legislative body for review, following a weird request made by the very same opposition party which on October 7 made the parliament to change some elements of it following the sentencing of its former leader and former President Hashim Thaçi and three other former leaders of the now disbanded Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) which fought for liberation and independence from Serbia, on war crimes charges during the 1998-1999 war.

“The European Union welcomes the decision by Kosovo’s President Justina Shiroka-Pula to return the law, amending and supplementing the Law on the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, to the National Assembly for reconsideration,” spokesperson of EU foreign service EEAS.

The changes sponsored by the main opposition Democratic Party (PD) would limit the mandate of the court and also include eventual retrial to be moved to the court in capital Prishtina, in case the appeal panel decides retrial.

But the EU has expressed “deep concern” without explicitly clarifying what exactly it is contesting in the changes of October 7 during the tense session.“The EU has consistently expressed its deep concern about the initiative to amend the Law on the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, both prior and after its adoption by the Kosovo Assembly on 6 October 2026. In the spirit of the 2014 exchange of letters between the EU High Representative and the Kosovo President, which sets out the modalities for consulting the EU before changing the legislation, we expect that the European Union be consulted if discussions resume in the Assembly. Rule of law and the protection of fundamental rights, including those of the victims and witnesses, remain of paramount importance,” spokesperson said.

“The Kosovo Specialist Chambers is an independent judicial institution established by decisions of the Kosovo Assembly in 2014–2015, based on a Special Agreement with the EU, operating within the Kosovo legal system and enshrined in Kosovo’s Constitution. Their current mandate and independence must be fully and unreservedly respected. The EU stands in solidarity with all victims, survivors and their families from all communities affected by wartime atrocities,” reads the statement.

American Judge Charles Smith announced on September 16th that the panel of judges sentenced the four for being responsible on charges of “arbitrary detention of 385 individuals (Albanian and Serbs); cruel treatment against 49 individuals; torture against 303 individuals and murder against 96 individuals” in Kosovo and northern Albania by members of the KLA they were leaders of.

The sentences take credit of their times served in The Hague court since 2020 detention.

According to the verdict, the victims were Albanians and Serbs considered by the Kosovo guerilla members of being collaborators of Serbia, spies and traitors.

According to the indictment, the crimes charged were committed from at least April 1998 to June 1999 and took place in several locations across Kosovo as well as in Kukës and Cahan, in Northern Albania.

Two other former KLA members are already sentenced to prison terms in separate trials in The Hague.

The prosecution had sought 45 years of imprisonment for each of the four former KLA leaders.

Earlier this month the prosecution sought additional 6 years of imprisonment for Thaçi on charges of pressure on witnesses during the trial.

Formation of the EU-sponsored and USA-backed special court was triggered by a report of the late Swiss politician, Dick Marty, adopted in 2011 by the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe.

Marty said in his report that Thaçi, the former speaker of Parliament Kadri Veseli, Jakup Krasniqi, also a former Speaker of Parliament, and former member of the Parliament Rexhep Selimi, engaged in human organ harvesting of Serb and Albanian civilians during and after the 1998-1999 war, which they have denied.

The indictments by the prosecution have not included human harvesting allegations by Marty.

Many in Kosovo see the court financed by the EU, UK and the USA; as “mono-ethnic” and of “selective justice” imposed by western powers.

The office of the prosecution has ignored war crimes committed by Serbia army, police and paramilitaries on ethnic Albanian civilians during the 1998-1999 war, despite EU-27 governments saying seven years ago that the law, written at the EU headquarter in Brussels, enables investigation and prosecution of “all alleged war crimes”.

The EU Council of Ministers in June 2019 said that the law of August 2015 of Kosovo parliament, with which the court was formed after pushed to change the Constitution first, enables the court to tackle all crimes, including those committed by the regime of the then President of Serbia, Slobodan Milosevic.

Nearly 13,000 Albanian civilians were massacred by Serb forces, 20,000 girls and women raped, 120,000 houses destroyed and more than 800 000 deported forcibly to Albania and North Macedonia during the two-year war by Serbia forces.

“The existing legal framework enables proper investigation and prosecution of all alleged war crimes,” reads the text of conclusions of the EU Council of 18 June 2019.

But no charges are filed by special court’s prosecution against any members of Serbia forces, despite.

Around 15OO civilians are still missing from the two-year war, of which around 500 Serbs believed to be killed by KLA members in revenge.

https://balkaninsight.com/2026/10/23/pro.heading: Proposed Law to Curb Powers of Hague-Based Court Returned to Kosovo Assembly | Balkan Insight
https://balkaninsight.com/2026/10/23/pro.body:
Supporters of former Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) leader and former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci take part in a march in support of him in Pristina, Kosovo, prior to the verdict, September 12, 2026. EPA/GEORGI LICOVSKI

Kosovo President Justina Shiroka Pula sent the amended Kosovo Specialist Chambers (KSC) bill back to parliament on Thursday for review on the request of the Democratic Party of Kosovo (PDK) which had proposed the bill, less than three weeks after its controversial approval.

The law, which aims to curtail the jurisdiction of the Hague-based court, came after weeks of street protests led by Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) veterans, who rallied under the slogan “Not in my name” – a reference to the KSC judge’s choice of words, “In the name of the people of Kosovo”, when he read the verdict.

“The president received a formal proposal from the parliamentary group of the Democratic Party of Kosovo – the sponsor of the legislation – to allow the assembly to reconsider the law, specifically the provisions concerning the jurisdiction and mandate of the Specialist Chambers,” read a statement from the president’s office on Thursday.

“The president has reiterated her opposition to any attempt to distort the historical truth of Kosovo, to cast doubt on the liberationist nature of the war, or to equate the people who fought for freedom and survival with the regime that oppressed them,” the statement read.

The initial bill was passed after four former KLA leaders were convicted by the KSC for the war crimes of arbitrary detention, cruel treatment, torture and murder, committed between April 1998 and June 1999.

Hashim Thaci and Jakup Krasniqi were sentenced to 25 years in prison each and Kadri Veseli and Rexhep Selimi received 18 and 13 years, respectively, with credit for time served in detention from November 2020. The verdict can be appealed and their lawyers are working to challenge the conviction.

Given the uncertainty over whether the KSC will indict anyone else, the effect of the bill is uncertain, but the message it sent was clear, and the European Union was unhappy.

“The Law […] goes against Kosovo’s international obligations towards the EU,” read a statement from the EU after the law was initially approved. The EU finances most of the court’s operations.

In a speech at the Berlin Process Summit in Montenegro on Thursday, European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos said that “weeks and months of defining moments” lie ahead for the Western Balkans and reminded Kosovo of its obligations under international law.

On Thursday, Perparim Gruda, a MP from PDK who was involved in drafting the recent KSC bill wrote on Facebook that “there is no error in the law amending the Law on the Specialist Chambers.”

The Kosovo Specialist Chambers is a hybrid court, part of Kosovo’s judiciary but located in The Hague and staffed by internationals. The court was established in 2015 under pressure from Kosovo’s Western allies. Hashim Thaci was one of the main Kosovar supporters of the establishment of the court.

Since the conviction of the former KLA leaders over a month ago, criticism of the KSC has continued unabated in Kosovo. On October 14, Kosovo’s Ombudsperson, Naim Qelaj, held an event in Pristina to demand external oversight of the KSC.

Qelaj claimed that the court “has not been subject to democratic monitoring and control by the institutions of the Republic of Kosovo, creating a lack of transparency and accountability towards the citizens and institutions of Kosovo”.

He said it should report to the Kosovo authorities and that the Ombudsperson institution should be able to have access to its work.

KSC spokesperson Angela Griep told BIRN that “according to the legal framework of the Specialist Chambers, the Kosovo Ombudsperson does not have any responsibility with respect to the Specialist Chambers. This responsibility falls exclusively with the Ombudsperson of the Specialist Chambers in accordance with the Kosovo Constitution”.

WASHINGTON ― Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence (MoD) has signed a letter of intent with Finnish firms ICEYE and Nokia to explore development of “sovereign” communications satellites as Kyiv seeks greater control over critical comms infrastructure.

“Modern warfare has proven that reliable communications are a matter of national security. We must all rely on capabilities that we can control. The Letter of Intent between the Ministry of Defense, ICEYE, and Nokia is an important step in this direction,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a statement provided to Breaking Defense today.

“I thank Finland and the Prime Minister of Finland for their consistent support. We value partners who not only help Ukraine, but also work with us to build Europe’s long-term security,” he added.

The agreement was announced Thursday during Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo’s visit to Kyiv. It comes amid uncertainty over Ukraine’s ability to use SpaceX’s Starshield military satellites for drone operations following a US move last week to throttle back the network’s speed — resulting in an ongoing political blame game over responsibility between President Donald Trump and SpaceX founder Elon Musk.

Zelenskyy told ABC News today that, despite assurances from Trump that the slowdown had been reversed, Ukraine’s access speeds remained limited.

ICEYE and Nokia announced their partnership Oct. 1 to “develop secure, sovereign and high-performance broadband low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications systems for governments, supporting missions from defense and border security to emergency services and disaster response,” according to a joint press release.

The companies said government customers would have “ownership and control of the satellites, ground segment and terminals,” with the first satellite planned for liftoff in 2028.

As NATO and European governments accelerate investment in space-based intelligence, decision advantage will depend on how quickly sovereign and commercial capabilities can be fused into a trusted operational picture.

Kyiv’s letter of intent marks the first expression of interest in the joint effort, although it falls short of an actual order.

“The LOI with the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine is an expression of intent and does not imply an ordering of any system for Ukraine,” an ICEYE spokesperson told Breaking Defense.

Under the partnership, ICEYE will provide the satellite platform underpinning the joint effort, with the spokesperson explaining that the firm has developed a “flexible platform now being used in satellite communications.”

Nokia will contribute “secure networking technologies” onboard the spacecraft, according to the joint press release.

“Together, the companies will integrate satellites, ground infrastructure and ruggedized end-user terminals to extend ICEYE’s sovereign intelligence from space business model to satellite communications,” the joint press release said.

Based in Helsinki, Nokia provides telecommunications infrastructure, networking capabilities and technologies related to the “internet-of-things.”

ICEYE, headquartered in Espoo, primarily operates synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging satellites and has been expanding both its sales and satellite production capabilities across Europe. The new partnership with Nokia is the company’s first move into SATCOM capabilities.

ICEYE has also been a vocal supporter of Ukraine during its years-long war with Russia. The company recently faced a security concern in orbit when a highly maneuverable Russian Cosmos bird closely approached one of the company’s spacecraft, raising concerns about potentially dangerous on-orbit maneuvers.

https://www.stripes.com/theaters/europe/.heading: Ukraine says Starlink limits still disrupting military operations | Stars and Stripes
https://www.stripes.com/theaters/europe/.body:
A Ukrainian soldier stands beside an anti-aircraft gun as air defense forces prepare to repel a Russian drone attack in Kyiv on Sept. 19. Ukrainian officials say Starlink restrictions continue to hamper military operations despite President Donald Trump’s claim that SpaceX CEO Elon Musk had restored Ukraine’s access to the service. (Efrem Lukatsky/AP)

By JENNIFER H. SVAN STARS AND STRIPES

Ukrainian defense officials said Starlink, the satellite internet service the country uses for communications in its war against Russia, was still not fully functional a day after President Donald Trump said SpaceX had restored its access.

Speaking to reporters Thursday, Trump declined to confirm a news report that he had called Musk a day before and asked him to lift the restrictions. Musk is the CEO of SpaceX, which owns Starlink.

Despite Trump’s comments, Ukrainian drone units and defense officials say connections with Starshield, a military-grade service using Starlink’s vast network of satellites, continued to fail throughout most of the country when drones flew faster than 100 miles an hour, The Wall Street Journal reported Friday.

Serhii Beskrestnov, a defense technology adviser to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said Friday that forces were “not observing any lifting of restrictions on Starlink.”

“There are isolated instances where a Starlink terminal can operate slightly faster than the limit, but this is likely due to how SpaceX’s algorithm works or specific operating conditions, rather than the lifting of the restriction,” Beskrestnov said in an X post by ArmyInform, the information agency of Ukraine’s military.

The Kyiv Post also reported that as of Friday morning, the military was experiencing satellite connectivity losses at drone speeds of more than 100 miles an hour, citing a source in the country’s defense ministry.

Both Trump and Musk have denied responsibility for deliberately throttling the service. Musk has maintained that the U.S. military controls Starshield and that any limits on speed or usage would be determined by the Pentagon and ultimately the White House.

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth said earlier this week that the Pentagon has not “pulled anything back,” suggesting that the issue may be connected to violations of Starlink’s terms of service.

The slowdown came after both Musk and Trump criticized Ukraine for drone strikes on Russian refineries, which the U.S. president blamed for driving up global energy prices. Trump has lifted some sanctions on Russia in a bid to curb fuel costs.

Starshield’s slowdown began affecting Ukraine’s military on Oct. 14 and “has continued since, despite earlier reports of partial improvement,” Beskrestnov said.

Ukraine’s assertions that SpaceX had restricted its Starlink military receptors date from more than a week ago. A cap of about 100 mph caused terminals to shut down and interceptor drones targeting Russian jet-powered Shahed munitions to crash, Zelenskyy said.

The source of the disruption has raised broader questions on Capitol Hill about Musk’s influence over U.S. policy toward Ukraine.

“We’re putting too many eggs in one company’s basket when it comes to our space assets,” Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., said Thursday, according to Politico.

Cramer received a briefing Thursday from Air Force Secretary Troy Meink about Starshield, the report said.

A member of the Armed Services Committee, Cramer said he was concerned about the power of “one individual and one company over America’s ability to protect the domain of space, which is a war-fighting domain,” Politico reported.

Also on Thursday, Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., said he had launched an inquiry into the sudden restrictions of Starshield services in Ukraine.

The move “raises serious questions about who controls critical capabilities the U.S. government has spent billions of dollars to procure,” he said.

Russia and Ukraine have agreed to engage in another round of U.S.-led peace negotiations, even as both sides continue to exchange military strikes.

Russia launched a major overnight attack Thursday on Ukraine’s energy facilities, knocking out electricity for over 500,000, Ukraine’s energy ministry said.

Ukrainian news outlets reported that flights had been halted at all four airports serving Moscow because of a Ukrainian drone attack. Sheremetyevo Airport was evacuated, according to British newspaper The Telegraph, which cited the airport’s press service.

Jennifer H. Svan reports on the U.S. military from Kaiserslautern, Germany, where she writes about the Air Force, Army and DODEA schools. She’s had previous assignments for Stars and Stripes in Japan, reporting from Yokota and Misawa air bases. Before Stripes, she worked for daily newspapers in Wyoming and Colorado. She’s a graduate of the College of William and Mary in Virginia.

https://arminfo.info/full_news.php?id=10.body:
ArmInfo. Armenia has de facto withdrawn from the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO), Secretary General Taalatbek Masadykov stated in an interview with TASS.

According to him, the CSTO continues to send documents to Armenia, but the Armenian side does not participate in their discussions or decision-making. At the same time, Yerevan does not hinder the organization's work and does not object to decisions made by other states.

"They listen to weekly reports, but do not participate in our main events, exercises, and the like. Therefore, I think Article 25 \[of the CSTO Charter\] is relevant here. In principle, they have already de facto withdrawn," Masadykov noted.

Masadykov stated that the heads of CSTO member states may consider Armenia's membership on November 11 at a meeting of the Collective Security Council in Moscow. According to him, the relevant proposal could be made by the country holding the presidency or another member state of the organization.

He also explained that, according to Article 25 of the CSTO Charter, a country has no voting rights if it fails to pay membership dues and fill quota positions. At the same time, an Armenian representative participates weekly in meetings of the organization's Permanent Council, where various issues and possible solutions are discussed.

As a reminder, Armenia has been boycotting CSTO events since the end of 2022. In February 2024, Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan stated that Armenia had effectively frozen its participation in the CSTO, as the organization had failed to fulfill its obligations to Armenia, which could not go without consequences. And on September 18, 2024, at the Second World Armenian Summit, Pashinyan stated that the CSTO poses threats to Armenia's security, its continued existence, sovereignty, and statehood.

https://civil.ge/archives/755815.heading: Botchorishvili Hosts Central Asian Foreign Ministers in Batumi – Civil Georgia
https://civil.ge/archives/755815.body:
Georgian Dream Foreign Minister Maka Botchorishvili hosted a meeting of counterparts from five Central Asian countries in the coastal city of Batumi, discussing bilateral partnerships and Middle Corridor cooperation amid Tbilisi’s intensifying engagement with the region.

The visiting officials included Turkmenistan’s Foreign Minister Rashid Meredov, Kazakhstan’s Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tleuberdi, Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Zheenbek Kulubaev, Tajikistan’s Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Muhriddin, and Uzbek Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov.

As part of the event, Botchorishvili held a series of bilateral meetings with her counterparts, discussing further deepening “bilateral and multilateral relations” and the importance of “developing the Middle Corridor,” a trade route linking Asia and Europe while bypassing Russia, the Georgian Foreign Ministry reported.

In a briefing following the October 23 meeting, Botchorishvili spoke about “a historical friendship, shared economic interests, a common goal of strengthening the ties between Europe and Asia, and the particular importance of the development of the Middle Corridor.”

“Today’s meeting also showed that Georgia is a very important country for Central Asia to have access to international markets,” she added.

The evening before, on October 22, Georgian Dream Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze also hosted the visiting Foreign Ministers at an official dinner, where he reiterated that “deepening relations with Central Asian countries and further developing cooperation across various sectors is a priority for the Government of Georgia,” according to the official press release.

The Batumi meeting is a continuation of Tbilisi’s increased engagement with Central Asian countries as Tbilisi seeks to promote its role in the Middle Corridor, including through a series of recent high-level visits and signing strategic partnership documents with Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

Georgian Dream government officials, led by Kobakhidze, have traveled in recent months to Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Kazakhstan, while in July two Central Asian leaders, Uzbekistan’s President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Turkmenistan’s President Serdar Berdimuhamedov, visited Georgia.

The increased engagement between Georgia and Central Asian countries also comes amid strained relations between Tbilisi and its traditional Western partners, including the United States and the European Union.

https://www.interpressnews.ge/en/article.heading: Co-rapporteurs of the Congress of Local and Regional Authorities of the Council of Europe: The Constitutional Court of Georgia’s examination of a request by members of the ruling party to ban five major opposition parties is deeply alarming | News agency «Interpressnews»
https://www.interpressnews.ge/en/article.body:
Anders Knape (Sweden, EPP/CCE) and Urs Janett (Switzerland, ILDG), Co-rapporteurs of the Congress of Local and Regional Authorities of the Council of Europe, have released a statement on the situation of democracy in Georgia.

According to them, the Constitutional Court of Georgia’s examination of a request by members of the ruling party to ban five major opposition parties is deeply alarming

“Such a ban could constitute a dangerous escalation and distance Georgia from its commitments under the European Charter of Local Self-Government and its Additional Protocol.

“Democracy at all levels of government cannot exist without political pluralism and effective checks on the concentration of powers. As we have already warned this year, the continued dismantlement of the foundations of Georgian democracy is a matter of grave concern. If the parties were banned, thousands of citizens could be prevented from participating in local democracy because of their political affiliation, as the Venice Commission recently alerted. Pluralism would de facto no longer exist in Georgian municipalities.

“We remain committed to supporting Georgia in fulfilling its obligations as a member State of the Council of Europe in safeguarding democracy, human rights and the rule of law at local level. We will follow the proceedings closely, as well as their implications for local democracy, to ensure that all Georgian citizens have a voice on matters closest to them.”

https://oc-media.org/second-georgian-cit.heading: Second Georgian citizen detained over murder of Russian anti-Putin artist in Poland
https://oc-media.org/second-georgian-cit.body:
Polish authorities have detained a 22-year-old Georgian citizen identified only as Makhmud A suspected of aiding and abetting the murder of Russian satirical artist Robert Kuzovkov, also known by his pen name Semyon Skrepetsky, in June.

Kuzovkov, a 44-year-old Russian citizen, known for satirical drawings criticising Russian President Vladimir Putin, was shot dead in the eastern Polish city of Biała Podlaska on 15 June 2026. Prosecutors have said he was shot five times while walking his dog near his home.

Kuzovkov fled Russia in 2021 over fears of political persecution. Before his death, he reported on social media that he had received death threats from supporters of Chechen Head Ramzan Kadyrov, a close ally of Putin who had also been the subject of Kuzovkov’s satirical cartoons.

Poland’s secret service chief Tomasz Siemoniak announced the second arrest on Thursday, saying the suspect had been placed in three months of pre-trial detention by a court.

‘Officers of ABW have detained the second suspect in the case of the murder of a Russian citizen in Biała Podlaska, which took place in June this year’, Siemoniak wrote on X, referring to Poland’s Internal Security Agency (ABW).

The investigation is being conducted by the agency’s regional office in Lublin jointly with Polish police, under the supervision of the National Prosecutor’s Office.

Siemoniak added that the investigation was ongoing.

Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office said Makhmud A had been detained by the ABW on 19 October in a car park along the A2 motorway.

The ABW said the suspect had arrived in Poland from Georgia on 18 October, accompanied by two other Georgian citizens. The two men are to be expelled from Poland and banned from re-entering the country for 10 years.

Makhmud A is accused of aiding and abetting Kuzovkov’s murder by ‘undertaking a number of actions in the period from 1 to 11 June 2026 that made it easier for Elnur A to commit the murder’. He is also charged with illegal possession of firearms and ammunition.

A spokeswoman for the district court in Lublin told broadcaster TVN that Makhmud A allegedly provided Elnur A with a weapon, transport, and a mobile phone equipped with an application that enabled the monitoring of Kuzovkov’s vehicle.

The court has ordered Makhmud A to remain in pre-trial detention for three months. Prosecutors argued that he could otherwise ‘flee, go into hiding, or unlawfully obstruct proceedings’.

The first suspect, a 36-year-old man identified as Elnur A, was arrested within 72 hours of the killing. The following day, Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office charged him with the murder. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on 18 June that he held a Georgian passport.

Elnur A has not confessed to the crime and has refused to provide explanations during questioning, prosecutors have said. He was placed in three months of pre-trial detention over concerns that he might flee or destroy evidence. He has been held in custody since his arrest.

Polish media have also reported that Elnur A speaks Azerbaijani and had previously lived in Poland.

Two Belarusian citizens were also detained in connection with the case but were subsequently released.

The investigation is ongoing, and the role of the second suspect has not yet been established in court.

https://astanatimes.com/2026/10/kazakh-f.heading: Kazakh Foreign Minister Highlights Middle Corridor Potential at Central Asia-Georgia Meeting in Batumi - The Astana Times
https://astanatimes.com/2026/10/kazakh-f.body:
in International on 23 October 2026

ASTANA – Kazakhstan has called for coordinated efforts to strengthen transport and transit links between Central Asia and the South Caucasus, highlighting the strategic importance of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route, also known as the Middle Corridor, during a meeting of foreign ministers from Central Asian states and Georgia on Oct. 23.

Kazakhstan’s Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi joined his Central Asian counterparts and Georgia’s foreign minister in Tbilisi to discuss regional cooperation and the development of the Middle Corridor. Photo credit: MFA.

Kazakhstan’s Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi took part in the meeting at the invitation of Georgian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Maka Botchorishvili. During the meeting, the participants highlighted the strong potential for cooperation among the six countries, noting their similar or fully aligned approaches to key areas of cooperation and regional issues.

The ministers emphasized their shared interests in maintaining regional stability, achieving sustainable development and expanding cooperation between Central Asia and the South Caucasus. They also underlined the importance of maintaining regular dialogue to develop practical solutions and advance joint initiatives.

Particular attention was paid to developing the Middle Corridor, which connects Asia and Europe. The ministers discussed measures to improve its competitiveness, including modernizing transport infrastructure, digitalizing freight transportation and simplifying transit procedures.

The Kazakh side stressed the importance of coordinated action to unlock the transport and transit potential of Central Asia and the South Caucasus. According to the discussions, reliable and predictable logistics connections could create additional opportunities to increase mutual trade, attract investment and improve access to international markets.

The development of transport infrastructure and more efficient transit procedures remains an important area of regional cooperation, as the participating countries seek to strengthen connections between their economies and international markets.

Regional cooperation and potential development

The meeting provided an opportunity for the six countries to discuss shared priorities and explore ways to deepen cooperation in areas where their interests and approaches align. Participants highlighted the importance of continued dialogue and joint initiatives in supporting regional stability and sustainable development.

During the visit, Tileuberdi and his counterparts explored the potential of Batumi Sea Port in Georgia. The port is a Kazakh asset and one of the key links along the Middle Corridor. The visit offered an opportunity to examine the port’s role in regional transport and transit connections, particularly as the countries seek to improve the efficiency and competitiveness of routes linking Asia and Europe.

BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 23. Tajikistan and the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) discussed prospects for expanding cooperation, the Tajik Foreign Ministry reports.

The discussion took place on October 22, 2026, during a meeting between Deputy Foreign Minister of the Republic of Tajikistan Idibek Kalandar and Acting Deputy Head of Office and Officer-in-Charge of the OSCE Programme Office in Dushanbe, Fejzo Numanaj.

During the meeting, the sides exchanged views on the current state and prospects of Tajikistan's cooperation with the OSCE, and also discussed the implementation of previously reached agreements.

The Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) is the world's largest regional security organization, bringing together 57 participating states from Europe, Central Asia and North America. Its mandate covers politico-military issues, economic and environmental matters, and the human dimension, including human rights, democratization and media freedom.

Furthermore, the OSCE Programme Office in Dushanbe has operated in Tajikistan since 1994, when the organization opened its mission in the country. The office works with the Tajik government on a range of areas, including border management, countering terrorism and extremism, police reform, economic development, environmental protection, gender equality and support for civil society.

The mandate and activities of the office are agreed with the host country and are periodically reviewed by the OSCE Permanent Council in Vienna.

https://www.bta.bg/en/news/bulgaria/1231.heading: BTA :: Rudozem-Xanthi Border Crossing Opens New Prospects for Cooperation between Bulgaria and Greece
https://www.bta.bg/en/news/bulgaria/1231.body:
A Bulgarian-Greek meeting at the new Rudozem-Xanthi border crossing between the two countries on Friday marked the completion of the project to build the road and its associated infrastructure. The event was organized by the Managing Authority of the Greece-Bulgaria INTERREG Cross-border Cooperation Programme.

It brought together representatives of central and local authorities from both sides of the border to discuss plans to improve the Rudozem-Xanthi road link and opportunities to continue joint initiatives and partnership projects. Participants included Maria Nezeriti, Head of the Managing Authority of the Greece-Bulgaria INTERREG 2021-2027 Programme; Smolyan Regional Governor Georgi Pepelanov; Christodoulos Topsidis, Governor of Greece's Region of Eastern Macedonia and Thrace; representatives of Bulgaria's Ministry of Regional Development and Public Works and Road Infrastructure Agency; and the Greek company Egnatia Odos.

Speakers at the meeting said the Rudozem-Xanthi border crossing is an investment in the development of the cross-border region and offers better prospects for cooperation in business, tourism, culture and trade.

Smolyan Regional Governor Georgi Pepelanov raised the need to draw up a joint plan with specific deadlines to allow buses and trucks to use the Plovdiv-Smolyan-Rudozem-Xanthi route. According to Pepelanov, a joint investment package with clearly identified funding sources and measurable results is needed.

"We are marking an important moment for Bulgaria and Greece and for the prospects of people on both sides of the border. The opening of the road is an important step towards bringing the two regions closer together," said Christodoulos Topsidis, Governor of Eastern Macedonia and Thrace. He said the opening of the border crossing is not merely a transport infrastructure project, but a new stage in cross-border cooperation that turns a historic border into a foundation for partnership and shared opportunities.

https://www.bta.bg/en/news/bulgaria/1231.heading: BTA :: PM Radev Says Bulgaria Taking All Possible Measures to Protect Black Sea Shipping
https://www.bta.bg/en/news/bulgaria/1231.body:
Bulgaria is doing everything possible to enhance the security of shipping in the Black Sea, Prime Minister Rumen Radev stated during a meeting with representatives of the National Grain Producer Association (NGPA) in Sofia on Friday, the government press service reported.

The meeting was also attended by the Minister of Agriculture and Food, Plamen Abrovski, and the Minister of Transport and Communications, Georgi Peev.

Discussions covered the possibility of transporting grain exports from Northwestern Bulgaria to the country's Black Sea ports via Bulgarian State Railways (BDZ) trains. Currently, low water levels in the Danube River are hindering navigation, forcing produce to be transported to the ports by truck. This results in additional costs for producers and places a strain on road infrastructure.

Peev assured the agricultural producers that the state railways possess the necessary capacity to transport grain produce to the Black Sea ports. He also briefed the industry representatives on government projects aimed at the large-scale development of the transport sector and the establishment of more efficient transport corridors, particularly along the North-South axis.

Abrovski said that the budget for the coming year includes funding for the digitalization of all dams, which will enable real-time monitoring of their water levels. The NGPA supported the need to maintain funding for Cohesion Policy and the Common Agricultural Policy within the European Union’s next Multiannual Financial Framework for the 2028–2034 period.

Ships bound for Varna and Burgas that serve the Bulgarian economy have not stopped and will not stop, Radev stated to journalists on Tuesday. He dismissed claims that the movement of the merchant fleet in the Black Sea has been halted, stressing that there is currently no such risk to Bulgarian shipping.
