President Nikos Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhurman will next meet on Tuesday, government spokesman Konstantinos Letymbiotis said on Friday, with the meeting set to be the latest in an ongoing series of weekly talks between the pair.

Letymbiotis also said that following the conclusion of the leaders’ meeting, the pair will hold a joint meeting with the bicommunal technical committees on youth and cultural heritage, as well as the civil society steering committee.

The meeting will come with the Greek Cypriot side reporting that progress has been made on the prospect of opening new crossing points between the island’s two sides, with Greek Cypriot chief negotiator Menelaos Menelaou saying that a dispute over the routing of the planned transit road between Athienou and the Nicosia suburb of Aglandjia “has been overcome”.

He said that the outstanding dispute now remains over the question of whether a planned crossing point to connect Louroujina, the southernmost Turkish Cypriot village, with nearby Lymbia, will open at the same time.

The Turkish Cypriot side’s position is that the road between Athienou and Aglandjia constitutes two crossing points, one in Athienou and one in Aglandjia, and that they are part of a package of four alongside plans for a crossing point in the eastern Nicosia suburb of Mia Milia, and one in Louroujina.

However, the Greek Cypriot side treats the road between Athienou and Aglandjia as one crossing point, counterweighted by the Mia Milia crossing point, and is therefore of the view that the Louroujina crossing point should only be opened if a second transit road, through the Turkish Cypriot Kokkina exclave in the Tillyria region, also be opened.

Away from the matter of crossing points, the sides remain locked on the question of the meaning of political equality, with the Turkish Cypriot side insisting that a rotating presidency between the island’s two major communities is an “indispensable component” of political equality which must be agreed upon before negotiations begin.

However, Christodoulides has on this front accused Erhurman of attempting to set “preconditions” on the resumption of negotiations.

“It is clear that the Turkish side … is setting terms and preconditions for the resumption of talks. They are demanding that we accept, in advance, specific positions of interest to the Turkish Cypriot community, while showing absolutely no willingness to discuss or accept our own positions on other significant aspects of the Cyprus problem,” he said.

Erhurman remains resolute on his four-point methodology which he says must be met before negotiations recommence in earnest.

Those four points foresee that the Greek Cypriot side accept political equality, time-limit negotiations and preserve all past agreements, and that the UN guarantee that embargoes placed on the Turkish Cypriots be lifted if the Greek Cypriot side leaves the negotiating table again.

However, more recently, Christodoulides brought 19 new points for discussion to the table, among which was a proposal to open and repopulate the fenced-off area of Varosha under the United Nations’ administration and open the port of Famagusta under the European Union’s control.

Erhurman said he had rejected this because it falls short of the entry into force of the European Union’s direct trade regulation.

The direct trade regulation is a pending EU regulation which would allow Turkish Cypriot goods, as certified by the Turkish Cypriot chamber of commerce, to be exported directly into Europe via the Green Line, and given preferential treatment inside the European single market as European goods.

It was proposed in July 2004, three months after the rejection of the Annan plan by the Greek Cypriot side in a referendum, shortly after the Republic of Cyprus’ accession to the EU.

https://news.err.ee/1610174659/defense-m.body:
The top official at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Jonatan Vseviov, has said he will resign on Thursday to run in next spring's national election for the opposition Social Democratic Party (SDE). He hopes to be the party's prime ministerial candidate.

Vseviov is currently in his second term as the ministry's secretary general and is Estonia's former ambassador to Washington. Previously, he was secretary general at the Ministry of Defense.

Vseviov will submit his resignation on Thursday and will leave his post on November 1.

"I have devoted my entire life so far to protecting and developing Estonia as a diplomat and civil servant. I have had the honor of leading dedicated teams with whom we have shaped Estonia's foreign and defense policy and implemented many of the decisions that have brought us to where we are today," Vseviov said.

"Today, however, I see that protecting Estonia and moving it forward requires more than what I can do as a civil servant. That is why I have decided to leave the civil service, join the Social Democrats and run in the upcoming elections," he said.

SDE Chairman Lauri Läänemets said Estonia's security and its position in the international arena require strong leadership.

"Jonatan Vseviov knows Estonia's security and foreign policy inside out and has extensive international experience. He has shaped Estonia's defense policy, led the Ministry of Defense, represented Estonia as ambassador in Washington and headed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs," Läänemets said.

Vseviov took office as secretary general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in February 2021. Before that, he had served as Estonia's ambassador to the United States since August 2018.

From 2008 to 2018, Vseviov worked at the Ministry of Defense, eventually becoming its secretary general.

Before being appointed secretary general in January 2016, Vseviov served as deputy secretary general for defense planning, acting deputy secretary general for defense policy and director of the policy planning department.

Vseviov graduated from the University of Tartu with a degree in political science and earned a master's degree with honors in security studies from Georgetown University.

From 1999 to 2005, Vseviov was a member of the Reform Party.

Läänemets said the party reached an agreement with Vseviov in the summer. The deal included Vseviov becoming the SDE's candidate for prime minister. At the time, the media was linking the secretary general to a possible presidential bid.

Läänemets said at a press conference on Thursday morning that he will propose at a board meeting on November 1 that Vseviov stand as the party's prime ministerial candidate.

Läänemets told ERR the process began around a year ago, when he started thinking about how the party could achieve the best possible result in the 2027 Riigikogu elections.

Asked whether the agreement also included the position of candidate for prime minister, Läänemets said it did.

"The idea didn't start with me saying, 'Come into politics.' As secretary general, he attended government meetings when I was a minister, and you could see common ground developing from there. Ultimately, it was a process of growing closer on both sides."

Läänemets added that security determines a great deal in Estonia today and that, given Vseviov's experience and knowledge, he would make a very good next prime minister of Estonia.

"We came to the conclusion that we cannot move forward the way [Reform Prime Minister Kristen] Michal is doing things now. Or the way [Isamaa Chairman Urmas] Reinsalu would do them. And I'm not even going to talk about [Center's Mihhail] Kõlvart. Can anyone imagine Kõlvart negotiating with Russia on behalf of Ukraine?" the chairman said.

Vseviov said: "I will now first seek a mandate from the Social Democratic Party — specifically from the Social Democratic Party, because I see in this team the potential to be a responsible and forward-looking force at Estonia's helm. And if the party grants me that mandate, I will seek a mandate from the Estonian people."

Läänemets said he will continue as leader of the party and will also run in the elections.

'We are capable of more and deserve better'

Both men said Estonia must be able to assert itself more on the international stage and participate in various discussions concerning security.

"We must understand that the surest guarantee of our freedom is that it is also valuable to other like-minded countries. Our freedom must be valuable to others, and then others will value our freedom. For our freedom to be valuable to others, we need courage, sharpness of mind, intellectual reach and political reach as well, to bring Estonia back into Europe's political core. In doing so, we must understand that those who remain silent go unnoticed, so we must not remain silent. But those who rant are not listened to, so we must not rant either," Vseviov said.

"I feel that today we are desperately lacking both intellectual reach and the courage to assert ourselves," he added.

Vseviov said Estonia needs radical progress to survive, and that the Reform Party no longer offers this.

"If I believed that Estonia's current political leadership was up to the task, I would continue working as a civil servant and would not be standing here before you today. I am absolutely convinced that with the current leadership, we are incapable of sailing through this storm, and I believe that the team beside me and behind me is the team that today offers Estonia intelligent but also forward-looking policies," he said.

"Some want to tell us that we should be satisfied that the economy is no longer shrinking and that the war has not yet reached Estonia. My message is that we are capable of more and deserve better," he said.

Läänemets was more specific in his criticism of the government, saying that it should have responded immediately to the arson attack on defense industry company Milrem's production facility and made greater efforts to secure a seat at the table in discussions concerning Ukraine's security.

"As for Ukraine and the negotiations or conditions being imposed on Ukraine, the president of Finland and the Norwegian head of state are holding meetings, the Americans are going there, and I ask whether Estonia has even tried to have a say in this at the level of its national leadership, to get involved. Certain things are beyond the reach of civil servants; there are limits to what officials can do. But when such agreements are being made in one place or another and we are not invited, does that mean we should not at least try to have a say? We could start listing examples, both close to home and farther afield, where Kristen Michal simply takes the opportunity to do nothing," Läänemets said.

Vseviov said his decision to enter politics has absolutely nothing to do with the fact that he was nominated as a presidential candidate.

Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said Vseviov's move did not come as a surprise to him.

"For several years, I have encouraged senior civil servants to enter politics. And I am glad that some of them are doing so. Because there is a big difference between developing policies as a civil servant and literally putting your own skin in the game. Taking a mandate and assuming responsibility as a politician. So in that sense, it was not a surprise to me. Jonatan Vseviov informed me yesterday that he would be running in the elections with the Social Democrats," Tsahkna told ERR.

The minister did not want to comment on Vseviov joining the SDE, adding it is up to him to explain his ideological choices.

Tsahkna said he had not forced Vseviov to resign.

"But I didn't try to keep him either. We discussed it, and it was his own suggestion that these things are incompatible if you have decided to enter politics and are moving into the active campaign phase while simultaneously serving as secretary general. Although, yes, there is no legal requirement whatsoever for a person to leave their position. But it was his own wish, and as of November 1, Jonatan Vseviov will no longer be secretary general of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs," he said.

Tsahkna said there are no criteria for the next secretary general to come from within the ministry.

"But clearly, this person must not only understand foreign policy theoretically and be an expert, but also know how foreign and security policy is handled in Estonia and who is involved. It is certainly difficult to separate defense policy from foreign policy, because today they are very closely intertwined. So this person must be capable of working with everyone: the Riigikogu, the president, coordinating our own ministry, the Ministry of Defense, and also think tanks. And communicating with international partners. That is also extremely important," the minister said.

Reform: Vseviov took offense when we didn't make him defense minister

According to Reform Party Secretary-General Kristo Enn Vaga, the Reform Party held extensive talks with Jonatan Vseviov both when it was looking for a presidential candidate and when it needed to find a new defense minister following Hanno Pevkur's resignation.

"When we were looking for a defense minister, we sounded out whether he would be willing to talk to us if we were to give him a call. The response was positive," Vaga told Äripäev.

The Reform Party ultimately chose former Estonian Defense Forces commander Martin Herem, which Vaga said was the right decision for Estonia's defense policy.

"That certainly left him [Jonatan Vseviov] feeling somewhat resentful toward us because we didn't choose him after all. I suppose that may have been the deciding factor in why he went with the Social Democrats," Vaga said.

According to Vaga, the Reform Party also courted Vseviov over the summer when it was still looking for a presidential candidate and Vseviov was one of the leading contenders. This is why Vaga finds Social Democratic Party leader Lauri Läänemets' claim that Vseviov had already decided to join the Social Democrats in the summer questionable.

This story was updated to add comments from Margus Tsahkna, Jonatan Vseviov, Lauri Läänemets and Kristo Enn Vaga.

https://www.novinite.com/articles/241227.body:
French and British fighter jets simulated a nuclear strike over the Mediterranean Sea in the first joint exercise involving France’s airborne nuclear capabilities, Paris announced, as the two allies deepen military cooperation amid tensions with Russia, Reuters reported.

The exercise followed an agreement reached by France and the United Kingdom in July 2025 to strengthen cooperation on their nuclear arsenals in response to growing threats to Europe and uncertainty over their shared ally, the United States.

French Minister of the Armed Forces Catherine Vautrin said the two countries could coordinate their nuclear forces while maintaining their independence.

“Our nuclear cooperation with the UK continues to deepen: on Tuesday evening, British Typhoon fighter jets participated for the first time in a French nuclear exercise alongside Rafale aircraft,” Vautrin added.

According to a statement from the French Ministry of the Armed Forces, French jets took off from Saint-Dizier airbase in northeastern France, accompanied by British Typhoon fighters, and simulated a nuclear strike during the exercise, codenamed “Rummy.”

British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting said the joint mission demonstrated the allies’ commitment to European security.

“In an increasingly dangerous world, our adversaries must be left in no doubt: the UK and France are united in their commitment to European security and to maintaining the deterrence that has helped preserve peace for generations,” Streeting said.

French President Emmanuel Macron announced in March that France would increase its nuclear arsenal. He also launched an initiative enabling European partners to take part in joint exercises and potentially host French nuclear-capable military assets on their territory for short periods.

France spends approximately 5.6 billion euros annually maintaining its stockpile of around 290 nuclear warheads, which can be deployed from submarines and aircraft. According to Reuters, France has the world’s fourth-largest nuclear arsenal.

The United Kingdom possesses 225 nuclear warheads, while Russia and the United States each have more than 5,000.

https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/23/fran.heading: France bolsters security as businesses fear renewed unrest during Saturday protests | Euronews
https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/23/fran.body:
Some 70,000 law enforcement officers are set be deployed across France on Saturday, while the Louvre and several other major Paris museums will be closed as authorities seek to prevent renewed violence during protests.

Last weekend, peaceful demonstrations were overshadowed by violence and unrest which erupted across the country. Masked individuals looted shops and intimidated their owners, stormed public buildings, smashed shop windows, and clashed with police forces.

Demonstrators plan to take to the streets on Saturday to denounce the cost of living crisis, while students are still protesting against what they view as inadequate school conditions. Students, members of the CGT labor union and activists from the “ yellow vest ” movement are set to join.

While some protests have been banned for security reasons in several cities, including Lyon, Nice and Montpellier, marches are expected in many other places including in Paris and Marseille. Authorities have also diverted some protest routes away from shopping streets and public buildings to limit damage.

French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said some 70,000 police officers and gendarmes would be deployed, along with helicopters, armoured vehicles and water cannons. In addition, elite police units will help secure public buildings like city halls in a “highly mobile” security operation, he said.

“There have been numerous calls from radical far-left groups on social media to commit acts of violence and vandalism. There have also been renewed calls for looting, with those messages clearly being spread by rioters," Nuñez said at a news conference.

“We will be absolutely uncompromising" with those involved in violence, he added, warning that police will have a “very firm approach to making arrests, and there will be legal consequences.”

Landmark Paris sites including the Louvre, the Musée d'Orsay, the Picasso museum, along with the Grand Palais will close their doors on Saturday.

Art Basel, one of the world's most prestigious contemporary art fairs, opened to the public Friday — but only for the day, with the threat of unrest prompting organisers to cancel the weekend program.

"This decision has not been taken lightly, and the safety of everyone involved in the fair remains our utmost priority," organisers said in a statement Thursday.

The manager of a supermarket in central Paris, which was looted last weekend told Euronews on condition of anonymity that his entire team remained on edge ahead of Saturday's protests, despite bolstered security measures.

He said that his shop would remain open during the morning and that he would "assess the situation" later in the day.

"We have a metal shutter and we've added some plywood, but we know that these metal shutters took about a minute and a half for protestors to break through. The same goes for our electronic door. So, unless we implement security like banks have, there's really no way to stop them. Last weekend they arrived in huge groups, used bricks, it was incredibly violent."

When teenagers ransacked his supermarket last Saturday, overwhelmed police forces were unable to intervene. The next day, when the looting resumed, law enforcement made it to the scene, pushing back gangs of violent teenagers.

Many of the staff remain traumatised, "we've worked so hard to ensure we managed to clean and restock. But, frankly, I haven't had a proper rest in about 13 days. Everyone on our team

"Frankly, I haven't had a proper rest in about 13 days. We're all under a lot of pressure. Everyone on our team is feeling it. There's a palpable tension, and we're trying to manage it, but to keep everyone calm and prevent any major incidents from occurring. Unfortunately, there's a risk that something bad will happen, and we need to prevent that from happening."

A demonstration in the city of Orléans, located south of Paris, will also take place on Saturday.

About 50 organisations have called for a protest against the far right on the sidelines of the two-day congress of Marine Le Pen’s nationalist, anti-immigration party ahead of next spring’s presidential election. Organisers include labor unions, left-wing political parties, student organisations and anti-racism groups.

Hugues Moutouh, the prefect of the Loiret region, said that 20,000 to 30,000 demonstrators from across the country were expected.

Le Pen, whom opinion polls place as the front-runner in next year’s election, accused left-wing organisations and political parties of trying to “disrupt a political party’s democratic congress,” on public news broadcaster FranceInfo.

Still, she said she had “no concerns” about security because the government had “recognised the need for measures allowing the congress to proceed safely.”

https://www.internazionale.it/ultime-not.heading: France investigates suspected Islamophobic shooting of girl near Paris as terrorism - Internazionale
https://www.internazionale.it/ultime-not.body:
PARIS, Oct 23 (Reuters) - A gunman who officials suspect may have been motivated by Islamophobic hatred opened fire from a car west of Paris on Friday, killing one person and wounding four others, including a 12-year-old girl.

“The investigations are ongoing, but it is clearly a terrorist crime. It is an extremely serious act,” Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told reporters from the Yvelines district west of Paris where the attack took place.

Officials said the 39-year-old suspect, who has not been named, drove through the town of Trappes, where he fired an automatic weapon at a petrol station, a medical centre and a children’s playground.

Broadcaster BFM said the wounded girl had been hit eight times and was in a serious condition.

“(It was) objectively a racist attack, probably Islamophobic,” said Ali Rabeh, the mayor of Trappes, whose parents came from Morocco. “The people targeted today could just as easily have been my mother, my brothers or my sisters-in-law.”

Police managed to arrest the man before he could injure anyone else. Video images showed his car riddled with bullets.

The shooting comes at a moment of particular tension in France, after nationwide protests turned violent last Saturday and before further demonstrations this coming weekend.

Some far-right politicians have blamed immigration for the wave of looting and vandalism that battered a number of French cities on October 17.

Rabeh, who is a left-wing politician, called for a collective condemnation of rhetoric that “ideologically arms those capable of carrying out such acts”.

The anti-terrorism prosecutor’s office, known as PNAT, said its investigation included looking at whether the shooting was racially or religiously motivated.

PNAT can take over any criminal investigation it believes meets the criteria for terrorism, including violence inspired by far-right ideas. Terrorism sentences are tougher, and counter-terrorism forces have greater investigative powers.

Nicolas Dainville, the mayor of nearby La Verriere, said the suspect lived in the town of Plaisir, which is also in Yvelines, and was “of a European type”. Rabeh said two of the victims were of African and North African origin, respectively, and did not provide details about the backgrounds of the other victims.

(Reporting by Juliette Jabkhiro, Dominique Vidalon, Zhifan Liu and Sudip Kar-Gupta; Writing by Crispian Balmer, Editing by Makini Brice and Peter Graff)

https://www.dpa-international.com/politi.body:
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has urged Israel to comply with international law in light of its announced sealing off of the West Bank.

"Of course, Israel's security against Hamas terror is of crucial importance," the conservative politician said on Friday in Istanbul.

"At the same time, we have been following the escalation in the West Bank in recent months with deep concern," said Wadephul. Israel was obliged under international law to uphold and protect the rights of Palestinians, he said. "These obligations must be consistently fulfilled."

After an attack in the West Bank that killed two soldiers shortly before Israel's parliamentary election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has held out the prospect of sealing off the Palestinian territory. This means all crossings into the Palestinian territory would be closed.

The announcement came after an attack with firearms near Hebron in the West Bank. According to military data, two soldiers were killed and three others injured. The two Palestinian attackers from Hebron were killed, it said.

Wadephul condemned "this terrible attack." His thoughts were with those affected and their relatives. "The terrorists must not succeed in stirring up further hatred through their actions and further escalating the situation as a whole," he said.

https://www.tovima.com/politics/kikilias.heading: Kikilias Says Greece Will Not Yield on Sovereign Rights - tovima.com
https://www.tovima.com/politics/kikilias.body:
Athens is seeking to counter opposition claims of a “national defeat” over the Turkey-Libya agreement by emphasizing international law and accelerating talks with Egypt on expanding their maritime boundaries

Minister of Maritime Affairs and Insular Policy Vassilis Kikilias has said Greece will not compromise on its sovereign rights amid renewed tensions over the 2019 maritime agreement between Turkey and Libya, describing foreign policy as an ongoing struggle that cannot be won or lost in a single day.

Speaking to Greek broadcaster SKAI, Kikilias also discussed government plans to support ferry services as fuel costs rise, ways to increase the economic benefits of Greece’s shipping industry and recent allegations of misconduct in Greek basketball.

Kikilias said he had submitted a proposal to the prime minister’s office and the Finance Ministry to help the ferry industry manage rising fuel costs and keep ticket prices stable.

He emphasized the importance of maintaining connections between Greece’s islands, particularly during the winter, when ferries carry fewer passengers but remain essential for residents and the transportation of goods.

“I am glad that, based on my proposal, you have heard the prime minister’s statements,” Kikilias said, adding that institutional meetings with representatives of the industry were expected in the coming period to determine how support would be provided.

He said several policy tools were available despite the country’s difficult fiscal circumstances and urged European institutions to give member states room to help their citizens.

“We will not depart from our fiscal commitments to Europe and those who make the decisions, I agree. But there must also be an understanding of the crisis we are facing,” he said.

Kikilias noted that ferry ticket prices did not rise in 2025, despite the industry announcing planned increases of around 15%. Prices also remained stable in 2026 amid the war in the Middle East, following €60 million in support approved by the government’s economic team and the prime minister after his proposal.

He said the government would do everything possible to support ferry services serving smaller islands and routes that are not commercially viable without public assistance.

Kikilias also highlighted opportunities to translate Greece’s strength in global shipping into broader economic benefits for domestic businesses.

Referring to his recent trip to Japan and China, where he met government officials and shipping industry representatives, he said Greece’s position as the world’s largest shipping power gave it significant weight in Asian markets.

He noted that Greek-owned vessels account for 68% of shipbuilding activity in China, citing the figure as an example of the sector’s scale.

During his meetings, Kikilias said he asked for Greek marine equipment manufacturers to receive preference when equipment is purchased for ships being built in those countries. He also called for closer ties that would allow Greece’s shipping strength to generate greater returns across the domestic economy.

He described the Shipping and Island Policy Ministry as an economic development ministry, with responsibilities extending beyond ferry connections, migration and maritime border enforcement.

He also pointed to port infrastructure and the development of Greek ports as opportunities to strengthen tourism, yachting and the cruise industry, bringing benefits to local communities.

Turning to the Turkey-Libya maritime memorandum, Kikilias said the agreement was not a new development, noting that it was signed in November 2019 by the government in western Libya.

He described the agreement as unlawful and said its recent ratification by Libya’s House of Representatives reflected the influence Turkey had built in the country. He also referred to the removal of the parliament’s speaker.

Kikilias said the latest development was unwelcome but should not be treated as decisive for Greece’s foreign policy.

“I do not believe that anyone loses in foreign policy in a single day or wins in a single day. It is a constant struggle and a major effort,” he said.

He called for serious policymaking, a clear and professional approach, and for those with the necessary expertise to lead discussions. He added that people who are not involved in negotiations do not have the full picture.

“As a member of this government, I have said many times, regarding Turkey, that when it comes to our sovereign rights, we will not take even one step back,” he said.

Kikilias, a former international basketball player, also described recent revelations about Greek basketball as “a disgrace” and called for the investigation to proceed without prejudging anyone’s guilt.

He said the authorities should establish the facts methodically and determine who, if anyone, was involved, stressing the importance of the presumption of innocence.

Kikilias said allegations of misconduct risk undermining children’s confidence in sports and the fairness of competition. Children should be able to win or lose a game and leave with their heads held high, he said, trusting that the rules are applied fairly.

He described the issue as a serious structural problem in a field that should promote healthy values. He praised the sports judge and those who conducted the investigation, calling for it to continue to its conclusion.

Kikilias also warned against a growing perception that everyone in public life or institutions is equally implicated in wrongdoing.

“I do not agree with that, and I do not accept it. I want to say that everyone is equal, yes, but not everyone is the same,” he said.

He called for allegations involving organizations, political parties or public bodies to be investigated by the judiciary, rather than through public condemnation.

“Not public uproar and people’s courts. Justice,” he said.

Greece has formally restated its objections to the 2019 maritime agreement between Turkey and Libya in a letter sent to the United Nations following its recent approval by Libya’s House of Representatives.

The letter was sent on Thursday, October 22, by Greece’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Aglaia Balta, to Secretary-General António Guterres, acting on instructions from Greek Foreign Minister George Gerapetritis, according to diplomatic sources.

The correspondence addresses the recent decision by Libya’s House of Representatives to approve the 2019 Turkey-Libya memorandum, which Athens considers illegal.

In the letter, Greece reiterates its longstanding position that the agreement is invalid and without legal standing. It argues that the memorandum contradicts international law, particularly the law of the sea, and cannot produce legal effects for third countries.

https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/23/ital.heading: Italy preparing with elite troops and drone surveillance for 24 October protests | Euronews
https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/23/ital.body:
Nationwide protests against the rising cost of living are expected in Italy and France on Saturday 24 October. Authorities and business owners fear a repeat of what happened on 17 and 18 October, when hundreds of people were involved in violent incidents targeting shops and law enforcement.

Protests are planned in several Italian cities, including Milan, Bologna, Genoa, Turin, Rome and Florence. According to "Mappa della rivolta", a website that collates protest initiatives, more than 30 mobilisations are scheduled, ranging from marches and sit-ins to assemblies and strikes.

The capital will be under tight security for the occasion. Rome's police headquarters has drawn up a security plan to manage both notified demonstrations and spontaneous rallies announced online. In addition to the usual units deployed to handle protests, drones from the State Police's 1st Flight Department and aircraft from the Carabinieri will also be used. In all, around 1,500 officers will be deployed, with checks stretching from city squares to railway stations.

Rome's Cybersecurity Centre is also operational, monitoring posts and activities on social media in coordination with Digos, the specialized operational division of the Italian State Police.

The digital dimension is making it harder to manage the protests. On Telegram, TikTok and Instagram, guides on how to prepare for clashes are circulating. Advice ranges from bringing water, painkillers and vinegar to lessen the effects of tear gas, to guidance on what to wear and how to behave if disorder breaks out.

In Milan, there will be around one thousand police officers and Carabinieri, 300 municipal officers and 500 soldiers deployed following the latest government security decree. Here too, drones will be used to monitor the marches. Authorised demonstrations will take place away from the Duomo, while protests are banned in the Garibaldi and Porta Venezia districts.

In Turin, a demonstration is expected that has been organised by activists from the antagonista scene linked to the former Askatasuna social centre, together with members of the 17 October Movement and students. Marches are due to start at 2 p.m. in Piazza Arbarello.

Following the unrest on 17 October, on Friday Digos carried out searches targeting around 100 people, 51 of whom were minors. Operations took place in several cities, including Bari, Bergamo, Florence, Genoa and Verona.

https://www.defensenews.com/global/europ.heading: Leonardo, Rheinmetall secure $4 billion contracts with Italian Army, report says - Defense News
https://www.defensenews.com/global/europ.body:
Italy’s Leonardo and Germany’s Rheinmetall have secured, through their joint venture, two contracts with the Italian Army worth $4.16 billion in total for armored vehicles, Italy’s MF newspaper reported on Thursday.

The orders are for the supply of the A2CS combat vehicles and the new-generation MBT tanks and are part of Italy’s wider military modernization program, the Italian financial daily added.

Leonardo CEO Lorenzo Mariani said he could not confirm whether the contract had been signed “as any communication on the matter must be coordinated with our clients.”

Leonardo and Rheinmetall launched their 50-50 joint venture in 2024.

“The programme is ready to enter production from our side. We are actively working on both the tank programme and the Future Combat System (FCS), and are progressing on both in close cooperation with Rheinmetall,” Mariani said in Rome.

Speaking on the sidelines of the annual meeting of the state-backed Fondo Italiano d’Investimento, he stressed the importance of tanks for the modernization of Italy’s defense, for exports and for the broader partnership with Rheinmetall.

https://www.lrt.lt/en/news-in-english/19.heading: Lithuanian FinMin defends deficit budget: there was pressure to cut defence spending - LRT
https://www.lrt.lt/en/news-in-english/19.body:
There was considerable pressure, including from coalition partners, to sharply reduce defence spending while preparing next year’s government spending bill, Finance Minister Taurimas Valys said, defending the 2026 budget proposal that includes a sizable deficit.

“There were many temptations, including from some coalition partners, to make drastic cuts. Or to resort to certain tricks that might have been ill-considered and not coordinated with our defence partners,” Valys told LRT.lt in an interview.

“There were many proposals to look at other NATO countries and tie ourselves to the minimum required by our main partners, the Americans. But we stood firm. We created expectations among our partners and, by setting an example, are already seeing certain dividends,” he said.

Valys added that the government had also faced considerable pressure from the opposition.

According to the minister, Lithuania’s decision to allocate more than 5% of its GDP to defence is already paying off.

“We are no longer treated as a war zone. We are seen as resilient and determined, investing in defence and capable of attracting the attention of the world’s biggest market players,” he said.

Lithuania has committed to maintaining defence spending at a level in excess of 5% of GDP.

Valys also said that next year’s pension increases could potentially be financed using the surplus in the State Social Insurance Fund’s (Sodra) reserve, rather than drawing on the reserve itself.

“That question remains open,” he said.

https://www.dutchnews.nl/2026/10/cyber-s.heading: Cyber security centre warns PHP hacking situation could worsen - DutchNews.nl
https://www.dutchnews.nl/2026/10/cyber-s.body:
The Netherlands’ National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) is investigating the first signs of successful hacks on websites following the exposure of critical vulnerabilities on the web, and says the situation could “rapidly worsen”.

A spokesperson told the Volkskrant on Thursday that the signals came from the NCSC’s international network, and that there was no sign yet of abuse involving Dutch websites. The centre is still checking whether the reports are accurate.

Cybersecurity researchers, working with the help of AI, found that PHP, the programming language on which a majority of the web is built, had at least two serious vulnerabilities in its code.

Details of the weaknesses were leaked online on Monday, and the PHP developers announced they would issue an upgrade by Wednesday afternoon.

Hacking attempts began even before the leak, with Amazon reporting an attack attempt on October 17. US internet security firm Cloudflare said it saw hacking attempts run from thousands before the upgrade to millions afterwards.

Initially, the NCSC said that there were no signs of active hacks and the PHP developers said there were no indications of breaches.

Large amounts of government, healthcare and news sites were forced to go dark temporarily while awaiting the upgrade, including Dutch News.

The Netherlands was fast to act, closing a large amount of its sites and issuing warnings early on Wednesday, after which governments in Belgium, Germany, France and Finland did the same. The issue is now a global concern.

Dutch privacy watchdog AP said on Thursday it had not yet received any reports of data breaches linked to the vulnerabilities.

https://nltimes.nl/2026/10/23/dutch-emba.heading: Dutch embassy in Cairo closes after days of protests against the Netherlands | NL Times
https://nltimes.nl/2026/10/23/dutch-emba.body:
The Dutch embassy in the Egyptian capital of Cairo is closed to the public until further notice. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs made this decision following nine days of demonstrations against the Netherlands at the embassy, the embassy said on Facebook.

The protesters are demonstrating against the Dutch police arresting Ahmed Nasser, the deputy head of the Union of Egyptian Youth Abroad and a spokesperson for the government, NOS reports. He was arrested on October 10, reportedly for threatening an activist in the Netherlands, and his pre-trial detention has since been extended.

The Egyptian government typically does not tolerate protests, so the ones at the embassy are likely not spontaneous. According to NOS, protesters are dropped off daily by bus. At each protest, the embassy had to be evacuated for security reasons.

According to NOS, Nasser was arrested for threatening activist Anas Habib, who gained notoriety this summer when he used a padlock to lock the gate of the Egyptian embassy in The Hague. Habib filmed the act, saying it was a protest against Egypt keeping the Rafah border crossing with Gaza closed to Palestinians trying to flee Israeli attacks. His protest triggered a chain reaction, and activists locked the gates of Egyptian embassies in several other countries.

A short time later, a video leaked showing the Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs addressing the ambassador in the Netherlands. “I’ve said a hundred times, whoever touches the [embassies] should be held accountable,” the Minister says. He goes on to say that if anyone is caught touching the embassy’s fence, “drag him inside” and “give him hell.”

It is unclear when the Dutch embassy in Egypt will reopen. It remains accessible for consular assistance in case of emergencies.

Katarzyna Pełczyńska-Nałęcz, the leader of a junior party in Poland’s ruling coalition, has announced that her resignation from the government and the leadership of her party, the centrist Poland 2050 (Polska 2050), in protest over a parliamentary vote on Thursday.

Poland 2050 (Polska 2050) is set to remain in the government, thereby maintaining Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s parliamentary majority. However, the dispute has highlighted tensions within the ruling coalition just a year ahead of parliamentary elections at which it will seek another term.

Dwukadencyjność samorządów została utrzymana. Tak zdecydował dziś Sejm. Wygraliśmy! Zmiana, której chce 75% Polaków dojdzie do skutku!

Stało się to jednak pomimo głosów K15X. Koalicja, w tym niestety znaczna część posłów Polski 2050, stanęła przeciw ludziom, a za politykierskimi Show more

Pełczyńska-Nałęcz, who serves as minister for funds and regional policy, made her decision in the wake of an unusual voting result in the Sejm, the more powerful lower house of parliament, on Thursday.

Another junior partner in the ruling coalition, the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), had proposed a bill abolishing two-term limits for mayors. Those limits had been introduced in 2018 with the aim of reducing corruption and cronyism by preventing local officials from becoming entrenched in power.

However, PSL, which has a strong presence in local politics, argues that the limits prevent effective, popular mayors from being re-elected, thereby denying voters the right to decide who they want to represent them.

Although the government has a majority in the Sejm, the bill was narrowly defeated, with 213 votes in favour and 215 against, after 15 MPs from the ruling coalition joined with the right-wing opposition in voting against it.

How MPs from each parliamentary group voted on the bill ( za = for, przeciw = against, wstrzymało się = abstained, nie głosowało = did not vote)

Pełczyńska-Nałęcz herself is not a member of parliament, so did not vote. Her party was split, with six MPs voting for the bill, three against, three abstaining, and three not voting at all.

Aftewards, Pełczyńska-Nałęcz made clear that she opposed the bill and celebrated the fact that it was blocked. She also announced her resignation from the government and the leadership of her party.

“The coalition, unfortunately including a significant portion of MPs from Poland 2050, stood against the people and in favour of backroom political deals,” she wrote. “I am leaving Donald Tusk’s government because values are more important to me than positions.”

“I am leaving the party in the hands of its founder, who stepped away but then returned,” she added, referring to Poland 2050’s founder, Szymon Hołownia. “I hope that he remembers what values he came to power in the name of.”

Pełczyńska-Nałęcz’s decision follows a year of turmoil for Poland 2050. In September 2025, Hołownia, who had led the party since founding it in 2021, announced that he was stepping down.

However, a first attempt to choose a new leader was invalidated in January after technical problems with voting. Hołownia then hinted that he may reverse course and seek to continue leading the party, though in the end that did not happen.

In February, Pełczyńska-Nałęcz was chosen as the new leader. That prompted her rival candidate, Paulina Hennig-Kloska, to quit the party, taking half of its MPs with her. They formed a new group called Centrum (Centre).

Both Poland 2050 and Centrum remain in the ruling coalition. However, Pełczyńska-Nałęcz has had an uneasy relationship with Tusk.

Around half the MPs from Poland 2050, a junior member of Poland’s ruling coalition, have split from the party and formed a new parliamentary caucus.

They expressed dissatisfaction with the actions of the party's recently elected new leader, @Kpelczynska https://notesfrompoland.com/2026/02/18/polish-junior-ruling-party-splits-amid-fallout-from-leadership-election/…

Polish junior ruling party splits amid fallout from leadership election\\

On Friday, Tusk, who is on a state visit to India, sarcastically responded to Pełczyńska-Nałęcz’s resignation by saying, “I thought she’d at least call before she left”. He admitted that “cooperation \[with her\] has not been the easiest for a long time”.

The prime minister, however, added that he “does not think \[her resignation\] will have any impact on the future work of the coalition…My intuition tells me that this is her individual decision”.

Hołownia, who currently serves as head of Poland 2050’s parliamentary caucus, confirmed at a press conference on Friday alongside fellow MPs that the party intends to remain in Tusk’s coalition. But he also warned that, without Poland 2050, the government would not have a parliamentary majority.

W @PL\2050 dowiedzieliśmy się o decyzji @Kpelczynska z mediów.

The episode highlights the tensions within the ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right and contains parties that disagree on a number of issues.

It also points to the pressure smaller coalition partners are feeling ahead of next autumn’s parliamentary elections. Only parties that win at least 5% of the vote nationally can enter parliament. But Poland 2050 has been polling at around 1% and PSL is on 3%.

In the 2023 election, Poland 2050 and PSL in fact stood together as an alliance called the Third Way (Trzecia Droga), helping ensure that the two parties won enough votes to enter parliament. However, in 2025, they split from one another and confirmed that they would not stand together again.

PSL and Poland 2050, the two parties that make up the Third Way alliance, have confirmed that they are splitting and will stand separately at the next elections.

They will, however, remain part of @donaldtusk's ruling coalition https://notesfrompoland.com/2025/06/18/polands-third-way-alliance-confirms-split-but-remains-within-tusks-ruling-coalition/…

Poland's Third Way alliance confirms split but remains within Tusk's ruling coalition\\

The fact that the bill to end two-term limits for mayors was defeated has also caused tension between PSL and its coalition partners.

In the wake of yesterday’s vote, PSL immediately announced that it would push for the introduction of two-term limits for members of parliament, arguing that the same rules should apply to national and local elected representatives.

The right-wing opposition has long hoped that it could tempt PSL, the most conservative element of Tusk’s coalition, to quit the government. A recent report even claimed that US President Donald Trump had, at the behest of Poland’s opposition, suggested to PSL’s leader that he leave Tusk.

https://www.romania-insider.com/society/.heading: EU, Romania step up Black Sea security response
https://www.romania-insider.com/society/.body:
The European Parliament and Romania’s Supreme Council for National Defense (CSAT) called for stronger measures to address escalating security threats in the Black Sea following attacks on civilian vessels and repeated airspace violations. Both mentioned the need for closer cooperation with NATO allies, improved drone detection, and faster implementation of the EU’s planned regional maritime security hub.

The European Parliament announced that it adopted its resolution on Thursday, October 22, with 432 votes in favor, 52 against, and 88 abstentions. MEPs condemned the latest deadly strikes off the Romanian and Bulgarian coasts and held Russia responsible for escalating its war against Ukraine into the western Black Sea.

The attacks were described as part of a “clear pattern of Russian escalation” involving the systematic targeting of civilian shipping.

Moreover, the MEPs called on the EU and its member states to consider deploying a naval operation in the Black Sea.

The resolution also urged NATO to consider a Black Sea initiative based on discussions about a possible “Black Sea Sentry” and called for closer cooperation among Romania, Bulgaria, and Türkiye.

EU countries, working with NATO, should provide further assistance to Romania and Bulgaria for the early detection and tracking of hostile drones, MEPs said. They also proposed using unspent funds from the SAFE defense instrument to help the two countries address regional threats.

Separately, Romania’s CSAT met at Cotroceni Palace under president Nicușor Dan on Thursday to assess the same escalation and the measures already taken. The council described recent attacks and airspace violations as “direct consequences of the Russian Federation’s aggression beyond Ukraine’s borders.”

CSAT said the situation posed immediate risks to human life, access to Romanian ports, and energy infrastructure in the country’s exclusive economic zone.

Thus, the Council decided that Romania’s priorities will include accelerating the development of maritime surveillance, mine countermeasure capabilities, and systems able to respond to drones entering national airspace or territorial waters. Authorities will also conduct regular exercises and update intervention plans for incidents affecting shipping, economic assets, and the marine environment.

Plus, the Council also discussed the rapid operationalization of the EU’s Black Sea security hub. It also considered greater use of the regional mine countermeasures task force, whose role was expanded in 2026 to include protecting critical infrastructure.

Several commercial vessels have recently been struck by drones in the Black Sea, including within Romanian territorial waters. NATO announced on October 20 that it would send “additional resources” to the region following attacks in Romanian and Bulgarian waters.

On October 17, Romanian F-16 fighter jets shot down two Geran-family attack drones shortly after they entered the country’s airspace over its territorial waters.

https://www.politico.eu/article/drone-hi.heading: Drone hits another ship in Black Sea near Romania, killing at least 1 sailor  – POLITICO
https://www.politico.eu/article/drone-hi.body:
A drone has hit a commercial ship off the coast of Romania, killing at least one crew member with three more still missing, Romanian President Nicușor Dan said Friday.

“This morning we experienced a security incident: A vessel was struck by a drone approximately 13 nautical miles from the coast, just beyond Romania’s territorial waters,” Dan said, praising the coast guard for saving nine sailors as part of the rescue operation. “Unfortunately, one sailor has died and three others are still being searched for,” he added.

The Khoryv ship, flying under the flag of Comoros, suffered significant damage, capsized and partially sank, according to Romania’s Interior Ministry.

The incident is the latest in a string of drone attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea. Dan told POLITICO last week that Russia’s intention was clearly to weaken Romania’s support for Ukraine in the war but vowed not to back down.

NATO allies met Tuesday to discuss the threat to Black Sea shipping and Dan said Romania would receive “additional capabilities” to help defend the area.

“Evidently, this is an incident within the broader process of escalation that Russia is pursuing in the context of its war in Ukraine,” the Romanian president said.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said she was “deeply alarmed” by “yet another Russian escalation in the Black Sea.” The ship was carrying Ukrainian and Azerbaijani crew, she said.

“These reckless attacks target innocent lives and openly defy international law. My thoughts are with the family and loved ones of the sailor that was killed. And with the families of the three crew members still missing.”

Over the last month, drones have hit several cargo ships and chemical tankers close to Romania and Bulgaria — both NATO members — killing more than 20 people in total.

Reuters reported that the ships hit by drones in recent weeks had been near or heading towards the Sulina Canal, linking the Danube River and the Black Sea. This has become a key export route for Ukrainian grain and food oil after Russia attacked Ukraine’s own Black Sea ports.

https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/23/jiha.heading: Jihadists reportedly urge attacks during protests in Portugal and Spain | Euronews
https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/23/jiha.body:
Spanish authorities have reportedly detected calls from jihadist groups to attack police officers and demonstrators during protests taking place in several European countries, including Portugal.

Portugal's Internal Security System (SSI) says it is "closely monitoring" the alert: "The Secretary-General of the Internal Security System is closely monitoring the situation referred to [jihadist calls for attacks on police officers and demonstrators] within her remit and in constant liaison with the relevant authorities," the SSI said in a response to the main Portuguese news agency Lusa.

According El País, the Spanish Interior Ministry reportedly identified messages on a website allegedly linked to the Islamic State (IS) group, urging attacks on police officers and demonstrators during protests that have been going on for several weeks in European countries including Portugal, Spain, France and Italy.

The demonstrations peaked last weekend amid a wave of violence in France, where buildings such as Limoges City Hall and the Lyon tourism office were set on fire and largely destroyed. Italy also saw violent incidents, including arson attacks, particularly in Milan.

In Portugal and Spain, the daily protests and "camp-outs" in the squares of some of the largest cities, notably Lisbon, Porto and Madrid, have been largely driven by the cost of living and the housing crisis.

The Spanish daily says it has seen an internal document from the Cybersecurity Coordination Office containing messages encouraging militants to take advantage of mass demonstrations and street clashes to carry out attacks.

According to El País, the way the protests are organised, with those in France alone estimated to have brought together more than 800,000 people last weekend, offers "a rare opportunity to attack them" and means that the police "become easy prey when there are skirmishes with demonstrators".

The jihadists are also said to have provided practical advice on how to carry out the attacks, calling for "martyrdom" through suicide bombings or vehicle-ramming attacks.

https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/workplace/s.heading: Swiss government accepts it could have handled F-35 procurement better - SWI swissinfo.ch
https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/workplace/s.body:
+Get the most important news from Switzerland in your inbox

In its statement published on Friday, the government announced measures in response to criticism of the F-35 procurement. In future, defence procurement is to be conducted more transparently, risk management is to be improved, and the legal department of the Federal Office for Defence Procurement (Armasuisse) is to be strengthened.

At the same time, the Federal Council has rejected allegations that the contracts were barely scrutinised. It regrets the impression that only the then project manager had read the contracts in full. In addition to the former head of armaments, other Armasuisse experts had studied the texts in their entirety, whilst the defence ministry and former Defence Minister Viola Amherd, had examined the pricing clauses in depth.

Pakistan is mediating between Iran and the United States even as it sends troops to defend Saudi Arabia against attacks by Tehran’s allies, placing Islamabad in the conflicting roles of peace broker and military partner to Iran’s rivals.

On Tuesday, Pakistan's military chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and security chief Mohsen Rezaei in Tehran.

Munir has also cultivated a close relationship with President Donald Trump, including meetings at the White House.

Islamabad helped broker the June agreement between Washington and Tehran. The truce did not last, but Pakistan has kept its mediation channel open.

Pakistan has taken a direct military role in Saudi Arabia's defense.

Reuters reported in May that Islamabad had deployed approximately 8,000 troops, a squadron of fighter jets and air-defense systems to the kingdom under a bilateral agreement. Saudi Arabia financed the deployment, according to Pakistani officials cited by Reuters.

Pakistan’s commitment to Saudi security deepened in August when Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement, treating an attack against one member as an attack against all.

This week, Islamabad announced that Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had completed ratification, while Turkey's remained pending. The partners have also discussed further military mobilization following attacks by Iran-aligned Houthis on Saudi territory.

On Wednesday, Pakistan signed another defense agreement, this time with Turkey, Qatar and Indonesia. The Badr agreement, signed in Doha, offers opportunities for industrial cooperation and defense production.

Together with Makkah, the agreements deepen Pakistan's military, diplomatic and economic ties across countries pursuing different regional agendas.

That tension was evident during Munir's Tehran visit. Pakistani government sources told Turkey's state-run Anadolu news agency that the talks focused more on stopping Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia than on reviving US-Iran negotiations.

Munir pressed Iranian leaders to use their influence over the Houthis, citing Pakistan's commitment to defend the kingdom.

Saudi Arabia and other Persian Gulf states supply much of Pakistan’s energy, while millions of Pakistani workers live in the region. Defense cooperation brings financial support and industrial opportunities, while diplomacy helps protect relations with competing partners.

Pakistan appears to be carving out an unusual role: mediating between Iran and the United States, helping defend Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, and joining new regional defense ventures while retaining direct access to Iranian leaders.

But the same network could become harder to manage if regional tensions escalate. The more security commitments Pakistan assumes, the greater the chance that relationships which currently give Islamabad leverage could eventually force it to choose between them.

https://www.internazionale.it/ultime-not.heading: Ship attacks in Strait of Hormuz hit record high in October - Internazionale
https://www.internazionale.it/ultime-not.body:
OSLO, Oct 23 (Reuters) - October has been the worst month for attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waterways, according to data compiled by a Washington-based think tank that has tracked maritime security incidents worldwide since 2017.

“October has seen the highest number of ship attacks on record,” said Noam Raydan, a senior fellow at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy.

Raydan, who maintains the institute’s interactive shipping incident map, has recorded 28 confirmed and reported attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waterways in October and 113 since the US-Israeli war with Iran began on February 28.

The institute’s map shows most of the attacks that took place in September and October were in the Strait of Hormuz.

AROUND 3.5% OF WORLD SUPERTANKER FLEET ATTACKED

The tally broadly aligns with data from the International Maritime Organization (IMO), which recorded a total of 120 incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and the wider Middle East since the conflict with Iran began.

The IMO lists more than 30 supertankers, or Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs), that were damaged during the attacks, including 11 in October alone, a Reuters review of the IMO list and MarineTraffic vessel data showed.

Each VLCC can carry about 2 million barrels of crude. The listed vessels account for about 3.5% of the total global VLCC fleet, which exceeds 900.

More tankers came under attack as shipowners became increasingly willing to load cargoes inside the Gulf, lured by daily freight rates exceeding $1 million and steeper discounts offered by regional producers against dated Brent.

“October 2026 has emerged as the most intense period of maritime attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz since the escalation of hostilities in March,” Greece-based consultancy Marisks said.

Between October 5 and October 11, a dozen ships were attacked, marking also the highest weekly number of attacks since the conflict began, it also said.

NOT ALL ATTACKS MAY BE CAPTURED IN DATA

By intensifying attacks, Iran is seeking to slow the recovery in shipments and maintain pressure on global energy markets ahead of November’s US midterm elections, Raydan said.

Earlier this month, Reuters reported about Tehran adopting such tactics, citing two senior Iranian officials.

UKMTO, the British maritime security service, which recorded 135 incidents related to the US-Iran conflict as of October 16, said it was struggling to capture the whole picture due to insufficient voluntary reporting by shippers.

The UKMTO data also showed a sharp rise in ship damage caused by attacks in October.

(Reporting by Nerijus Adomaitis, editing by Alex Lawler and Tomasz Janowski)

https://www.defensenews.com/global/midea.heading: Saudi missile plant expansion may produce more powerful missiles, study says - Defense News
https://www.defensenews.com/global/midea.body:
Saudi Arabia appears to be expanding its ballistic missile factory to build larger solid-fuel missiles that could fly farther or carry heavier payloads, according to two U.S. researchers who analyzed more than a year of commercial satellite images.

More capable missiles could help Saudi Arabia to deter attacks by Iran and make its military more self-reliant, while possibly strengthening its position in a deadly conflict with Yemen’s Tehran-backed Houthi fighters.

But they risk fueling a regional missile race and could deepen opposition in the U.S. Congress to a U.S.-Saudi civilian nuclear agreement that has already raised concerns about proliferation.

Satellite company Planet Labs, based in the U.S., took images of the al-Duwadimi complex about 125 miles west of Riyadh between April 2025 and September 2026.

The two researchers, Sam Lair and Michael Duitsman of the Foreign Policy Research Institute, assessed that those images show a new building that houses casting pits — wells in which a mixture of fuel ingredients is poured into missile motor casings and allowed to harden.

The Saudi embassy and Information Ministry did not respond to requests for comment.

The building, flanked by what appear to be walls to protect nearby structures from accidental explosions, is at least twice as large as the one believed to house the plant’s existing casting pits, Lair and Duitsman said in their assessment. The Foreign Policy Research Institute (FPRI) is a non-partisan research organization in Philadelphia.

A second new building could be used to store fuel ingredients or finished missile components, they said.

The imagery “suggests that Saudi Arabia is expanding the infrastructure at the missile production complex, likely to produce larger missiles which could deliver larger payloads or reach longer ranges,” they wrote.

Militaries favor solid-fuel missiles because they can be stored for long periods and launched more quickly than liquid-fuel systems.

Lair and Duitsman and experts from the London-based International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) and the CNA research and analysis organization told Reuters that the makeup of Saudi Arabia’s missile force suggests that the al-Duwadimi complex relies on Chinese technology. Lair and Duitsman said that its characteristics are also similar to Chinese missile plants.

Saudi Arabia secretly acquired about 40 liquid-fuel DF-3 ballistic missiles from China in 1987, according to a 1991 declassified CIA estimate. It displayed two of them for the first time in an April 2014 military parade, according to a YouTube video and photographs of the event.

The FPRI team also recently identified from social media videos and photos what they assessed was the wreckage in Yemen of a Saudi-fired Chinese-designed DF-15 missile.

Lair said the kingdom may now be producing the solid-fuel DF-15, and that the expansion of a1-Dumadimi is likely for the production of the longer-range DF-21 or a similar missile.

Riyadh is believed to have turned to Beijing because Washington has long restricted exports of longer-range missile systems.

The Chinese embassy and defense ministry did not respond to requests for comment. The CIA declined to comment. The White House did not respond to a request for comment.

Sascha Bruchmann, a research fellow at IISS, said longer-range missiles would allow Saudi Arabia to strike Iran without risking its U.S.-supplied F-15 jet fighters against Iranian air defenses.

“You’d want a system to threaten whatever is holy to Tehran … if you don’t have the political will to send an F-15 with JDAMs over Tehran,” said Bruchmann, referring to U.S.-made satellite-guided bombs. “Iran has a lead because its missiles and drones can strike Saudi wherever it wants. The Saudis could close that capability gap a bit.”

Bruchmann, who reviewed the FPRI analysis at Reuters request, concurred that the expansion of al-Duwadimi could be for producing more powerful solid-fuel missiles.

Janes, the defense intelligence company, also reviewed it and said the buildings “may suggest an effort to expand production capability or support the development of longer-range missiles.”

Saudi Arabia’s apparent pursuit of more powerful missiles comes as other Gulf powers are also seeking to expand their offensive and defensive arsenals, said Decker Eveleth, a CNA analyst who has been tracking the al-Duwadimi construction with commercial satellite imagery and concurred with the FPRI assessment.

“This is being replicated across the Middle East,” he said. “You see exactly the same thing happening in the UAE. You see the exact same thing happening in Turkey. Everybody is doing this now.”

The expansion of al-Duwadimi could have political consequences in the US by stiffening bipartisan congressional opposition to a US-Saudi agreement under which the US would help Riyadh establish uranium enrichment for power generation.

Opponents say that the deal lacks sufficient safeguards to prevent Riyadh from secretly building a nuclear weapon. The kingdom has denied any such plan.

The FPRI assessment said the Planet Labs imagery showed that the expansion at al-Duwadimi began in April 2025 with ground-clearing and digging for the suspected storage building. Work on the suspected casting-pit building began later that month or in early May, it said.

A December 12, 2025, photo showed what researchers assessed were two deep pits inside the building that had no roof yet.

A Sept. 18, 2026, photo shows the roof still partly missing and “heavy duty blast diverting walls” on either side to prevent accidental explosions from damaging adjacent structures.

The walls, the researchers said, are somewhat similar to those depicted in imagery of US and Iranian missile plants and “further evidence the building is for casting solid propellant motors.”

Finishing the roofs would not take long, the FPRI said, but installing casting equipment may take several months. The facility could be ready to start producing missiles as early as the end of the year.

Minister Fidan expressed understanding of our concerns and stressed the need for continued consultations to address them https://t.co/Pwn7HMNNn6

— Badr Abdelatty (@EgyptForeignMin) October 23, 2026

Abdelatty reaffirmed Egypt’s position during a meeting with Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, focusing on the approval of the agreement by Libya’s eastern-based House of Representatives, according to a post by the Egyptian minister on X.

The memorandum was signed in November 2019 by Turkey and the then Tripoli-based Government of National Accord, led by Fayez al-Sarraj. It seeks to delimit maritime jurisdiction between Turkey and Libya in the Mediterranean and has been at the center of a long-running dispute over maritime boundaries and sovereign rights in the eastern Mediterranean.

According to Abdelatty’s account, Egypt reiterated its categorical rejection of the agreement’s ratification. Fidan, for his part, expressed understanding of the Egyptian side’s concerns and stressed the need for continued consultations to address them.

The meeting comes amid mounting regional opposition following the eastern Libyan parliament’s approval of the memorandum on Oct. 20, reversing its previous rejection of the agreements concluded with Ankara in 2019.

Cairo has argued that the memorandum violates international law, including the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), and cannot have legal consequences for Egypt’s maritime rights. Egypt has also rejected any actions based on the agreement that conflict with its declared maritime boundaries.

Greece has likewise lambasted the memorandum, arguing that Turkey and Libya do not have opposite or adjacent coastlines that would provide a legal basis for the proposed delimitation and that the agreement flagrantly disregards the maritime entitlements of Greek islands, including Crete, the fifth-largest island in the Mediterranean. Athens has maintained that the Libyan parliament’s decision does not change the agreement’s legal status.

The dispute has also prompted Greece to raise the issue at the UN Security Council, while the European Union has reiterated that the memorandum infringes on the sovereign rights of third states, does not comply with the international law of the sea and is null and void.

Greece and Egypt signed an agreement partially delimiting their exclusive economic zones in August 2020. Both countries have stressed the importance of settling maritime-boundary disputes in accordance with international law and UNCLOS, while continuing diplomatic coordination over the implications of the Turkey-Libya memorandum.

https://www.turkishminute.com/2026/10/23.heading: European, Mideast foreign ministers discuss regional crises in İstanbul - Turkish Minute
https://www.turkishminute.com/2026/10/23.body:
Foreign ministers from eight countries met in İstanbul on Friday for their first talks in an expanded format on the Strait of Hormuz, conflicts across the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine war.

Ministers from Britain, France and Germany — the so-called E3 — and Italy met their counterparts from the newly created R4 group of Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt to discuss the Palestinians, developments in Yemen and Hormuz, and ways to end the Russia-Ukraine war, a Turkish foreign ministry source said.

The talks began at a hotel overlooking the Bosporus after separate meetings among the European ministers and their regional counterparts, the source added.

British Foreign Minister Ed Miliband’s office said the talks would focus on “the Strait of Hormuz and the situation in Saudi Arabia.”

Miliband “will advocate for a diplomatic solution to the [Hormuz] crisis that restores full navigational rights and freedoms,” his office said.

He will also stress “how Iranian tactics are being replicated across the region, with attacks on Saudi Arabia further destabilising the region and increasing pressure on vital waterways and global chokepoints, such as Bab El-Mandeb and the Suez Canal,” it added.

France confirmed the talks would address “the Iranian crisis in its various ramifications,” describing the meeting as a first “in this format … against a backdrop of extreme instability and uncertainty in the region.”

The aim is to “strengthen coordination between Europeans and Middle Eastern countries in the face of crises that we did not choose and that affect us all,” the French foreign ministry said.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan is hosting the meeting as Ankara seeks a stronger regional role, including through the Mecca Defence Alliance, a defense pact launched with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in August.

Turkey says the pact is not directed against any specific country and remains open to other members, including Egypt.

Cairo has yet to decide whether to join. On Wednesday President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said Egypt would “defend Saudi territory” and would not take part in any attack on Yemen.

Intensifying attacks by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis have forced Saudi Arabia to close its main airport and postpone a major investment conference. A maritime blockade has also threatened oil exports from the world’s largest crude exporter.

Riyadh has since secured support from its allies. During a surprise visit Wednesday, French President Emmanuel Macron said French forces would help protect the Red Sea oil terminal of Yanbu.

Britain announced a day earlier that it would deploy fighter jets to help defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks.

Fidan praised regional cooperation Friday, saying, “Lasting solutions cannot be imposed from outside,” in an address to a mediation conference.

During the talks, he is expected to stress that countries in the region must “assume responsibility” for their security and that Turkey favors cooperation based on “regional ownership,” according to Turkish officials.

He is also expected to say that “existing disputes should not be allowed to feed one another, conflicts should not be allowed to spread to new areas, and regional tensions should not be allowed to turn into broader instability.”

On the Palestinians, Fidan is expected to call for increased international pressure on Israel over settlement expansion and what Ankara describes as “settler terrorism.”

He will also reiterate Turkey’s support for Saudi Arabia’s security against Houthi attacks and the need to safeguard freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb.

The Black Sea is also on the agenda, with Fidan expected to highlight Turkey’s efforts to prevent the Russia-Ukraine war from spreading into the region.

https://pajhwok.com/2026/10/23/putin-ukr.body:
KABUL (Pajhwok): Russian President Vladimir Putin has said future negotiations to end the war in Ukraine should focus on guaranteeing the security of Russia and Ukraine, as well as establishing a European security framework.

Reuters reported that Putin made the remarks in an interview with Russian state television on Thursday, a day after meeting Steve Witkoff, the US president’s special envoy.

Putin said Russia was ready to resume US-mediated negotiations with Ukraine next month.

He said the talks should aim to reach a peace agreement that guarantees the security of both countries, rather than establish a temporary ceasefire.

Putin said Witkoff had also emphasised the need to broaden discussions to include Europe’s security framework, a position with which he agreed.

Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who met Witkoff in Norway on Tuesday, said his country was ready for negotiations that could take place by early next month.

Zelenskyy added that Ukraine supported any proposals for a ceasefire, an end to the war, a ceasefire in the energy sector and humanitarian initiatives.

According to the report, US-led efforts to advance negotiations in February were suspended following the outbreak of hostilities involving the US, Israel and Iran.

Territory remains one of the main points of disagreement between Russia and Ukraine. Russia is demanding the handover of the entire Donbas region in eastern Ukraine, while Kyiv opposes surrendering areas it currently controls.

Putin said any discussions about territory in eastern Ukraine must take into account what he called “historical Russian territory”.

He also claimed that residents of these areas had voted to join Russia in referendums held seven months after Russia launched its invasion.

Austria’s foreign ministry said earlier that it declared the Vienna-based Russian diplomats personae non gratae over “activities incompatible with their diplomatic status,” a term usually used for spying.

“A response will follow inevitably,” Russia’s Deputy Foreign Minister Dmitry Lyubinsky told TASS without providing further details.

Three of the expelled diplomats worked at Russia’s Embassy in Vienna and one at the Russian delegation to the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) on military security and arms control, the Austrian ministry said.

The move brings the total number of Russian diplomats expelled in Austria over the past six years to 18. While Austria is a neutral country, politically its governments have sided with Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.
