KHERSON, Ukraine (AP) — Humanitarian aid is poised to roll into the stricken city of Oleshky, a Ukrainian official said Thursday, as a localized ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine stretched into a third day and military units cleared away landmines.

Moscow and Kyiv have observed the truce in and around the devastated southern Ukrainian city since Tuesday, but remain otherwise locked in the war that began with Russia’s full-scale invasion more than 4 ½ years ago. Previous efforts to secure ceasefires either never worked out or the truces quickly fell apart.

Elsewhere, a jet-powered Russian drone hit two passenger trains stopped at a station in Dnipro in central Ukraine on Thursday, killing at least 14 people and injuring 14 more, including a 40-year-old man whose legs were amputated, officials said.

Also, a Russian cruise missile killed two 15-year-old girls in the northern city of Chernihiv, and three more civilians died when a Russian drone hit an apartment block in the central Ukraine city of Kremenchuk, authorities said. In all, 56 people were injured in the strikes, including 10 children.

Russia’s Defense Ministry said air defenses downed 1,214 Ukrainian drones overnight in one of the largest drone attacks launched by Kyiv. Around half of the drones were heading to the Russian capital, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said.

The planned six-day ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky has brought a rare and welcome stillness for civilians in the nearby city of Kherson, which is held by Ukraine and has also been wracked by the war.

Both sides thanked U.S. first lady Melania Trump for what the White House said was her role in helping broker the temporary ceasefire so food and medical supplies can be delivered to some 2,000 desperate people trapped in Oleshky. Pope Leo XIV also pressed for a truce.

“The parties are fully adhering to the agreements, and no violations of the ceasefire have been reported,” Ukrainian ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said Thursday, adding that aid deliveries were due to begin the following day.

His Russian counterpart, Yana Lantratova, confirmed the truce was holding and that Russian engineers are working on demining Oleshky’s roads.

“Both sides are fully honoring their commitments, and no violations have been recorded,” she said. “This allows military personnel to continue clearing roads of mines and to prepare a safe passage for the humanitarian convoy.”

Local people will also be able to evacuate, either into Russia or Ukraine, officials say. The mechanics of how that might work are unclear.

Lantratova said she and her team were on their way to Oleshky for the aid delivery, adding that the operation was five months in the making.

Russian and Ukrainian representatives met in the Belarus city of Homel on Thursday to fly together to the Kherson region, Belarus state media reported.

A volunteer from Oleshky, Ksenia Arkhipova, told The Associated Press roughly 1,000 residents have told her they want to leave the city.

She said it was important that the Ukrainian delegation was present in Oleshky because many residents fear Russian authorities would identify individuals with pro-Ukrainian views or ties to Ukraine’s military.

In the nearby city of Kherson, growing numbers of people were out on the streets as the truce held.

Nataliia Myronenko, 42, had a steady stream of customers at her coffee kiosk since early Thursday.

“Now, during the quiet, we have people at lunchtime and in the evening, which we didn’t have under the attacks,” she said. “For a while, people would race down this street because they were afraid to stop.”

The pause has brought a sense of relief, she said. “It’s a breath of freedom, when you don’t look at the sky. You keep looking at your feet because of the mines, but you’re not afraid of dying. It’s so great,” she said.

“It’s such a privilege and a joy, but we understand it will end soon.”

Moscow and Kyiv are keen to curry favor with Washington ahead of possible three-way talks next month.

American military support is vital for Ukraine, but U.S. President Donald Trump has waived sanctions on Russia and publicly chided Zelenskyy, indicating he is disengaging with Kyiv.

Tankers carrying Russian diesel are sailing to the United States, and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov is expected to attend a G20 ministerial meeting in Atlanta, Georgia, starting Friday, according to Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova.

European leaders, on the other hand, have been trying to diplomatically isolate Russian President Vladimir Putin over Moscow’s invasion and what they call a campaign of sabotage across the continent.

Ukraine earlier this month reported sudden and unexpected limits on Starshield, the military-grade version of the Starlink satellite internet service owned by Elon Musk’s SpaceX that is the backbone of Ukraine’s drone operations and communications.

Putin said Russia has been in contact with the American tech titan to coordinate their orbiting activities because it is building its own equivalent of Starlink.

“Elon Musk is a genius. Truly, a real genius,” Putin said late Wednesday.

“We and our American partners value this relationship, and despite all the political issues, we continue to work closely together,” he added.

Associated Press journalists Yuras Karmanau in Tallinn, Estonia; Vasilisa Stepanenko in Kherson, Ukraine; and Susie Blann and Derek Gatopoulos in Kyiv, Ukraine, contributed.

Follow the AP’s coverage of the war in Ukraine at https://apnews.com/hub/russia-ukraine

https://apnews.com/article/trump-iran-st.heading: US warns allies to prepare for potential Iran strikes after election | AP News
https://apnews.com/article/trump-iran-st.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — U.S. officials have told several Middle East countries and regional allies to be prepared for potential renewed military action against Iran after next week’s midterm elections in the United States — as well as the possibility that Iran will attempt to retaliate against them, according to two diplomats briefed on the matter.

Both of the diplomats spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to comment about the sensitive warnings conveyed by U.S. diplomats and defense officials.

President Donald Trump has not made a final decision on whether to carry out new strikes against Iran, the diplomats stressed. The president, however, has repeatedly said that he is weighing ordering new military action once the critical Nov. 3 elections in the United States are over.

Those threats and the fresh U.S. urgings for allies to prepare for potential retaliation are putting the region on alert that a return to major operations could now be on the horizon.

The U.S. is warning Middle East allies that attacks against Iran may resume soon. AP correspondent Jennifer King reports.

The White House and U.S. officials declined to comment.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday in a post on X that Tehran “continues to give diplomacy a chance to succeed” and is working with mediators to review ideas that Tehran included in a proposal floated last month — summarily rejected by Trump — that the Iranians still want to see used as the basis to return to a ceasefire.

Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates foreign ministry issued a statement urging the sides to “exercise wisdom and pursue political solutions to help contain tensions” and prevent a return to full-scale operations in the war that began in late February.

The U.S. has told regional allies that the new round of military action could last for several days, but regional officials are bracing for Iran and its proxy groups to retaliate — leading to a fight that could last even longer, the diplomats said.

The allies have also been urged by U.S. officials to take precautionary measures in anticipation that Iran’s response will include retaliatory strikes on energy facilities and other crucial infrastructure.

It’s unclear how soon the U.S. military would be ready

While the U.S. has not carried out a strike against Iran since early September, the situation in the Middle East has become more complicated.

The conflict has spread, with Iran-backed Houthi rebels carrying out attacks on Saudi Arabia’s oil infrastructure and airports. A Saudi-led coalition has responded with its own deadly attacks on Houthi-held territory in Yemen.

The Wall Street Journal reported earlier on Gulf nations being briefed to be prepared for potential escalation by the U.S.

The Pentagon late last month deployed the USS Theodore Roosevelt, along with a series of amphibious landing ships with Marines aboard -- roughly 9,000 troops in all -- from San Diego to the Persian Gulf to bolster the U.S. military in the region.

At the time, one U.S. official said this deployment could lead to an unusually high naval presence of more than 20,000 sailors and Marines, as well as hundreds of aircraft, in the region, which has only occurred a handful of times in the last two decades. The Navy had three carrier strike groups in the Middle East in April for the first time since 2003.

Late Wednesday, reports emerged that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had fired the Pentagon’s top military planner. Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia was removed as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff, according to a defense official who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive personnel matters. That official said there is no immediate replacement for Sylvia and no reason has been given for the firing.

Trump, who has focused in recent weeks on campaigning for Republicans ahead of the Nov. 3 elections, has been evasive about what he plans to do next with Iran.

The war has proved to be a heavy weight on Republican candidates as they make their case to voters who are fatigued by rising gasoline prices, a byproduct of the war that’s driven up costs across nearly every sector in the global economy. The cost of fighting the Iran war to American taxpayers has grown to $47.1 billion, according to the latest estimate the Pentagon has provided to Congress.

While campaigning for Republicans, Trump has consistently assured voters that the war’s end is near, while also threatening that a new round of bombing could be coming once the election passes.

During a campaign stop in Lubbock, Texas, on Tuesday, Trump said a conclusive end to the eight-month-old conflict could be coming “in a couple of weeks, if you don’t mind.”

“Somebody asked me before, when will the war in Iran end?” Trump said earlier in the same address. “I said, ‘Whenever I want it to end.’ It’ll be very quick, but we have to have it end properly, with total and complete -- a total statement, they will never have a nuclear weapon.”

Trump may be looking at a postelection timeline for possible action, but the region is on edge that Tehran could do something provocative before then -- especially if they feel U.S. actions is imminent, said Jonathan Schanzer, executive director at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, a hawkish Washington think tank.

“Why would they wait until after the elections here ... if they could initiate it and potentially gain the upper hand?” he said.

The Pentagon has revised the number of U.S. troops who have died during operations related to the war against Iran to 23.

That total in the Pentagon’s reporting database, the Defense Casualty Analysis System, includes additional noncombat deaths recorded in updates Wednesday and Thursday.

The latest deaths were airmen. The Air Force did not provide any additional details.

https://ipn.md/en/fines-of-e5500-in-alba.heading: Fines of €5,500 in Albania for participants in violent protests - ipn.md
https://ipn.md/en/fines-of-e5500-in-alba.body:
The authorities in Tirana have introduced fines of €5,500 for participants in demonstrations that turn violent, even if they do not personally commit any acts of violence. The measure was adopted amid anti-government protests that have been ongoing for several months, IPN reports.

According to The Guardian, the measure, approved by the government, provides for fines of up to 500,000 lek, equivalent to €5,500, for people who remain in a crowd engaged in violence or looting in a public place, or who conceal their identity. The average gross salary in Albania is around €930, the British newspaper notes.

At the same time, police have been granted additional powers to temporarily restrict gatherings in certain areas, including near educational institutions, medical facilities and government buildings, if there is a risk of violence breaking out. The measures also provide for penalties for inciting violence online and compensation for small businesses whose property was damaged during the protests.

Peaceful anti-government protests have been taking place in Tirana since May. Demonstrators oppose plans to build a luxury resort in a nature reserve, a project backed by Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump. This month, the demonstrations escalated into violent clashes between protesters and police. Students have also joined the demonstrations, taking to the streets to protest against corruption, shortcomings in the healthcare system, and the lack of opportunities for young people in Albania.

Prime Minister Edi Rama has repeatedly attributed the violence to foreign state actors, accusing both Russia and Iran of spreading disinformation online. At the same time, he has called for dialogue between protesters and the authorities.

https://euronews.al/en/tensions-erupt-in.heading: Tensions Erupt in Albanian Parliament as Opposition MPs Light Flares, Four Expelled from Session - Euronews Albania
https://euronews.al/en/tensions-erupt-in.body:
The Albanian Parliament’s plenary session resumed amid tensions after opposition MPs lit flares inside the chamber, blocked the parliamentary rostrum and blew whistles.

Following the disruption, Speaker of Parliament Niko Peleshi decided to expel four opposition MPs from the plenary session: Xhelal Mziu, Bledi Himçi, Ivi Kaso and Bledion Nallbati.

Tensions also escalated during Thursday’s plenary session when Speaker Niko Peleshi barred Democratic Party leader Sali Berisha from speaking for the remainder of the session, arguing that he had incited violence from the parliamentary rostrum.

The decision followed remarks by Berisha, who, referring to the violence used against students during protests, said that the same violence should be used against Socialist Party MPs.

Peleshi described Berisha’s statement as an incitement to violence and decided to revoke his speaking rights for the remainder of Thursday’s session.

https://en.vijesti.me/world-a/balkan/833.heading: Four people killed in EUFOR helicopter crash in Bosnia and Herzegovina
https://en.vijesti.me/world-a/balkan/833.body:
Four EUFOR members were killed and 11 were injured in the crash of an Italian military helicopter near Brčko, Bosnia and Herzegovina, today.

The injured are in stable condition and are receiving medical assistance, it was confirmed by the European Union military mission that oversees the military implementation of the Dayton Peace Agreement.

The helicopter crashed during a routine training exercise, they said.

No civilians were injured in the accident, nor was there any damage to civilian infrastructure, property or vehicles.

Bosnia and Herzegovina emergency services and members of EUFOR's Liaison and Observation Teams (LOT) arrived at the scene of the accident.

They participated in the extraction of people from the helicopter, after which they were all transported to health facilities in Brčko.

EUFOR announced that a detailed investigation has been launched to determine the facts and circumstances that led to the tragic accident.

They said the public would be informed of the new information after it was verified.

https://en.vijesti.me/news-b/politika/83.heading: Ibrahimović: Turkey is a sincere friend, reliable partner and important ally of Montenegro
https://en.vijesti.me/news-b/politika/83.body:
Montenegro sincerely values its friendship with Turkey and remains committed to its further development, said Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Ervin Ibrahimović, at a ceremonial reception marking the Day of the Republic of Turkey, organized by the embassy of that country in Podgorica.

Congratulating the 103rd anniversary of the founding of the Republic of Turkey, Ibrahimović emphasized the importance that the country has on the regional and international scene, emphasizing that Montenegro sees Turkey as a sincere friend, reliable partner and important ally, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced.

"Montenegro sincerely values its friendship with Turkey and remains committed to its further development. Our countries are connected by history and common heritage, but what makes us especially happy is the future that we can build together," said Ibrahimović.

Speaking about bilateral relations, he recalled their "deep historical roots", pointing out that diplomatic relations between the Principality of Montenegro and the Ottoman Empire date back to 1878. He emphasized that the common historical and cultural heritage, visible in architecture, tradition, language and everyday life, represents an important part of Montenegro's multicultural identity and a solid foundation for contemporary relations between the two countries.

He particularly emphasized the role of emigrants from Montenegro in Turkey, who "throughout generations preserve ties with the land of their ancestors and at the same time contribute to the development of Turkish society." As he pointed out, it is the people, their family ties and mutual closeness that give lasting value to the friendship between the two countries.

Reflecting on contemporary relations, Ibrahimović assessed that the friendship between Montenegro and Turkey is developing through intensive political dialogue, mutual trust and increasingly meaningful cooperation in the areas of economy, investment, tourism, education and culture. He expressed his belief that the existing partnership will continue to be improved through concrete projects and initiatives that benefit the citizens of both countries.

The minister, as announced, particularly emphasized Turkey's constructive role in the Western Balkans and its contribution to regional dialogue, peace and stability, emphasizing that the NATO alliance further strengthens bilateral relations and shared responsibility for the security of the region and the wider Euro-Atlantic area.

In this context, he reiterated that Montenegro remains firmly committed to the strategic goal of membership in the European Union, while thanking Turkey for supporting Montenegro's European aspirations.

Finally, Ibrahimović expressed his gratitude to the Turkish Ambassador to Montenegro, Ayda Unlu, for her hospitality and commitment to strengthening bilateral relations, along with congratulations to the leadership and citizens of Turkey on the occasion of the national holiday and "wishes for further progress, peace and prosperity."

"May our friendship be even stronger, our meetings even more frequent, and our ties even closer," Ibrahimović said.

https://europeanwesternbalkans.com/2026/.heading: Milojko Spajić: A new era has arrived in relations between Montenegro and Serbia - European Western Balkans
https://europeanwesternbalkans.com/2026/.body:
PODGORICA – Speaking about regional relations during Prime Minister’s Hour in Parliament, Prime Minister Milojko Spajić announced that a new era has arrived in relations between Montenegro and Serbia, RTCG reported.

“We have been ready for top-level cooperation with Serbia since the start of our mandate, though the opportunity was not there. We welcome statements from election winners indicating a turning point. With great pleasure, we will work to build the climate these two peoples deserve”, he noted.

Spajić stressed that Montenegro, as the smallest Balkan nation, holds a special duty to foster good neighborliness.

“Our country lacks a dominant identity group, perhaps uniquely in Europe, and has long been a divided society. Gone are the days when a census was a life-or-death dilemma or a simple statistical question. Today, Montenegro is a civic state where everyone can freely express their views”, he remarked.

https://n1info.rs/english/news/vucic-den.heading:
Vucic denies planning election night violence: “No foreign officials called me”
                - Vesti iz Srbije, regiona i sveta - N1 info
https://n1info.rs/english/news/vucic-den.body:
Aleksandar Vucic, the lead candidate on the United Serbia electoral list, denied Thursday that he had planned election night violence or that he allegedly backed down after receiving calls from abroad.

Speaking at a Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) press conference, Vucic said that, as the leader of the United Serbia electoral list, he had met with top police officials and told them that if he lost the election, he would concede immediately - but if he won, he would not allow anyone to steal that victory.

“No one called,” Vucic said, noting that his “first conversation with a foreigner” took place around 11:15 pm, when former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban called him. He added that he later spoke with French President Emmanuel Macron and a few other friends, and two days later with European Council President Antonio Costa.

According to Vucic, the initial results on election night came from smaller polling stations, showing his list in the lead. However, once he saw the stratified voting sample, he realized they had suffered a landslide defeat, primarily in Belgrade and Vojvodina, and that the vote gap was much wider than initially thought.

He said that he felt it was pointless to keep counting votes and prolonging tensions, which is why he decided around 9:30 pm to concede the election and congratulate his political opponents.

“Not a single foreign official had called me up to that point. Not one,” Vucic said, repeating accusations against the student movement for what he called “outright terror” against political opponents following their election victory.

https://en.vijesti.me/world-a/balkan/833.heading: Protests in Kosovo over the murder of a woman in Peja, who repeatedly reported violence and sought protection
https://en.vijesti.me/world-a/balkan/833.body:
Today is the second day of protests in Kosovo with banners reading "Sleep will not be able to catch you, you will burn" and "Silence protects the abuser, not the victim", in connection with the murder of Arljinda Zekaj on October 25th in Peja.

The protesters are demanding the resignations of the Ministers of Justice and Interior, Donika Gervala and Dželjalj Svečlja.

Liridona Sijarina from the Collective for Feminist Thought and Action said, in a speech in front of the Kosovo Government building, that protests will be held daily until the demands are met.

They also demand the prosecution of those responsible who, according to the protesters, neglected the case of Arljinda Zekaj, who was killed by her former brother-in-law even though she sought protection from the authorities.

The Kosovo Prosecutorial Council today suspended the Chief Prosecutor of the Basic Prosecution Office in Peja, Ljumturije Vučetaj, as well as Arljinda Nalbani Gacaferi, the prosecutor who led the case of Arljinda Zekaj.

Disciplinary proceedings have also been initiated against them, and an investigative panel has been formed to review the manner in which the case was handled.

The Kosovo Police, at the proposal of the Kosovo Police Inspectorate, suspended 11 senior police officials in Peja for failing to act in accordance with the law in the Zekaj case.

It was announced that the inspectorate has hired a team of investigators and is undertaking investigative and verification actions regarding the manner in which the Kosovo Police acted in the cases reported by Zekaj.

It was announced that the Kosovo Police Inspectorate has so far determined that the police did not document that the protection order in the Zekaj case from September 7 was executed, and the second protection order, from October 16, was executed with a delay of six days, at the urging of Zekaj herself.

It is added that the chain of command failed to act on a letter dated October 23, 2026, sent by a police investigator requesting a case assessment and additional support in a domestic violence case, as well as an assessment of the level of risk and enforcement of the decision of the competent court.

The omissions relate to the Regional Police Directorate in Peja, the Police Station in Peja, the Police Substation in Vitomirica, as well as investigative units at the regional and police station levels.

In accordance with this recommendation, the acting regional director of the Regional Police Directorate in Peja, the head of regional investigations of the Regional Police Directorate in Peja, the commander of the Police Station in Peja, and the deputy commander of the Police Station in Peja were suspended.

The Head of the Investigation Sector at the Peja Police Station, the Acting Head of the Operations Sector at the Peja Police Station, the Commander of the Vitomiric Police Substation and four police investigators at the Peja Police Station were also suspended.

Arljinda Zekaj was killed on the evening of October 25th in Vitomirica near Peja, a few minutes after she returned to her family home with police escort, where, according to the prosecution, she was killed with an axe by her brother-in-law, Aljbert Silaj. He was arrested in Dečani on October 27th.

Zekaj had previously reported domestic violence several times and sought protection from institutions, and on October 22, three days before the murder, she addressed the Chief Prosecutor in Peja, complaining about the way her case was handled and the non-enforcement of the court decision.

Prime Minister Albin Kurti has requested detailed reports from the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Interior to clarify institutional failures, accountability, and the reasons why warnings about the danger to Arljinda's life did not lead to effective protection.

https://eng.belta.by/politics/view/belar.heading: Belarus seeks to expand production of machinery in Vietnam
https://eng.belta.by/politics/view/belar.body:
MINSK, 29 October (BelTA) – Belarusian Minister of Foreign Affairs Maxim Ryzhenkov visited Vietnam’s Hung Yen Province on 29 October during his official visit to the country, BelTA learned from the Belarusian Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Representatives of the Belarusian ministries of health, education, and industry also travelled to the Vietnamese province as part of the delegation.

During the meeting between Maxim Ryzhenkov and Nguyen Manh Quyen, chairman of the Provincial People’s Committee, the Vietnamese side laid particular emphasis on the historical brotherly ties between the two countries. The Belarusian minister, in turn, noted that personal agreements between Belarusian President Aleksandr Lukashenko and General Secretary of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Vietnam To Lam provided the foundation for developing bilateral relations.

Maxim Ryzhenkov said that interregional cooperation was viewed as a key tool for translating the strategic partnership into concrete projects. In his words, Hung Yen Province could serve as a reliable point of support for Belarus in Vietnam.

The parties discussed prospects for expanding supplies of Belarusian agricultural, municipal, and forestry machinery, as well as issues of transferring competencies for servicing that machinery and training relevant engineering personnel. In this context, Maxim Ryzhenkov recalled Belarus’ significant historical contribution to the mechanization of Vietnam’s agriculture.

Minsk Automobile Plant (MAZ) trucks are already assembled in the Vietnamese province. The Belarusian side proposed expanding the range of goods manufactured there to include specialized vehicles and expressed hope that the local authorities would support these efforts.

The talks also addressed plans to establish dairy production using Belarusian raw materials. Minsk expects the formalities required to begin construction of the plant to be completed soon.

The parties also agreed to strengthen cooperation between Minsk Oblast and Hung Yen Province. On behalf of the Minsk Oblast Executive Committee leadership, Maxim Ryzhenkov invited the provincial leader to visit Belarus.

The Vietnamese side acknowledged the considerable untapped potential for bilateral cooperation and confirmed its readiness to facilitate the implementation of practical projects.

Maxim Ryzhenkov also visited GMA Automobile Industry, where he looked at the MAZ truck assembly process. He discussed prospects for further developing the company with its management and the deputy chairman of the Hung Yen People’s Committee.

During his visit to Hung Yen Province, Maxim Ryzhenkov also toured the Vietnam Military History Museum and laid a wreath at a monument honoring Soviet specialists who contributed to securing Vietnam’s independence and peace.

https://en.belsat.eu/96193346/ukrainian-.heading: Ukrainian and Russian officials meet in Homiel before Oleshky humanitarian operation
https://en.belsat.eu/96193346/ukrainian-.body:
On October 29, Ukrainian and Russian delegations participating in a humanitarian operation in Oleshky met in Homiel.

According to the BelTA news agency, representatives of the two countries shook hands and conversed, with "a positive tone set from the very first minutes of the meeting."

"Homiel Airport has become the starting point for the major route of this operation," BelTA reported regarding the meeting of the Ukrainian and Russian delegations taking part in the humanitarian mission to rescue residents of Russian-occupied Oleshky in Kherson Region.

The Ukrainians, led by Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets, arrived in Homiel via the Novaya Huta border checkpoint, while the Russian delegation arrived by plane.

"A positive tone was set from the very first minutes of the meeting. Representatives of Moscow and Kyiv exchanged handshakes and spoke. The meeting took place with the participation of the Belarusian side, which is also joining the humanitarian operation," the state-run media outlet writes.

The agency emphasizes that Belarus "is actively participating in this major international process, has become the initial staging ground, and has already begun fulfilling its part of the obligations under previously reached agreements," while "Minsk is providing necessary comprehensive assistance to Moscow and Kyiv and acting as a guarantor of these processes."

Fox News recently published a letter stating that residents of Oleshky who wish to evacuate to Ukraine will be transported via Homiel. Evacuees will first be taken to Anapa, and from there, on October 31, by a Russian Defense Ministry military transport aircraft to Belarus.

The ceasefire in Oleshky has been ongoing since October 27. Since that day, both Ukraine and Russia have confirmed that the cessation of hostilities is being observed.

Additionally, both sides confirm that they have begun clearing mines from roads connecting the town to ensure the safe delivery of humanitarian supplies.

The sides agreed to the ceasefire thanks to mediation by US First Lady Melania Trump. The humanitarian mission will be observed by four journalists from the American conservative media outlet Newsmax.

"They will independently record everything happening and provide continuous documentation of this historic humanitarian mission," Trump stated.

According to the Ukrainian side, since May 2026, Russian-occupied Oleshky has remained under complete blockade without access to food and medicine.

Before the full-scale war, the town had a population of about 24,000, while current figures from the Kherson Region administration place it at around 2,000.

https://www.moldpres.md/eng/politics/mol.heading: Moldovan Ambassador to Austria, at Forum for Security Cooperation, says Moldova condemns Russia’s attacks on Ukraine, warns of risks to regional security
https://www.moldpres.md/eng/politics/mol.body:
Moldova’s Ambassador to Austria and Slovakia, Permanent Representative at OSCE Victoria Rosa has firmly condemned the Russian Federation’s war of aggression against Ukraine at a meeting of the Forum for Security Cooperation (FSC). The official highlighted the war’s serious impact on the security of Moldova and the entire region.

According to the Foreign Affairs Ministry (MAE), the ambassador drew attention to repeated violations of Moldova’s airspace, including recent incidents in which drones crashed near the localities of Codrenii Noi, Donduseni district, and Chistelnita, Telenesti district.

"These incidents constitute violations of our country’s sovereignty and endanger the safety of citizens. Since February 2022, national authorities have recorded 102 airspace violations, of which 65 this year. The MAE firmly condemns the Russian Federation’s attacks on Ukraine’s civilian population and energy infrastructure, which cause loss of life and worsen the humanitarian situation, particularly as the cold season nears. We reiterate the need to hold those responsible for these attacks accountable", the institution said.

Moldova also expressed solidarity with Romania, in the context of destabilizing actions and violations of its airspace.

"We condemn the attacks on commercial vessels and port infrastructure in the Black Sea and support the European Union’s call for the immediate establishment of a moratorium on these attacks", the MAE emphasized.

In the context, the MAE called on the Russian Federation to end its war of aggression and withdraw its military forces from the territory of Ukraine. The institution reiterated that Moldova supports a just and lasting peace, based on respect for international law and for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

https://www.rferl.org/a/moldova-cyberatt.heading: Moldovan President Calls Security Meeting After Massive Data Breach
https://www.rferl.org/a/moldova-cyberatt.body:
Moldovan President Maia Sandu has convened a meeting of the country's National Security Council (CNS) days after a large-scale cyberattack on government information systems.

The attack, most likely carried out with the help of artificial intelligence, resulted in the extraction of personal data belonging to approximately 750,000 Moldovans.

On October 29, Sandu's office announced that the meeting would take place in "the coming days to assess the attack and determine appropriate response measures."

A day earlier, Prime Minister Vasile Tofan told cabinet ministers that there were "indications of a broader campaign involving foreign state actors" and that investigators were looking into "their involvement in the recent incident."

He did not specify which countries were suspected of being involved.

Officials from several European nations have been warning for months of an expanding campaign of hybrid activity -- hostile actions short of open warfare, including cyberattacks, sabotage, and the weaponization of migration -- by Russia amid its war on Ukraine.

Wedged between NATO member Romania -- with which it shares close linguistic and cultural ties -- to the west and war-ravaged Ukraine to the east, Moldova has struggled to shield itself from the fallout of Moscow's full-scale invasion.

According to Moldova's Electronic Government Agency (AGE), the attack targeted about one million people, almost half of the country's population, with attempts to extract data associated with personal identification numbers (IDNPs) taking place between October 19 and October 23.

Authorities have preventively suspended 82 digital public services and disconnected over 30 information systems to limit unauthorized access, it added.

The compromised data could include identification details, such as names and dates and places of birth; information about immediate family members; health insurance status and family doctors; social benefits, pensions, and disability status; driver's license details and photographs; vehicles and companies owned or managed; and financial information, including International Bank Account Numbers (IBANs), tax debts, and payment histories.

AGE said bank card data was not affected and that no unauthorized changes were identified in state registers.

The attackers allegedly exploited vulnerabilities in services accessible without authentication, subsequently using the information obtained to attempt additional data extraction.

Authorities said security problems had been addressed in most affected services, while the remaining ones would be gradually restored once security measures had been verified. A broader review of government systems was also under way to identify and fix vulnerabilities.

AGE warned that cyberattacks pose a growing threat to public institutions, with advances in artificial intelligence making it easier to automate attacks and identify security weaknesses.

RFE/RL’s Moldova Service reaches 30 percent of the population in Moldova each week, increasing listeners’ understanding of local, regional, and global events.

https://ipn.md/en/maia-sandu-revokes-mol.heading: Maia Sandu revokes Moldovan citizenship of three people, including two members of the so-called legislature in Tiraspol - ipn.md
https://ipn.md/en/maia-sandu-revokes-mol.body:
President Maia Sandu has revoked the Moldovan citizenship of Iurie Cara and Andrei Safonov, members of the so-called Supreme Soviet in Tiraspol, as well as that of Serghei Verdes, who allegedly obtained citizenship in breach of the legal procedure, IPN reports.

The president has signed decrees revoking their citizenship. According to a statement from the President’s Office, Iurie Cara and Andrei Safonov took part in adopting unconstitutional measures that violate the rights of Moldovan citizens in the Transnistrian region. They also promote the ideology of the “Russian world” and advocate maintaining Russia’s illegal military presence in the country.

In the case of Serghei Verdes, the President’s Office states that he was granted citizenship of the Republic of Moldova in violation of legal procedures, despite an adverse opinion from the Intelligence and Security Service.

The procedure to revoke citizenship was initiated by the Public Services Agency on the basis of findings by the Security and Intelligence Service (SIS), the President’s Office said.

The law provides for the revocation of citizenship in cases involving particularly serious acts that harm the interests of the state, as well as in cases where citizenship was acquired by circumventing legal requirements.

https://www.vaticannews.va/en/vatican-ci.heading: Pope’s Almoner visits Ukraine to offer support to war-affected population - Vatican News
https://www.vaticannews.va/en/vatican-ci.body:
Archbishop Luis Marín de San Martín, Prefect of the Dicastery for the Service of Charity, visited Kyiv on 28 October as part of a mission to bring Pope Leo XIV’s support to people affected by the war in Ukraine.

Accompanied by Dicastery Undersecretary, Massimo Ralli, the Archbishop visited charitable centres, shelters and Church communities providing food, accommodation and psychological support to those in need.

The visit began on Tuesday, 27 October, following a 12-hour drive from Warsaw, Poland. Kyiv was the first stop on the mission, which is scheduled to conclude on Friday, 30 October, with visits to several cities, including Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro and Fastiv.

After celebrating Mass at the Apostolic Nunciature, Archbishop Marín visited a Caritas-Spes centre in Kyiv with Apostolic Nuncio Archbishop Visvaldas Kulbokas; Bishop Oleksandr Yazlovetskyi, Auxiliary Bishop of Kyiv-Zhytomyr and President of Caritas-Spes; and Father Vyacheslav Grynevych, its Executive Director.

The centre distributes food, provides shelter during attacks for people without a safe place to go, and offers material and psychological assistance to older people and women raising children while their husbands serve at the front.

Particular attention is given to children, many of whom have spent years away from in-person schooling, first because of the Covid-19 pandemic and later because of the war. Many have also been separated from their friends and face isolation.

The organization creates opportunities for children to meet and spend time together, helping them cope with the psychological effects of the conflict.

Archbishop Marín met volunteers and visited the areas where people take shelter during bombardments. Those who come to the centre can find warmth, a hot meal and a place to charge their mobile phones.

The delegation also visited an underground shelter equipped with camp beds. Archbishop Marín blessed the shelter and the people gathered there, praying for the Lord’s protection.

In Kyiv, the delegation also visited a Catholic church that is still under construction but already active as a parish and humanitarian centre.

Volunteers prepare hot meals there every day for hundreds of people, regardless of their religious affiliation. Generators provide electricity and heating, making the parish a place where people can find assistance and shelter.

The church also has a shelter with beds for people seeking protection during nighttime bombardments.

At the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church’s Curia in Kyiv, Archbishop Marín was welcomed by its general bursar, Liubomyr Yavoriv, together with collaborators and volunteers.

After visiting the Patriarchal Cathedral of the Resurrection of Christ, the delegation learned about the services provided by the Church, including the daily preparation of hundreds of hot meals and material, spiritual and psychological support for soldiers through the military ordinariate.

The Church also operates a radio station that broadcasts the Pope’s words and catechesis, helping maintain ties with the Church among people who cannot gather in person.

The meeting included a discussion of the most urgent needs and an exchange of gifts.

The final stop in Kyiv was a small centre established beside a building damaged by bombing.

A military chaplain founded the community in a prefabricated building, where Mass is celebrated and children and families receive material and psychological assistance. The community also offers pastoral care and organizes activities for children.

At Easter, for example, children painted eggs with their fathers who had returned from the front for a few days.

The centre began with a small group of people and has since grown into a larger community, providing support to families affected by the war.

https://armenpress.am/en/article/1264213.heading: Armenian, Azerbaijani and Georgian ambassadors to Italy discuss regional cooperation at panel - ARMENPRESS Armenian News Agency
https://armenpress.am/en/article/1264213.body:
Armenia’s Ambassador to Italy Vladimir Karapetyan, Azerbaijan’s Ambassador Elchin Huseynli, and Georgia’s Ambassador Tamara Liluashvili participated in a panel discussion titled "Caucasus at a Crossroads: Peace, Corridors, and a New Era of Cooperation," organized by Festival della Diplomazia.

The event was attended by approximately 150 academics and students from various Italian universities, journalists, and heads and representatives of think tanks, the Armenian Embassy in Italy said in a press release.

The discussion focused on strengthening peace in the region, developing transport links, expanding cooperation among South Caucasus countries, and prospects for improving connectivity between Central Asia, the South Caucasus, and Europe.

In his remarks, Ambassador Karapetyan addressed the steps and initiatives undertaken by the Armenian government and Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan to strengthen peace in the region, emphasizing the importance of dialogue, cooperation, and building mutual trust.

The ambassador also noted that, following the public’s backing in the parliamentary elections held this summer, the Armenian authorities had intensified their efforts to establish and maintain peace and stability in the region. He said that active dialogue with all countries in the region, initiatives to build trust, and concrete steps were aimed at consolidating the peace achieved.

Ambassador Karapetyan also expressed hope that the Armenian authorities’ commitment to ensuring a peaceful future for the region was in line with the aspirations of other South Caucasus countries.

https://hetq.am/en/article/185085.heading: Armenia Completes First Life-Saving Surgeries For Evacuated Gaza Children Under Joint WHO Humanitarian Mission
https://hetq.am/en/article/185085.body:
YEREVAN — Three children from the Gaza Strip, suffering from severe health conditions exacerbated by the ongoing war, have successfully undergone complex medical procedures and surgeries in Yerevan, Armenia’s Ministry of Health confirmed.

Accompanied by three guardians, the young patients arrived in the Armenian capital on September 30, 2026. Their evacuation and subsequent medical care were organized through a multi-agency humanitarian operation coordinated by Armenia’s Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the World Health Organization (WHO).

The initiative was first made public during a UN Security Council session on January 29, 2026. By April, the WHO had provided medical dossiers for forty children to Armenian authorities to evaluate local treatment capabilities. While early government assessments aimed to receive up to ten patients, three children were ultimately transferred in the initial phase and referred to specialized centers in Yerevan.

To fund the humanitarian mission, the Armenian government previously allocated 16.7 million drams from its reserve fund. The Ministry of Health noted that these funds covered the medical mission's airfare, short-term accommodation, visa fees, essential supplies like food and clothing, and the direct costs of the surgeries and hospital stays.

The patients were divided between two of the country's top pediatric and cardiovascular facilities:

Arabkir Medical Center: One child, who had previously undergone liver and kidney transplants in 2014 and 2015, was treated for a complex array of conditions. These included primary hyperoxaluria (a rare metabolic disorder), chronic kidney disease, liver failure, bilateral hearing loss, an eardrum rupture, and a severe skin infection in the knee. Following intensive treatment, doctors reported the child's transplanted organ functions as satisfactory and stable, and the patient is currently being discharged.

Nork-Marash Medical Center: The remaining two children underwent specialized surgeries for congenital heart defects. Hospital officials confirmed that one child has reached satisfactory condition and is preparing for discharge, while the second required an additional, clinically necessary follow-up surgery and is currently recovering in the postoperative phase.

The Ministry of Health expressed a clear intention to welcome subsequent groups of children from Gaza who require urgent medical intervention. However, officials emphasized that future transfers remain contingent upon a complex web of humanitarian, security, logistical, and financial variables.

Armenia Extends Two Support Programs for IDPs from Karabakh: Who Will Receive How Much

At a meeting on Thursday, the Armenian government decided to extend two social support programs for persons displaced from Nagorno-Karabakh.

YEREVAN, October 29. /ARKA/. At a meeting on Thursday, the Armenian government decided to extend two social support programs for persons displaced from Nagorno-Karabakh.

Specifically, beneficiaries of assistance under the program to support certain categories of IDPs will continue to receive payments until June 2027.

From January to March 2027, the monthly payment will be 30,000 drams, and from April to June, 15,000 drams. As of October 2026, approximately 46,000 people are using the program.

Specific groups of beneficiaries of this assistance include:

individuals with first or second degree disabilities, or with profound or severe functional limitations;

Persons receiving survivor's benefits or pensions;

Persons over 18 years of age studying in general education institutions, primary vocational (trade) institutions, or secondary vocational education institutions;

The government also extended the program of additional emergency social support for needy families displaced from Nagorno-Karabakh until December 2027.

The monthly assistance amount is 40,000 drams for the first displaced family member and 10,000 drams for each subsequent member.

Thus, a family with two displaced members can receive 50,000 drams per month, a family with three displaced members can receive 60,000 drams, and a family with four can receive 70,000 drams, subject to program conditions.

In October 2026, 8,600 families received assistance under this program.

Families with an average monthly income per family member of less than 55,000 drams are eligible for support. This figure is calculated by dividing the total monthly family income by the number of members.

IDPs from Nagorno-Karabakh are also eligible for other existing social assistance programs if they meet the established requirements.

Government Expenditures on IDP Support

In June 2026, Deputy Prime Minister of Armenia Tigran Khachatryan announced that 45.7 billion drams had been allocated from the state budget to support IDPs from Nagorno-Karabakh in 2025, and a total of approximately 146 billion drams from 2023.

Prime Minister of Armenia Nikol Pashinyan previously stated that the government plans to allocate approximately 800 billion drams to implement the housing program for IDPs from Nagorno-Karabakh.

On Azerbaijan's ethnic cleansing in Artsakh

On September 19-20, 2023, Azerbaijan launched a large-scale aggression against Artsakh using artillery, UAVs, and combat aircraft.

Residents of Artsakh were forced to move to Armenia. According to the Armenian government, more than 115,000 Artsakh residents have been registered, and assistance programs are in place.

https://arminfo.info/full_news.php?id=10.heading: Arminfo: A ruling party MP provoked a brawl in the Armenian parliament: a verbal altercation escalated into a fight.
https://arminfo.info/full_news.php?id=10.body:
Following offensive remarks by Taron Chakhoyan, a member of the ruling Civil Contract faction, about the family of Narek Karapetyan, head of the Strong Armenia faction, a verbal altercation erupted in the Armenian parliament.

It first escalated into a scuffle between members of parliament, and then into a physical altercation.

During his speech from the parliamentary rostrum, Chakhoyan made offensive remarks about members of Karapetyan's family.

Specifically, the member of parliament touched on the involvement of the Strong Armenia faction leader's relatives in political activities.

When Karapetyan attempted to respond to the ruling party representative's statements, Chakhoyan urged him not to speak, saying, "If you have the opportunity, speak from the podium."

After this, tensions in parliament increased.

Chakhoyan and Karapetyan began exchanging heated words, and representatives of the Strong Armenia faction attempted to prevent a potential fight.

However, the tension failed to subside, and the altercation escalated into a fistfight between legislators.

Amid the escalating situation, Armenian Parliament Speaker Ruben Rubinyan did not call a recess.

He stated that the session would continue so that citizens could see the behavior of the deputies and urged them to decide whether they intended to continue the fight or return to their seats.

However, tensions not only did not subside, but actually escalated.

Footage from the session hall shows scenes of physical altercation.

Moreover, cameras also captured the ruling party's Vice Speaker Vahagn Aleksanyan picking up a knife and throwing it at an opposition MP.

The Speaker of Parliament was forced to call in state security officers to calm the protesters.

However, the conflict continued in the parliament hallway.

Law enforcement officers were forced to build a wall between the ruling party and opposition MPs to calm them down.

The brawl resulted in damage to state property in the parliament hall.

https://www.pan.am/en/626902.heading: Mirzoyan challenges opposition to back constitutional referendum for peace (PAN.am)
https://www.pan.am/en/626902.body:
During a question-and-answer session in the National Assembly, Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan, addressing whether constitutional amendments are Azerbaijan’s final precondition for signing a peace treaty, proposed that the opposition support the government’s efforts to approve a draft new constitution in parliament and subsequently hold a referendum.

“Am I understanding you correctly that you are saying if this is the final outstanding issue, it is open for discussion and we could proceed with it? If it is confirmed that this is the final step standing between us and peace — the very last one — will you join us in taking that step? Think about it and let us know,” he said, according to 1lurer.am.

National Assembly Deputy Speaker Aram Vardevanyan had addressed a question to the foreign minister, noting that, on the one hand, officials say peace already exists on the ground and trade is taking place, raising the question of why a peace treaty has not yet been signed.

“Do you want a treaty? You don’t want to renegotiate the text that has already been drafted and initialed, do you? This is a very important historic acknowledgment. The opposition parliamentary faction believes that the initialed treaty text does not need to be negotiated or renegotiated, that it is acceptable and should be signed.

“Now, do you want to remove us from power? Let me say something else. Have you realized that the only way to remove us from power is through voting — a nationwide vote? Nothing else works. You have tried a military coup, you have tried a clerical-feudal movement, you have tried assassination attempts, there has been an attempt to kill me, and attempts to bribe people are continuing to this day, and so on. Can we establish that the only way to remove us from power is through elections?

“Therefore, it would be in your interest for us to go to the people as soon as possible, to another nationwide vote, wouldn’t it? Once again, I am making a political proposal: Let us bring forward the draft constitution, and you can declare right here that you condemn this draft constitution, that it is bad. Let us hold a constitutional referendum. Let us do it. This would be an opportunity for you. The people would say no to our constitution, and we would resign and leave office.

“Is that such a bad proposal? Dear citizens, I am proposing a solution. Demand that it happen,” Mirzoyan said.

Armenian Justice Minister Srbuhi Galyan has announced that the draft of Armenia’s new constitution will be presented to the public in the coming weeks. The minister particularly emphasized that the document to be made public is not final.

Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said during a press briefing that the draft constitution would be published soon, followed by public discussions. The draft would then be submitted to parliament, where the ruling political force would seek to convince the opposition that the matter is of fundamental importance.

“We will try to persuade them. If that does not work, we will pursue other scenarios, including the possibility of holding snap elections. Who said such a scenario is ruled out? What matters to me is that I have made a commitment to the citizens of the Republic of Armenia regarding both constitutional amendments and the signing and ratification of the peace agreement,” he said.

https://hetq.am/en/article/185092.heading: Former Armenian Finance Minister Gagik Khachatryan’s Detention Extended Amid Severe Health Concerns
https://hetq.am/en/article/185092.body:
YEREVAN — Armenia’s Anti-Corruption Court has extended the detention of Gagik Khachatryan, the country's former finance minister and former chairman of the State Revenue Committee (SRC), for an additional two months, sparking intense debate over his medical condition.

Khachatryan was originally placed in a penitentiary institution on September 2, 2026, following a ruling by Judge Aram Grigoryan. His arrest came after the Investigative Committee conducted extensive raids on September 1 at the residences of Khachatryan and his son, alongside the offices of roughly twenty-one affiliated companies. The multi-agency operation was part of an ongoing criminal investigation into allegations of especially large-scale bribery and money laundering.

Speaking to reporters following the extension, defense attorney Yerem Sargsyan raised serious alarms regarding his client's deteriorating health. Sargsyan stated that Khachatryan has been completely bedridden due to severe spinal issues since his initial detention nearly two months ago. The defense claims Khachatryan is already developing pressure sores and faces a high risk of contracting pneumonia.

According to Sargsyan, multiple appeals to the Penitentiary Medicine Center state organization to transfer Khachatryan to an inpatient medical facility have been repeatedly denied. The severity of Khachatryan's condition forced an adjournment during the recent extension hearing when the former minister suffered debilitating pain, requiring the administration of emergency painkillers.

Khachatryan, who served as Armenia’s Finance Minister from April 2014 to September 2016, has faced long-standing international scrutiny. In July 2024, the U.S. Department of Justice finalized a settlement to forfeit a US$60+ million Los Angeles mega-mansion belonging to his family, which U.S. prosecutors argued was purchased using a $20 million bribe from an Armenian businessman.

The defense is expected to continue challenging the detention on humanitarian and medical grounds as the state's large-scale corruption investigation proceeds.

https://www.azernews.az/nation/266450.ht.heading: Azerbaijan, Russia pledge to deepen cooperation in legal affairs
https://www.azernews.az/nation/266450.ht.body:
Azerbaijan’s Prosecutor General Kamran Aliyev met with his Russian counterpart, Alexander Gutsan, in Baku on October 29 to discuss bilateral cooperation between the two countries’ prosecution authorities.

Gutsan visited Baku at the invitation of Aliyev to attend the third high-level meeting of heads of anti-corruption law enforcement agencies of the member states of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation.

During his visit, Gutsan paid tribute to national leader Heydar Aliyev at the Alley of Honor, laying a wreath at his grave. He also visited the grave of prominent ophthalmologist and academician Zarifa Aliyeva.

During the meeting, Kamran Aliyev highlighted the importance of friendship, mutual understanding, trust and mutual assistance in Azerbaijan-Russia relations.

The sides emphasized the role of Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev and Russian President Vladimir Putin in strengthening ties between the two countries and their peoples, noting the significance of meetings and contacts between the two leaders.

Aliyev said that long-standing and effective cooperation had been established between the prosecution authorities of Azerbaijan and Russia, stressing the importance of further expanding ties in areas of mutual interest.

The parties discussed the prompt and effective processing of requests for mutual legal assistance, the extradition of individuals accused or convicted of crimes, and the exchange of experience and best practices in law enforcement.

They also highlighted the importance of the Statement of Intent on the Development of Cooperation, signed by the Prosecutor General’s Offices of Azerbaijan and Russia on April 9, 2021, in advancing collaboration in these areas.

Gutsan thanked his Azerbaijani counterpart for the warm reception and underscored the importance of the existing cooperation between the two countries’ prosecution authorities.

The meeting also covered tasks related to the implementation of the 2027-2028 Cooperation Program between the two prosecutor general’s offices, discussed in September in Kazan, as well as ways to improve international legal cooperation and prospects for further developing bilateral ties.

In recognition of his contribution to effective cooperation and strengthening relations with Azerbaijan’s prosecution authorities, Gutsan was awarded the Azerbaijani jubilee medal '100th Anniversary of the Prosecutor’s Office of Azerbaijan (1918–2018)' by Kamran Aliyev.

Following the meeting, the Russian delegation visited the History Museum of the Prosecutor’s Office of Azerbaijan.

Russian Ambassador to Azerbaijan Mikhail Yevdokimov also attended the meeting.

https://report.az/en/foreign-politics/az.heading: Azerbaijan raises missing persons issue at UN Security Council debate | Report.az
https://report.az/en/foreign-politics/az.body:
Azerbaijan has delivered a statement at the United Nations concerning people who went missing during the First Garabagh War.

Report informs that the statement was delivered by Nahida Baghirova, counselor of Azerbaijan's Permanent Mission to the United Nations, at the open debate on "Women, Peace and Security in the next quarter-century: Fulfilling the promise through implementation."

Baghirova recalled that the humanitarian consequences of armed conflicts require timely and adequate international support to address the needs and challenges faced by affected populations, including women and girls, as recognized in Security Council resolution 2474 (2019).

Despite the end of the decades-long conflict and the progress achieved in advancing the peace agenda in our region, the fate and whereabouts of thousands of Azerbaijanis who went missing in connection with the former armed conflict continue to be a pressing humanitarian concern.

Clarifying the fate of missing persons and advancing related international efforts in this regard remain matters of utmost importance to Azerbaijan.

In the post-conflict period, Azerbaijan has undertaken large-scale rehabilitation and reconstruction efforts to enable internally displaced persons to exercise their right to a safe, voluntary and dignified return to their places of origin.

Through the Great Return Program, specific measures have been introduced to empower women and girls and to ensure their meaningful participation in the recovery process.

These efforts, however, continue to be severely hampered by the persistent threat posed by landmines and other explosive remnants of war.

Since November 2020, 443 people, including women and children, have fallen victim to mine incidents and the numbers keep rising.

This grave situation underscores the urgent need for adequate international assistance to strengthen national humanitarian demining capacities and support demining efforts.

Notwithstanding these difficulties, approximately 96,000 people have already returned and are now living and working in newly rebuilt cities, towns and villages, as a result of the measures undertaken by the Government.

https://oc-media.org/moscow-forum-calls-.heading: Moscow forum calls for restoration of diplomatic ties between Georgia and Russia
https://oc-media.org/moscow-forum-calls-.body:
Participants at a forum in Moscow have proposed establishing a Russian-Georgian university, promoting the Russian language in Georgia, and restoring religious services at Georgia’s Lomisi Church, as part of a broader initiative to restore diplomatic relations between the two countries.

Georgia and Russia have had no diplomatic relations since the 2008 August War, but maintain trade and economic relations.

The forum took place on Wednesday, a week after Georgia’s government appointed First Deputy Foreign Minister Giorgi Zurabashvili as the prime minister’s special representative for relations with Russia after a yearlong vacancy. His mandate also includes the peaceful resolution of the conflict with Russia.

A survey conducted by CRRC Georgia and the National Democratic Institute (NDI) in October 2023 found that roughly a quarter of respondents supported deepening economic ties with Russia, while a similar share favored limiting them. Meanwhile, 34% said relations should remain as they were. Other polls taken around the same time indicated that a strong majority (77%) of respondents viewed Russia as Georgia’s primary political threat.

Following the forum, the Russian Interests Section at the Swiss Embassy in Georgia published a statement, emphasizing that the event’s main goal was ‘to promote the restoration of diplomatic relations between the countries’.

The document further called on Russian President Vladimir Putin and the Georgian government to support closer bilateral ties.

The event in Moscow was attended by Russian Foreign Ministry official Vasily Gavrilov (not to be confused with Russian MP Sergei Gavrilov, associated with the 2019 ‘Gavrilov’s Night’ protest), and several Georgian figures associated with pro-Russian initiatives, including Otar Romanov-Phartskhaladze, a former Georgian prosecutor general wanted by Georgian authorities and sanctioned by the US and UK.

During the forum, a foundation called ‘Unity of Russians and Georgians’ was created. Its co-founders include Phartskhaladze, Moscow-based businessperson Mamuka Pipia, and Davit Tsetskhladze, head of the Russian-Georgian Business Council.

Shortly after its establishment, a separate resolution was signed that proposed expanding the foundation’s activities, establishing a public supervisory board involving representatives of science, culture, education, and business, and preparing an initial action plan to implement the proposals.

Speaking at the forum, Pipia, who is also the international secretary of the Georgian pro-Russian Solidarity for Peace party, said the initiative aimed to help restore diplomatic relations between Russia and Georgia and move from intentions to practical steps.

In turn, Gavrilov said improving relations between Russia and Georgia was in the interests of both countries.

‘We see Georgia not as a launchpad against anyone, nor as a chessboard for risky geopolitical games, but as a place for human contacts, trade corridors, tourist routes, and energy projects. And it is encouraging that today the voices of friendship are much louder than the voices of discord’, Gavrilov said.

The Lomisi Church itself mentioned in the resolution has had its own share of controversy. It is located in Kirbali, near the Georgian-Ossetian separation line, in territory under Russian control. In November 2023, Georgian citizen Tamaz Ginturi was fatally shot there, while another Georgian citizen was captured by Russian border guards in South Ossetia, reportedly while trying to reach a disputed church.

https://georgiatoday.ge/berset-says-many.heading: Berset says ‘many elements’ of opposition party ban case could end up in Strasbourg - Georgia Today
https://georgiatoday.ge/berset-says-many.body:
Council of Europe Secretary General Alain Berset said elements of the case seeking to ban five opposition parties in Georgia could eventually reach the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg, while warning that dissolving a political party requires strong justification and strict compliance with the principles of necessity and proportionality.

Berset made the remarks on October 27 in Strasbourg, responding to a question from British politician Nadine Peatfield during a session of the Congress of Local and Regional Authorities of the Council of Europe.

Peatfield, who leads Derby City Council, asked what concrete steps the Council of Europe was taking, beyond monitoring and dialogue, to encourage Georgia to meet its obligations as a member state, referring to the ongoing Constitutional Court proceedings concerning five pro-Western opposition parties.

“Georgia’s democratic backsliding, we call it, is indeed worrying,” Berset said.

He pointed to restrictive legislation, shrinking civic space and pressure on the opposition, saying these developments “undermine political pluralism as well as the country’s commitments deriving from its membership of the Council of Europe.”

Addressing the possible legal implications of the case, Berset said he did not want to prejudge the outcome of the ongoing proceedings.

“Without prejudging the outcome, because we should never forget that we are based on the rule of law, member states have to respect the European Convention on Human Rights, as well as the case law of the European Court of Human Rights,” he said.

“I think this means that many elements of these issues could end up in our courts,” Berset added.

He stressed that his intention was not to influence the Constitutional Court’s position, but to urge the ruling majority to uphold political pluralism.

“As we all know, the dissolution of a party requires strong justification, as well as strict respect for the principles of necessity and proportionality,” Berset said.

The Council of Europe chief also referred to his discussions with Georgian officials and the organization’s work in the country.

He said he had raised concerns about democratic backsliding during a meeting with Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze in New York in September and emphasized the importance of respecting Georgia’s commitments.

Berset also pointed to recent recommendations by the Venice Commission concerning restrictive legislation, saying dialogue should lead to tangible progress.

“The membership of the Council of Europe is not just about being a member of a club of countries. It means taking high-level commitments, based on the European Convention on Human Rights, as well as the obligation to implement the judgments of the Court,” he said.

Berset said he continued to meet regularly with Georgian government representatives, noting that Georgia is one of the Council of Europe’s 46 member states.

By Aida Haidar in International on 29 October 2026

ASTANA – Kazakhstan’s Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi called for stronger political dialogue and closer trade and transport ties among Turkic states at an Oct. 29 meeting ahead of the 13th Summit of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS), the ministry’s press service reported.

Kazakhstan’s Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi. Photo credit: gov.kz

President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev arrived in Ankara on Oct. 28 for an official visit to Türkiye and is scheduled to attend the summit, Akorda reported.

The ministerial meeting focused on cooperation within the organization and current international and regional issues.

Tileuberdi emphasized the importance of strengthening unity and solidarity among Turkic states, deepening political dialogue and expanding trade, economic, transport and logistics links across the organization. He also highlighted the outcomes of the informal OTS summit held on May 15 in Turkistan under the theme Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development.

According to the ministry, Tileuberdi said the meeting had given new impetus to the organization’s digital agenda and laid the groundwork for deeper cooperation in artificial intelligence, innovation and advanced technologies.

At the end of the ministerial meeting, participants adopted documents to develop and expand the activities of Turkic organizations. They also reviewed and approved draft final documents for the 13th OTS summit.

By Staff report in Central Asia on 29 October 2026

ASTANA – Parliamentarians from five Central Asian countries discussed regional security, economic integration and digital cooperation at the fourth Inter-Parliamentary Forum of Central Asian States in Dushanbe on Oct. 29, Kazinform reported. The forum brought together lawmakers from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.

Kazakhstan’s delegation was led by Kurultai Chairman Aibek Dadebay. Participants discussed Kazakhstan’s political reforms and recent presidential initiatives, which the delegation said could create new development opportunities across the region.

The Kazakh lawmakers also emphasized parliament’s role in maintaining regional peace and security through timely legislation. Discussions addressed the continued importance of Central Asia’s nuclear-weapon-free zone and the proposed establishment of an International Agency for Biological Security.

The Kazakh delegation proposed exchanging legislative practices in e-commerce, digital customs administration, investment, transport and industrial cooperation to remove regulatory barriers and create a more integrated regional business environment. The initiative was linked to Kazakhstan’s goal of increasing intra-regional trade to $20 billion.

Participants also discussed strengthening water and climate security, with the Kazakh delegation stressing the importance of adopting a framework convention on water use.

Digital cooperation featured prominently, including proposals to strengthen educational ties and provide legislative support for Kazakhstan’s initiative to develop a Central Asian partnership program on artificial intelligence.

The delegation also proposed parliamentary support for volunteer initiatives and suggested establishing an annual Central Asian Week of Environmental Responsibility. The discussions underscored the role of regional cooperation in addressing shared challenges, including security, water management, environmental protection and the development of emerging technologies.

The forum concluded with the adoption of the Dushanbe Declaration.

President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan is scheduled to meet Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev on Thursday ahead of the 13th Organization of Turkic States (OTS) summit in Ankara.

Mirziyoyev arrived at Ankara Airport alongside his wife, Ziroat Mirziyoyeva, where they were welcomed by Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz.

The Uzbek leader's visit comes as Türkiye and Uzbekistan seek to deepen economic cooperation, with both countries aiming to increase bilateral trade to $5 billion.

Trade between the two countries reached $3.1 billion in 2025, while Ankara and Tashkent are working to expand joint investments, industrial production and access to third-country markets.

The 13th OTS summit, hosted by Erdoğan on Oct. 29-30, is expected to bring together leaders from the organization's five member states and senior representatives from three observer countries.

Alongside Erdoğan and Mirziyoyev, Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov are expected to attend the summit.

The Ankara summit will also offer member states an opportunity to review progress on connectivity, investment and digital transformation while identifying priorities for future cooperation.

For OTS countries, deeper economic integration will increasingly depend not only on expanding trade volumes but also on connecting businesses, strengthening industrial partnerships and improving regional supply chains.

Uzbekistan's total foreign trade reached $81.2 billion in 2025, comprising $33.8 billion in exports and $47.4 billion in imports.

Kazakhstan and Türkiye remained among Uzbekistan's major trading partners, with bilateral trade reaching $5 billion and $3 billion, respectively. Together, the two countries accounted for nearly 10% of Uzbekistan's total foreign trade.
