https://www.novinite.com/articles/241350.heading: PM Radev Says Bulgaria Was Ready to Deploy Jets Against the Black Sea Drones - Novinite.com - Sofia News Agency
https://www.novinite.com/articles/241350.body:
Prime Minister Rumen Radev said Bulgaria was ready to deploy L-39 military aircraft against drones that attacked a commercial vessel in the Black Sea if the unmanned aerial vehicles had entered the country's territorial waters, adding that a French patrol aircraft had detected them at least 30 minutes before the strike.

The Bulgarian Air Force had L-39 aircraft stationed in Balchik on standby for a possible response, Radev said as he discussed the recent Black Sea incidents and Bulgaria's ability to counter such threats.

Radev said authorities had obtained video footage of the attack and were examining it in cooperation with allied intelligence services. Forensic analyses are also underway to establish where the drones originated.

We have video footage, which we have shared with our allies. Every possible analysis is currently being conducted. I expect that we will finally have clear evidence as to where these drones came from, Radev said.

The prime minister added that the footage would be released publicly as soon as possible, but stressed that he could not yet identify those responsible for the attack.

We do not yet know where the drone originated. I have shared my logical assumptions with you, but I do not wish to jump to conclusions. I imagine you have seen discussions on social media, where all sorts of theories are circulating - suggesting, for instance, that the drone could belong to any of four or five different countries. However, such claims are not to be taken seriously. We intend to conduct a thorough and credible expert assessment in collaboration with our allies, Radev said.

He described the coordination between the Bulgarian Armed Forces and allied aircraft conducting patrols over the Black Sea, saying a French reconnaissance plane had spotted the drones in time to warn the targeted ship's crew.

We have been in constant communication with NATO, requesting assistance. As you know, there are already aircraft on patrol, including American ones. In fact, the French patrol aircraft spotted the drones at least half an hour before the strike; it detected them and even provided information on their trajectory. This gave the crew of the targeted ship the opportunity to take all necessary evacuation measures, the prime minister said.

Radev said allied forces and the Bulgarian military were exchanging information in real time. He reiterated that Bulgaria had been prepared to respond militarily if the drones had entered its territorial waters.

We were prepared to scramble L-39 aircraft based in Balchik and use their weaponry against these drones, had they entered our territorial waters. But it didn't come to that, he said.

However, Radev warned that Bulgaria's response options were subject to legal and practical restrictions. International law prevents the country from taking military action outside its own territorial waters, while weather, available equipment, and surveillance capabilities also limit its ability to detect and respond to threats in the exclusive economic zone.

Even if we possess the means to intervene, we cannot, from a strictly legal standpoint, take action outside our own territorial zones. We cannot do so, as it would constitute a violation of international law. Furthermore, there are various limitations regarding the capabilities at our disposal for surveillance, reconnaissance, and the detection of threats within the Exclusive Economic Zone, Radev said.

He also pointed to Bulgaria's limited naval capacity, which prevents it from maintaining a permanent presence across the entire zone.

Moreover, we are dependent on weather conditions. It is not always possible to fly, nor is it always possible to take action. Our fleet is limited in both number and capabilities. We are unable to maintain a continuous watch across the entire Exclusive Economic Zone, the prime minister said.

Radev confirmed that he had discussed the need for further allied support with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte.

We are waiting. I have also raised this issue with Mark Rutte. You can see that the quantities of weaponry available to NATO also have their limits. They are stretched from the Baltic Sea, across the land, to the Black Sea. So, everything that can be done is being done, he said.

Bulgaria has also pursued diplomatic action at the highest international level, including through the United Nations, NATO, and European institutions, Radev said. He argued that military measures and allied assistance could reduce risks but would not ensure that attacks on ships stopped.

From this point on, there is only one solution to ensure that these attacks finally come to an end: a ceasefire, sitting down at the negotiating table, and beginning talks. Until that happens, there is no guarantee regarding what can be done, Radev said.

He said the European Union and NATO should support diplomatic initiatives aimed at ending hostilities, citing efforts to open talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, including those by Finnish President Alexander Stubb and the Norwegian prime minister.

The only 100% guarantee is a ceasefire and the political will for dialogue. I believe the European Union and NATO should engage in these efforts, Radev said.

The prime minister also pledged formal diplomatic action if expert assessments establish the drones' origin and responsibility for the attack.

If the origin of these drones is proven, the Minister of Foreign Affairs will immediately summon the relevant ambassador to deliver a note of protest, Radev said.

Three drones struck a vessel 16 nautical miles off Cape Kaliakra, and its crew was rescued. The incident involved the merchant ship CONTSHIP JET, which was hit on October 28 about 16 nautical miles from the cape. Although the crew survived, the vessel was reported to have sunk the following day.

The attack has renewed concerns about the safety of commercial shipping in the Black Sea and the risks to trade routes close to Bulgarian territorial waters.

The European Commission also reacted to the attacks on civilian vessels, calling them an unacceptable escalation that threatens EU interests, maritime transport, and supply chains. Brussels expressed solidarity with Bulgaria and Romania, warning that the consequences of the war in Ukraine continued to pose serious security risks in the Black Sea region.

Radev defended Bulgaria's decision not to identify a country as responsible for the drone attacks before conclusive evidence was available. He cited Romania, which he said had blamed Russia but subsequently experienced another incident.

Bulgaria did not make definitive accusations against any country because we lacked concrete evidence at the time. Romania stated that the aggressor and the source of these drones was Russia. Yet, this failed to protect them. The very next day, drones sank a ship—within their own territorial waters, no less. Do you see the difference? Radev said.

He criticized Bulgarian politicians calling for the immediate naming of a suspected perpetrator, arguing that public accusations would not prevent further attacks.

I want to address all our politicians who so convincingly propagate the notion that if we speak out and declare, 'You, Russia, are the source of the attack', if we shake our finger at them, that will protect us. It cannot protect us. Look at what happened in Romania: the very next day, a ship was struck and sunk. And I repeat - this did not happen in the exclusive economic zone, but in territorial waters, the prime minister said.

Radev also commented on a Central Election Commission (CEC) decision concerning a complaint against him over his support for Iliyana Yotova's candidacy, which had been expressed through the government press office.

He said the Council of Ministers would comply with the commission's decision, while noting that the final course of action would depend on the court because the ruling had been appealed.

The Council of Ministers will comply with the decision of the Central Election Commission. Whatever the Bulgarian court decides, that is what we will do, Radev said.

https://cphpost.dk/2026-10-29/general/da.heading: Danish and Norwegian prime ministers discuss rift over joint Norway–Finland call to Putin - The Copenhagen Post
https://cphpost.dk/2026-10-29/general/da.body:
Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre says he had a "good conversation" with Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen on Wednesday after she criticised his joint phone call with Finnish President Alexander Stubb to Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"Mette Frederiksen is a close partner for me politically and personally," Støre told Dagens Næringsliv, according to Norwegian news agency NTB.

"We had a good conversation on the phone yesterday and agreed that we view that conversation differently," he said, referring to Tuesday’s 90-minute call with Putin.

Frederiksen had questioned the initiative, saying it had not been coordinated with other European partners.

"I am very sceptical of this Norwegian and Finnish initiative. It is not coordinated with the rest of us," she told TV 2 during a Nordic Council meeting in Finland.

"I think we should keep Europe together rather than go it alone."

The Danish prime minister said she did not know what Norway and Finland believed the call could achieve. She argued that European countries had previously stressed the importance of a united approach when individual leaders pursued contacts with Russia.

Responding to the criticism on Tuesday, Støre said all allies had been informed before the call.

Frederiksen declined to comment further when asked about the matter later that day at Amalienborg in Copenhagen.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, meanwhile, welcomed Norway and Finland’s involvement, writing on X that he was "grateful" for their "active support for our diplomacy and joint peace efforts".

https://www.thelocal.fr/20261029/french-.heading: French shooting suspect deliberately targeted Muslims and Africans, says prosecutor
https://www.thelocal.fr/20261029/french-.body:
A man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs last week, killing one person and wounding seven including a child, has admitted to "targeting individuals who appeared to be Muslim or African," prosecutors said on Thursday.

On Friday, the 39-year-old suspect, identified as Kévin T., opened fire with a submachine gun from a moving vehicle as he drove through the towns of Trappes and La Verriere, west of Paris. He was arrested later that day with tear-gas grenades in his car.

Earlier this week the suspect had said he did not "dispute the material facts", but contested "the racist nature of his crimes".

On Thursday, national terrorism prosecutor Olivier Christen told a news conference that Kévin T. now claims he chose the location for his actions because it was "a hotbed for Islamists".

He has since been held in police custody and was set to appear before a judge later on Thursday, Christen said.

Authorities initially said five people, including an 11-year-old child, had been wounded in the attack, but later revised the toll to seven injured.

Of the people seriously injured in the attack, "three of the victims remain hospitalised as I speak, and one of them is still in life-threatening condition," Christen said.

Kévin T. rejected suggestions he had "intended to kill children," but that he "might have been mistaken due to their size."

Nevertheless, he stated that he "feels no regret," Christen said.

The prosecutor noted the "very high level of preparation" behind the attack, including the acquisition in September of "several weapon components designed to enhance the tactical effectiveness of a Sten submachine gun, as well as a police armband and handcuffs."

Kévin T. denied any "terrorist intent," viewing his actions as "legitimate," the prosecutor said.

The opening of a judicial investigation by the office of the national anti-terrorism prosecutor (PNAT) allows a judge to take charge of the case, specifically regarding charges of "murder and attempted murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise".

A search of the suspect's home had uncovered "weapons or weapon components, specifically a magazine, two pairs of brass knuckles, a steel bayonet, and a silencer," Christen said.

Also found were several "books, including a Quran, a Bible, and Adolf Hitler's Mein Kampf", as well as stickers celebrating the far-right Rassemblement National (RN) party.

Christen said the stickers bore slogans such as "Long live France, RN, proud to be French", but they were not produced by Le Pen's party.

Kévin T. had told investigators that "he designed the stickers found in his home himself, and then ordered them to be manufactured via Amazon more than a year ago."

The suspect had said that "he is neither a member of nor a sympathiser with any political party", Christen said.

The attack triggered a number of demonstrations around France against the normalisation of racist hatred.

Authorities on Thursday banned a far-right, radical-leaning symposium on "remigration" - scheduled for Saturday in the suburbs of Paris - and a demonstration planned for Sunday in the capital.

The organisers said that they would appeal against the ban.

Outgoing European Chief Prosecutor Laura Codruța Kövesi has described the dispute over renewing prosecutors’ mandates in Greece as the clearest attempt to intimidate the European Public Prosecutor’s Office during her seven-year tenure.

Speaking in an interview with Politico, Kövesi said: “The most blatant attempt to intimidate EPPO happened in Greece, where we had this issue with the renewal of the European delegated prosecutors.”

Her remarks concern a confrontation over the terms of prosecutors handling sensitive investigations, including alleged fraud involving EU agricultural subsidies administered through Greece’s OPEKEPE payments agency.

Kövesi rejected accusations that the office’s investigations followed a political timetable. She argued that approaching elections could not justify suspending prosecutors’ work and said attention should focus on whether agricultural funding reached genuine farmers.

She also defended the request to lift the immunity of 11 Greek MPs, explaining that removing parliamentary protection allows investigators to gather evidence and does not constitute a finding of guilt.

In July, EPPO announced indictments against 22 defendants, including four serving MPs, while dismissing allegations against seven other serving lawmakers. Those indicted remain presumed innocent.

The Greece-related criticism formed part of a broader warning about EPPO’s future. Kövesi said inadequate funding, delayed reforms and bureaucratic obstacles risked weakening the office’s ability to investigate crimes involving EU money.

The dispute over Greek prosecutors’ appointments had already prompted a formal intervention. In May, EPPO said it had notified the European Commission that Greece’s Supreme Judicial Council had refused to recognise the full effect of its decision to renew three delegated prosecutors’ mandates for five years.

It also raised concerns about legislative changes affecting investigations involving MPs.

EPPO is the EU’s independent prosecution office responsible for crimes against its financial interests. Kövesi’s successor, German prosecutor Andrés Ritter, takes office on November 1. He has served as deputy European chief prosecutor since November 2020.

https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/gre.heading: EXCLUSIVE: Greek PM calls Turkey-Libya maritime deal 'void;' calls for global truce after Black Sea attacks | Reuters
https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/gre.body:
Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said on Thursday that the recently signed maritime deal between Libya's eastern parliament and Turkey was "blatantly illegal, null and void," adding that it "completely disregards the geography."

Mitsotakis, speaking to Reuters as Greece ends its UN Security Council presidency, also called for an urgent "international truce" to protect shipping in the Black Sea after the sinking of a Greek-owned container vessel on Wednesday.

Libya's eastern parliament last week approved a maritime boundaries deal with Turkey, drawing condemnation from Athens, but also Egypt, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates, as a threat to regional security and international legal order.

"It completely disregards the geography, the reality that there are Greek islands -- they seem to completely disappear in the thinking of Turkey and Libya," Mitsotakis said, accusing them of attempting to create a "fait accompli" that ignores the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.

Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan has said that reactions from the EU and others to the approval of the agreement, originally agreed in 2019, had no legitimate basis, defending Ankara's policy in the eastern Mediterranean.

Since the 2019 Libya-Turkey deal, Greece has awarded a license to a consortium led by Chevron to look for gas off the island of Crete and has sought a separate agreement with Libya on demarcating their maritime zones.

Mitsotakis assured "there's no risk that these explorations will be in any way challenged."

Referring to Libya and Greece as "natural neighbors," Mitsotakis urged the African country to negotiate directly with Athens and take the discussions "very, very seriously."

Mitsotakis, 58, spoke to Reuters after chairing a council debate on maritime security, only hours after a Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria in the latest strike on ships in the western Black Sea this month.

Greek-operated ships are among the world's largest fleets of tankers and are pivotal for trade across the Black Sea region, whose waters are shared by Bulgaria, Georgia, Romania and Turkey, as well as warring Russia and Ukraine, which Moscow invaded in February 2022.

"We do need some sort of international truce when it comes to the freedom of navigation," said Mitsotakis, adding that it was of "utmost priority" to allow for exports of grain from the region into the world through the Black Sea.

"Greek shipowners would be the first to resume trading in the Black Sea, also from Ukraine, assuming a safe passage is guaranteed," he said, stressing the rising costs of shipping as chartering and insurance expenses have "gone through the roof."

It was not immediately clear who had carried out the attack, which added to growing concerns about the impact of Russia's war in Ukraine on commercial shipping in the area.

Mitsotakis said that Ukraine was financially dependent on exports of its products: "They had a bumper harvest, but the grain is now sitting in silos, in danger of rotting."

"Unfortunately, for the moment, Russia doesn't seem to be interested in engaging in a substantive discussion," he said.

Mitsotakis also called on the European Union to bolster its naval mission to protect shipping in the Red Sea called Aspides, which was launched in 2024 to protect from attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis.

"My argument is simple: the European Union has an interest in having a concrete presence with hard assets in this part of the world, and we need more countries to participate in Aspides," Mitsotakis told Reuters.

He said Greece, Italy and France have deployed "assets" as part of the mission and that was "clearly not enough." Diplomats told Reuters as of late September there were six warships operating as part of the operation.

The Houthis said this week they had attacked Saudi military aircraft and repelled an advance by Saudi-backed forces near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, an important Red Sea shipping route.

"If we really want to send the message also to the Gulf countries that we take their security seriously, but we also protect the critical arteries and waterways that are absolutely indispensable for European trade, we should be willing to deploy more assets to this part of the world," Mitsotakis said.

Asked about US President Donald Trump's move earlier this month to lift sanctions on Russian diesel exports, Mitsotakis reaffirmed Greek support for sanctions on Moscow.

"We believe that we need to put economic pressure and impose more financial pain on Russia to send a very clear signal that as long as they prolong this war, they will suffer very specific economic consequences," he said.

https://eng.lsm.lv/article/society/defen.heading: Latvian border guards given clearer rights to use force and weapons / Article
https://eng.lsm.lv/article/society/defen.body:
Latvia's parliament, the Saeima, on October 29 adopted amendments to the State Border Guard Law and the Criminal Procedure Law intended to give border guards clearer rights to act and to better protect border infrastructure from hybrid attacks.

The changes determine the right of border guards to use physical force, special fighting techniques, weapons and dogs to repel an attack on an individual or state border infrastructure facility.

The amendments also determine the possibility of using a weapon without warning if giving a warning is not possible in a specific situation.

Until now, the law did not specifically provide for such rights for border guards to repel an attack.

"Currently, a hybrid war is taking place at the external border of our country. The inviolability of the state border and the protection of infrastructure are an essential part of Latvia's territorial integrity.

With the amendments to the law, we are strengthening the capabilities of border guards to immediately prevent violations and protect Latvia's security," said Raimonds Bergmanis (United List), the chairman of the Saeima Defence Committee responsible for the draft laws.

The changes also stipulate that if a person is injured or dies as a result of the use of a weapon, the border guard must immediately, but no later than within 24 hours, report this to the prosecutor's office.

In turn, changes to the Criminal Procedure Law stipulate that criminal offences committed by a border guard as a state official while performing duties within the framework of the enhanced border guard system operating regime will be investigated by authorized officials of the State Border Guard.

As official coalition talks get underway, the outlines of the possible distribution of posts in the next government are also beginning to emerge, according to a report on Wednesday evening by the Latvian Television programme 'Panorāma'.

Two of the candidates for ministerial posts – Normunds Staņēvičs, former chairman of the board of the Pauls Stradiņš Clinical University Hospital, and Kārlis Purgailis, an economist at Citadele Bank – could serve in the government as non-partisan professionals, taking up the posts of Minister of Health and Minister of Finance respectively.

The candidacy of cardiologist Andris Skride (United List) is also being considered for the post of Minister of Health.

Edgars Štelmahers (United List) could become Minister for Economics; the current Parliamentary Secretary at the Ministry of Justice, Viesturs Vitkovskis, is being discussed for the post of Minister for Justice; Līga Meņģelsone (United List) for the post of Minister for Welfare; the Minister of Defence could continue to be Raivis Melnis, nominated by New Unity, whilst Edgars Tavars (United List) would remain in the post of Minister for Smart Administration and Regional Development.

Edgars Putra (United List) could become Minister for Agriculture, whilst Česlavs Batņa (United List) could be nominated for the post of Minister for Education and Science.

Diplomat Edgars Skuja has been approached for the post of Minister for Foreign Affairs.

This is a provisional allocation of posts, which does not cover all ministerial posts in the new government, including those of Minister for the Interior and Minister for Transport.

As the parties seek compromises, the distribution of posts may change.

It is noteworthy that as the positions stand now, the Cabinet would be almost exclusively male.

The next round of government formation talks is scheduled for after 4 November – following the convening of the 15th Saeima.

https://www.dpa-international.com/politi.heading: Lithuania to reintroduce full conscription in 2032 | dpa international
https://www.dpa-international.com/politi.body:
The Baltic republic of Lithuania has announced plans to expand military service for young men and introduce general conscription in view of escalating tensions with neighbouring Russia.

The National Security Council of the EU and NATO member state agreed on the measure at a session in Vilnius on Thursday.

"We have decided that general conscription will be introduced starting in 2032," President Gitanas Nausėda said after the meeting. However, the parliament must still approve the plan.

In 2015, Lithuania partially reintroduced conscription, which was abolished in 2008, in response to Russia's illegal annexation of Crimea from Ukraine the previous year.

Since Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, concerns have deepened in Lithuania, which borders Russia's Baltic Sea exclave of Kaliningrad, as well as its ally Belarus.

According to Nausėda, more than 5,000 young men are currently drafted each year for nine months of basic training. This number will rise to around 7,500 with the introduction of general conscription.

Young women should continue to be able to complete military training on a voluntary basis, as before, the president said. The costs for the transition could amount to up to €120 million ($133 million), according to Nausėda.

He justified 2032 as the target date for the start of full conscription with the extent of the necessary preparations. For instance, appropriate accommodation for a larger number of conscripts must be created and instructors must be trained.

https://nltimes.nl/2026/10/29/dutch-king.heading: Dutch King receives Ukrainian president with open arms; Gov't promises more military aid | NL Times
https://nltimes.nl/2026/10/29/dutch-king.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visited King Willem-Alexander at Huis ten Bosch Palace on Wednesday. Footage shared by the president shows the King welcoming him with open arms, followed by an embrace. Before the meeting with the King, Zelenskyy met with Prime Minister Rob Jetten, who subsequently announced that the Netherlands would provide an additional €500 million in military aid to get through the coming winter.

During my meeting with King Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands, I spoke about the lives of our people under constant Russian attacks and our diplomatic efforts with partners to achieve peace.I thank His Majesty for his support and for the meeting. The Netherlands is one of… pic.twitter.com/PxUu9ulA0P

“During my meeting with King Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands, I spoke about the lives of our people under constant Russian attacks and our diplomatic efforts with partners to achieve peace,” Zelenskyy said on X. “I thank His Majesty for his support and for the meeting. The Netherlands is one of Ukraine’s closest and most reliable partners. We value all the assistance provided. It is important that we can be confident that support for our people will continue.”

The new “winter package” includes items like air defense weapons and drones, Jetten said during a press conference with Zelenskyy. Jetten condemned Russia’s intensification of attacks on civilian targets and critical infrastructure in Ukraine, particularly as the winter months approach. “Now more than ever, is the time to press ahead.”

In his statement, Zelenskyy said that he was “very grateful” for the newly announced support, noting that it was “necessary for the winter.” Ukraine and its allies fear that, much like last winter, Russia intends to leave the country in darkness and the cold—a concern compounded by the fact that Ukraine is frequently running low on the missiles needed to intercept and neutralize Russian projectiles.

While Zelenskyy is in The Hague, Minister for Foreign Trade Sjoerd Sjoerdsma is in Kyiv, Jetten said. In Kyiv, Sjoerdsma discussed the previously pledged 1.2 billion in non-military aid for Ukraine—funds earmarked for humanitarian assistance and reconstruction.

Jetten called for other allies of Ukraine to step up their support. To date, the Netherlands and a handful of other Northern and Western European nations have provided the lion's share of the aid.

Since the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the Netherlands has already provided support packages to Ukraine worth many billions—including ammunition for F-16s, drones, and air defense weaponry. This new package will be funded from the more than €3 billion that the cabinet had allocated for Ukraine this year.

https://www.dutchnews.nl/2026/10/china-c.heading: China controls key materials for Dutch chips, defence and energy - DutchNews.nl
https://www.dutchnews.nl/2026/10/china-c.body:
The Netherlands is heavily dependent on China for seven of the eight raw materials most critical to its economy, according to new research by national statistics office CBS.

The CBS ranked more than 30 materials on the EU’s official list of critical raw materials by three measures: their economic importance to the Netherlands, the risk of supply disruption and the expected growth in demand.

Gallium was top, followed by rare earth metals, germanium, graphite, lithium, cobalt, niobium and silicon metal.

All of those except niobium are mainly processed in China before they’re sent to the Netherlands, either as materials or part of finished products. China handles at least 74% of global processing for each of the seven. The figure is 99% for gallium, 94% for graphite and 84% for rare earths. For niobium, the Netherlands depends mainly on Brazil.

The materials are vital to the semiconductor industry, defence and the energy transition, the CBS said. Demand is growing because of AI, electric cars, faster networks and new defence systems.

Gallium ranks highest because China controls almost all of the world’s production and uses strict export restrictions as political leverage, the CBS said. The metal is also the basis for microchips and other high-tech products made by large companies.

In 2025, the Netherlands imported €17.2 billion worth of critical raw materials from outside the EU, plus €123.9 billion worth of products that contain them – almost a third of the value of all imports from outside the EU.

https://notesfrompoland.com/2026/10/29/p.heading: Polish opposition leader sparks controversy with speech on potential EU exit talks | Notes From Poland
https://notesfrompoland.com/2026/10/29/p.body:
Jarosław Kaczyński, the leader of Poland’s largest opposition party, has sparked controversy by appearing to suggest that Poland and some other allied European Union member states could launch the process of leaving the EU if they fail in efforts to reform it.

His remarks were condemned by Prime Minister Donald Tusk and other figures from the pro-EU ruling coalition, who have long accused Kaczyński and his national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party of seeking “Polexit” from the EU.

However, Kaczyński responded by accusing Tusk of misrepresenting his words, insisting that he wants Poland to reform the EU rather than leave it.

The comments in question came in an hour-long speech by Kaczyński at the Krynica Forum, an annual conference bringing together leaders from politics, business and civil society, which he used to outline his vision for sweeping reforms of the EU.

Repeating his longstanding criticism of Brussels, Kaczyński warned that there had been a 'consistent drive to transform the EU into a centralised state' with too much power over national governments. He also called the European Parliament in its current form a 'parody'.

But soon, said Kaczyński, 'a window of opportunity' for reform may appear because 'completely different governments could emerge' in Poland, France, and Spain, all of which will hold elections within the year.

PiS has previously enjoyed close relations with Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally (RN) party in France and the nationalist Vox party of Santiago Abascal in Spain.

Kaczyński suggested that Poland, if led by PiS, could work with other like-minded EU governments to push for reform of the bloc by influencing public opinion, identifying breaches of EU treaties, creating a blocking minority in the European Council, and trying to change the EU’s treaties.

However, the PiS leader then warned that, 'if [those] approaches fail to yield results, the states that want change could conclude a new treaty with the elements we are seeking, but with a delayed entry into force'.

Kaczyński then noted that the EU treaties 'include provisions specifying the terms under which a state may withdraw from the EU.' This all begins with negotiations. And simply begin these negotiations.

'It is a tough approach, a risky one, but the situation is so dire that it is worth employing such a method if all others fail to yield results,' he added.

The remarks immediately prompted condemnation from figures in Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right. They accused Kaczyński of effectively calling for Polexit – something they have long claimed he wants, even though PiS has not explicitly called for it before.

'Jarosław Kaczyński has just announced that Poland should begin negotiations on the terms of its withdrawal from the EU,' wrote Tusk himself on X. 'This is, among other things, what the current struggle in Poland is about – a tough struggle. I do not intend to lose it.'

'So they do want Polexit after all,' wrote foreign minister Radosław Sikorski. 'Customs borders with Germany, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, and Lithuania...An end to subsidies for farmers and investments...And they swore on their lives that they’d never do that.'

In the near future, Poland will transfer two Soviet-made MiG-29 fighter jets, as well as ammunition, to Ukraine.

This was announced by Darius Lukowski, director of the Department of Strategy and Defense Planning at the Polish Ministry of National Defense, according to Rzeczpospolita.

It is important to understand that the aircraft and ammunition will be part of a new Polish aid package worth approximately 50 million euros.

Journalists asked Lukowski when Ukraine would actually receive the fighter jets.

“In the near future. The decision has been made, and these two MiG-29s will be transferred,” the official emphasized.

As the media has discovered, one of the aircraft has already reached the end of its service life, while the second is still airworthy.

In addition, the aid package will include: 155-mm and 152-mm artillery ammunition; 20 rounds of 102-mm ammunition for the six-barrel cannons on F-16 fighter jets, as well as missiles for the “Perun” man-portable air defense systems.

The Polish Ministry of National Defense also added that the aid will include, in particular, the transfer of equipment that the Polish military is decommissioning at the end of its service life.

Although this equipment will no longer be used in Poland, it may still be useful to Ukraine.

At the same time, the Polish Ministry of Defense did not disclose exactly which weapons and equipment would be included in the new aid package, citing the confidential nature of the information.

https://www.stripes.com/theaters/europe/.heading: Poland calls security meeting on permanent US military base | Stars and Stripes
https://www.stripes.com/theaters/europe/.body:
Polish President Karol Nawrocki, left, walks with U.S. President Donald Trump to a meeting in the Oval Office in Washington, D.C., on Sept. 3, 2025. Nawrocki has called a national security meeting next week to discuss efforts aimed at attracting a new permanent U.S. military base in Poland. (Evan Vucci/AP)

Poland’s president has called a meeting with senior national security officials next week to discuss efforts aimed at attracting a new permanent U.S. military base in the country.

President Karol Nawrocki will hold the closed-door meeting Tuesday in Warsaw, his National Security Bureau announced this week.

The meeting comes as Polish officials prepare proposals for the Pentagon detailing basing options in the country. Warsaw has said it is prepared to pay for a new base, which could cost between $3 billion and $4 billion.

If the two countries agree on the terms, that could mean 5,000 more troops residing in Poland on a permanent basis. Most U.S. troops currently assigned there are on temporary rotational missions.

Polish officials have said they hope to eventually have a mix of 10,000 rotational troops and 5,000 permanent ones.

Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said Wednesday that the proposed American installation would be a central topic of Tuesday’s meeting.

Poland has identified four potential locations for a base, all in the western part of the country. The selected cities are Wroclaw, Poznan, Bydgoszcz and Szczecin, Kosiniak-Kamysz said in an interview last week with the Polish news outlet WNP.

U.S. soldiers listen to a Polish trainer at Bemowo Piskie Training Area, Poland, May 22, 2026. The president of Poland, Karol Nawrocki, will hold a closed-door meeting next week for talks about the country’s bid to obtain another permanent U.S. base. (Emilie Lenglain/U.S. Army)

Plans for a new base in Poland have been gaining momentum. While the Pentagon is currently wrapping up a force posture review that could include troop reductions in Europe, Poland has been a priority for the U.S. military.

In September, President Donald Trump said Washington and Warsaw are making progress toward a new basing deal.

“If this happens, the location will be announced very soon,” Trump said on Truth Social. “This will be a historic step for our Great U.S./Polish Alliance.”

Also in September, a U.S. delegation visited Poland to inspect possible locations for a permanent American base.

While the U.S. Army already has a small permanent base in Poznan, most of the military sites used by American troops in Poland are austere locations designed to serve rotational contingents.

Establishing a major permanent base would entail building family housing, schools and the other amenities typically required to support troops and their families.

John Vandiver covers U.S. military activities across Europe and Africa. Based in Stuttgart, Germany, he previously worked for newspapers in New Jersey, North Carolina and Maryland. He is a graduate of the University of Delaware.

https://www.romania-insider.com/society/.heading: Ukrainian citizen suspected of sabotaging Romanian industrial platform arrested in Poland
https://www.romania-insider.com/society/.body:
Ukrainian citizen Artem S., suspected of participating in the arson of the Carfil industrial platform in Romania, has been placed in pre-trial detention for seven days, the Warsaw District Prosecutor’s Office announced on Wednesday, October 28.

The man was wanted under a European Arrest Warrant issued by the Romanian authorities. The arrest took place on Monday, October 26, but the announcement was made by the Warsaw authorities two days later.

“By its decision of October 28, 2026, the Warsaw District Court imposed a preventive measure in the form of temporary detention for a period of seven days on Artem S., who is wanted by the Romanian authorities under a European Arrest Warrant. Artem S. did not consent to extradition to Romania and has a lawyer of his choice,” the prosecutor’s office announced on X.

Polish broadcaster RMF 24 claimed that Artem S. was tasked with identifying the target to be set on fire in Romania and ensuring payment for the operation. He was detained in an apartment in Warsaw’s Ursus district.

Two Belarusian suspects were detained in Germany while allegedly preparing similar acts. The suspects allegedly planned to set fire to a building or critical infrastructure in the Nuremberg area.

Artem S. informed the Polish authorities that he did not agree to be handed over to Romania and requested a lawyer, according to the Warsaw Regional Prosecutor’s Office.

Romania is requesting the extradition of all three suspected saboteurs.

On Monday, Romanian prosecutors within DIICOT announced that they had documented the criminal activities of two Belarusian citizens and a Ukrainian citizen, residents of EU member states, who were involved in a suspicious fire that engulfed the premises of several companies in Brașov County. DIICOT stated that the two Belarusian citizens had been arrested in Germany, while the Ukrainian had been “located” in Poland.

The Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) and Romanian prosecutors said that the three were part of a sabotage network coordinated from Russia. SRI added that the network’s targets extended beyond Romania’s borders, including state-owned and private arms factories, as well as other sites of military and industrial importance.

President Nicușor Dan condemned “in the strongest terms” any Russian involvement in sabotage on Romanian territory.

Russia has repeatedly denied accusations by Germany and other countries that it has carried out acts of sabotage. It also denied planning or coordinating the September 14 fire at the Carfil industrial platform in Brașov, central Romania.

https://apnews.com/article/spain-train-c.heading: Spain reckons with another deadly train crash as election nears | AP News
https://apnews.com/article/spain-train-c.body:
Spain’s second high-speed rail disaster this year, in which one train struck another from behind, killing 69 people, has raised fresh concerns about the safety of the country’s rail network ahead of a national election.

Search teams with sniffer dogs continued to look for victims on Thursday, a day after the collision in central Spain. Cranes shifted the carriages as police and soldiers picked through the wreckage strewn down the gravel slope where at least three train carriages were tossed by the impact.

One more body was found overnight, taking the death toll to 69, according to the regional leader of Castilla La Mancha, Emiliano García-Page. He added that 50 people remained hospitalized, while officials worked with family members to identify the dead.

“As a society, we have once again suffered a devastating blow, and we must adopt measures so that this doesn’t happen again,” Spain’s King Felipe VI said after visiting injured passengers at a hospital in Toledo.

Spain’s government declared three days of mourning starting Thursday. A minute of silence was held at various points at noon, including with lawmakers outside the Parliament and by rail workers and union leaders in Madrid’s main train station.

https://www.nbcnews.com/world/spain/spai.heading: Protests erupt in Spain after 68 killed in deadliest train crash in decades
https://www.nbcnews.com/world/spain/spai.body:
Spain began three days of mourning Thursday after at least 68 people were killed and dozens more injured in the country’s deadliest train crash in decades. But anger is mounting about the alleged incompetence that allowed the accident to happen and protesters clashed with police overnight outside the country’s transport ministry.

Once considered one of the country’s crowning achievements, Spain’s high-speed rail network had not endured a deadly crash since it came into service over 30 years ago.

After the second train accident in less than a year, the tragedy has deepened the feeling among many that there is something broken in Spanish society. The crash follows weeks of protests.

Rising costs and a housing shortage that is pricing many Spaniards out of the housing market, have already triggered massive and sometimes deadly protests across the country, and piled the pressure on the Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.

On Wednesday, four weeks before the country goes to the polls in a national election, Sanchez visited the site in the central province of Toledo where a quiet stretch of rail lined by olive groves had been turned into a scene of devastation.

Pictures showed several carriages lying on their sides next to the tracks and others twisted at angles, their wheels sheared off. Debris was strewn around the scene of the accident in the countryside in the province of Toledo after one train crashed into another that was stationary on the line.

Hundreds of emergency workers, firefighters, police, firefighters and soldiers attended the scene to rescue survivors and recover bodies, before cranes were brought in to move parts of the damaged trains late Wednesday.

Several Americans were hurt, according to the State Department, which did not provide further details.

Jacksonville firefighter Josue Garcia-Otero was on board with seven of his family members.

“We got to safety first, then began treating other patients that were critically injured,” Garcia-Otero said in a news release issued by the Jacksonville Fire and Rescue Department. “My wife is a nurse, and she was helping too.”

Pledging an investigation and improvements to prevent a similar tragedy in future, Sánchez said it was clear that we need to reinforce the safety of our train service to rebuild the trust in our high-speed rail.”

It was “not acceptable for a country like Spain to endure two high-speed train accidents in the same year,” he said, referring to an incident in January when 46 people died after one train jumped the track and slammed into the side of another going the opposite way in the south of the country.

Both crashes involved trains operated by the state-owned RENFE company and the privately owned IRYO.

His transport minister, Óscar Puente, said that the crash was caused by what he called the “inexplicable” order from a central command center for Spain’s trains after a security system had failed.

Puente, who is facing calls to resign, said the train engineers were not to blame, but instead a security system had stopped working because of a computer malfunction, causing all trains on the line to stop at about 8:30 a.m. local time (5:30 a.m. ET).

Shortly afterwards he said central command had told the RENFE train to start running again without any speed restrictions, adding that never should have happened and it ended up colliding with the stationary IRYO train at 8:53 a.m.

Riot police used tear gas outside his transport ministry in Madrid late Wednesday after far-right protesters gathered outside and pushed against a cordon set up by officers. Some threw flares and other objects as some chanted slogans against Puente and Sánchez.

Quite what effect the accident will have on Sánchez’s political ambitions remains unclear. The prime minister called a snap election next month after his Socialist party suffered several defeats on legislation aimed at addressing the country’s housing crisis.

His minority government had put forward two decree laws aimed at protecting tenants in the rental market after nationwide protests following the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her Madrid apartment. Maricarmen Abascal, who was a wheelchair user, was eventually allowed to return but died in hospital before she could do so.

Sánchez who took power in 2018 has weathered several crises during his premiership including the Covid-19 pandemic and the global inflation rise.

But he has faced attacks from right-wing parties over his liberal migration policies and accusations of corruption against his party and his wife, which both deny, and polls show he is facing and uphill battle to win votes ahead of the election next month.

Henry Austin is a senior editor for NBC News Digital based in London.

https://www.defensenews.com/global/europ.heading: Switzerland shortlists SAMP/T, Barak MX for long-range air defense - Defense News
https://www.defensenews.com/global/europ.body:
PARIS — Switzerland narrowed down the choice of the country’s second future long-range air defense system to either Israel’s Barak MX system or the French-Italian SAMP/T NG, while also sticking to plans to buy the United States’ Patriot air-defense system.

The federal government asked the defense department to continue evaluating the Barak MX developed by Israel Aerospace Industries and the SAMP/T NG from the Eurosam joint venture between MBDA and Thales, it said on Wednesday. In addition to technical, military and weapon-related aspects, the choice takes into account foreign-policy and economic-policy considerations, the federal council said.

Switzerland said in May it would evaluate long-range air-defense systems from manufacturers in Germany, France, Israel and South Korea, with a preference for a system produced in Europe, after delivery of the Patriot system was delayed by several years.

“The Federal Council considers it necessary to strengthen the country’s air defense to address the deteriorating geopolitical situation,” the government said. “Long-range ground-to-air defense systems are indispensable for this purpose, with an adequate supply of ammunition.”

The long-range systems, combined with short-range and medium-range systems as well as fighter aircraft, will allow Switzerland to counter attacks from a distance, including ballistic missiles, the government said.

“It is important that Switzerland can quickly equip itself, in addition to the Patriot, with a second system that meets its needs in light of the threat, allows to expand the protected area, and reduces dependence on a single supplier or a single supply chain,” the council said.

The council said it considered bids from four manufacturers in France, Israel and South Korea.

While the U.S. is prioritizing Patriot delivery to countries that have supplied their own systems to Ukraine, abandoning the Patriot purchase without a replacement system is not an option in the current situation, according to the government. It said discussions with the U.S. on delivery of Patriot systems are continuing.

Parliament is scheduled to review a government proposal for an additional 24 billion Swiss francs (US$30 billion) in defense and security spending during its winter session, including 6 billion francs to finance the second long-range air-defense system and a portion of the additional costs for Patriot, the federal council said.

Once the evaluations are complete and parliament has decided on funding for the armed forces, which is expected in early 2027, the council will decide on additional appropriation for the Patriot system and the next steps for the second long-range air-defense system, it said.

Switzerland previously agreed to buy Diehl Defence’s IRIS-T SLM system for medium-range air defense and the Oerlikon Skynex short-range system from Rheinmetall.

https://www.dawn.com/news/2040586.heading: Iran keeps diplomacy open as US weighs fresh strikes - World - DAWN.COM
https://www.dawn.com/news/2040586.body:
• Araghchi says ‘in contact’ with mediators after Qatar presents new seven-day plan to end war• US warns Gulf states of possible ‘short, intense’ Iran war after midterms, reports WSJ

TEHRAN: Iran’s foreign minister said on Wednesday that Teh­ran remained in close contact with mediators over ways to impl­e­ment its proposal to end the Middle East war, even as Iranian officials rejected ideas put forward by Qatar for a new agreement.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran continued to give diplomacy a chance to succeed and raised the possibility of the seven-day plan proposed by Tehran being completed in less than a week if implemented.

Araghchi’s remarks came as Qatari mediators have presented Iran with a new draft deal to end the war with the US and Israel, an official briefed on the negotiations said.

The official briefed on the negotiations, who is not from Iran, said a new draft peace proposal for the eight-month-old conflict was presented on Sunday and was being considered by Tehran, with a response expected by the end of the week.

Qatar, along with Pakistan, has led mediation to end the war, which has disrupted global shipping and oil supplies and recently spread to Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

The proposal presented by Qatar sets a seven-day timeline addressing both Tehran’s and Washington’s concerns, laying out daily confidence-building steps that each side must take, the official briefed on the negotiations said. The timeline could begin early next week and several countries would act as guarantors of the deal, the official added.

The draft discussed in Tehran on Sunday was different from that proposal, the official briefed on the negotiations said, though the details of the latest plan were not immediately clear. The official had previously told Reuters that the Qatari mediators had coordinated with Washington before going to Tehran.

On Friday, US President Donald Trump repeated threats to strike Iran again, while Iranian security officials told Reuters Tehran had drawn up detailed plans to attack Gulf undersea cables if the US and Israel resumed attacks.

Meanwhile, the US has told several Gulf Arab countries to prepare for a “short, intense military campaign” against Iran after the Nov 3 midterm elections, Anadolu reported, citing The Wall Street Journal.

The messages, conveyed through diplomatic and military channels, are among growing signs that the US and Israel are preparing a new round of heavy combat operations to wea­ken Iran and push it toward negotiations, according to the report.

Washington is moving a Patriot missile defence system from Texas to the region and has moved troops from bases where they were vulnerable, while US forces are restocking munitions and preparing bombers and fighter jets for strikes, the newspaper said, citing officials.

An additional aircraft carrier strike group and a Marine expeditionary unit are expected to join roughly 20 US warships in the Middle East next month, it added.

US President Donald Trump has not made a final decision, but is leaning toward a “large postelection attack” that could target Iranian infrastructure and nuclear sites, the report said, citing people familiar with his thinking.

The US military has spent over $47 billion so far to prosecute the war in Iran, more than 25 per cent higher than the Defence Department’s estimate in July, according to Pentagon data obtained by Reuters.

The Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment on its estimate, which has not been shared publicly.

The Pentagon’s latest estimate was tied to the operational costs of carrying out the war, with a projected cost of more than $29bn to replace expended munitions used in the conflict.

More than $6bn would be needed to replace military equipment and so-called “platform losses,” which include the loss of aircraft, including many drones lost during the war.

Published in Dawn, October 29th, 2026

https://www.dpa-international.com/politi.heading: UK maritime agency reports new tanker hit in Strait of Hormuz | dpa international
https://www.dpa-international.com/politi.body:
Another tanker has been hit by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, Britain's UKMTO maritime security organization reported on Thursday.

A shipping company's security officer had informed the organization that an unknown projectile struck the vessel in the afternoon as it was exiting the strait.

There was initially no information on potential injuries on board the tanker or about oil spills, nor details about the ship's country of origin.

In the conflict between the US and Iran, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has now become a central point of contention. Iranian armed forces have intensified attacks on vessels in the region in recent weeks.

The UKMTO had already reported one burning ship in the strait earlier in the morning, citing the captain of another ship in the vicinity. The cause of the fire was not initially known.

According to the organization, the report originated off the coast of Oman at the bend of the Strait of Hormuz, where the US Navy has been escorting tankers through the narrow sea passage.

Separating the Arabian Peninsula and Iran, the strait is only 21 nautical miles wide (39 km) and it consists of 2-mile-wide navigable channels for inbound and outbound shipping. Around 25% of the world's seaborne oil trade transits the route.

https://www.iranintl.com/en/202610286064.heading: UN’s Mai Sato details executions, mass trials in Iran crackdown | Iran International
https://www.iranintl.com/en/202610286064.body:
Iranian authorities have executed at least 34 people in connection with the January protests, conducted mass trials resulting in death sentences and detained thousands, UN Special Rapporteur Mai Sato said Wednesday.

Addressing the UN General Assembly, Sato described the scale of human rights violations during her two-year Iran mandate as extraordinary. “I struggled to find its precedent in recent history,” she said, warning that her findings represented only a fraction of the abuses committed against Iranians.

Her report, covering February through August 2026 following the December-January nationwide protests, detailed how the Islamic Republic used the war with the United States and Israel to intensify repression, treating peaceful protesters as agents of hostile foreign powers.

In just one case, 34 defendants were tried in five days, with 12 sentenced to death and seven already executed. She said such proceedings could not establish individual criminal responsibility, rendering the death sentences arbitrary.

Sato said senior Iranian officials had publicly demanded expedited trials, while courts conducted mass proceedings and broadcast alleged confessions within days of arrests. She added that lawyers defending protesters had been summoned, threatened and, in some cases, arrested.

The special rapporteur also reported thousands of arrests on national security charges, with many detainees held incommunicado at undisclosed locations, a pattern she described as enforced disappearance. She said families of protesters killed in the crackdown faced threats of prosecution and asset confiscation for demanding accountability, while some were denied the right to hold funerals.

Sato also described prisoners left locked inside overcrowded cells during airstrikes, with bars reportedly welded to ward doors. Government-imposed internet shutdowns prevented civilians from receiving warnings about incoming attacks and made documenting abuses dangerous. Under Iranian espionage legislation, sharing information with foreign media can carry the death penalty.

She said the authorities continued withholding information about executions and killings by security forces while publishing protest death tolls far below independent estimates.

“The result is that there is no lawful way left to dissent,” Sato said.

The UN's Independent International Fact-Finding Mission, which addressed the same session, concluded that the suppression of January's nationwide protests amounted to crimes against humanity. Sato said she saw no reason to depart from that finding.

Iran's representative, Ali Karimi Magham, rejected both UN investigative mechanisms, describing them as illegitimate and politically engineered instruments unrelated to genuine human rights protection.

Russia accused the investigators of advancing Western political interests and disregarding Iran's “complex and unique sociocultural context.”

North Korea similarly rejected the investigations, accusing the UN of the “weaponization of human rights.” Its representative argued that countries should determine their own societal models free from external interference and that country-specific investigations violated national sovereignty.

China concentrated on the consequences of war and sanctions, urging respect for Iran's sovereignty and calling for the removal of unilateral economic restrictions. Beijing said such measures violated economic and social rights and worsened the population's hardship.

Sato responded to Tehran's objections by pointing out that Iranian authorities had engaged with her office throughout her mandate, including extensively over the war, while continuing to withhold information about killings carried out by their own security forces.

Other delegations focused on the violations documented by the UN investigators, particularly the killing of protesters, executions and torture.

Britain described the killing of children during the January crackdown as “abhorrent” and condemned the torture of detainees, widespread violence against peaceful protesters and the authorities' internet shutdowns.

Australia accused Iranian authorities of using lethal force, mass arrests and a nationwide communications blackout to silence dissent and isolate Iranians from the outside world.

The European Union called for an immediate halt to executions, condemning the use of capital punishment and torture to suppress political opposition. It also warned about reprisals against critics, including those living abroad.

The Netherlands said the findings confirmed gross human rights violations, particularly a dramatic escalation in lethal force and mass arrests during the protests.

Canada raised concerns about proposed legislation that would criminalize contact with foreign organizations, civil society groups and diplomatic missions, potentially further restricting communication between Iranians and the outside world.

Sato also documented discrimination against Kurds, Baluch, Arabs and Azerbaijani Turks, alongside continuing persecution of Baha'is and Christian converts.

In her concluding remarks, Sato called on the United States and Israel to end hostilities and investigate their strikes, while urging Iranian authorities to halt executions and repression and investigate deaths caused by their forces.

Instead, she said, repression had deepened the grievances driving people into the streets.

https://www.iranintl.com/en/202610291360.heading: Cleric arrested in Iran protests sentenced to death twice | Iran International
https://www.iranintl.com/en/202610291360.body:
An Iranian cleric and former Revolutionary Guards member arrested during January's nationwide protests has been sentenced to death twice in separate cases, including for apostasy, US-based rights group HRANA reported Thursday.

The cleric, identified only as Mehdi, was sentenced to death alongside two other protesters, Amirreza Rezaei and Vahid Ghahremani, by Branch 23 of Tehran's Revolutionary Court, according to HRANA.

The charges against the three included allegedly carrying out operations on behalf of Israel, HRANA said. They were informed of their sentences in prison on Monday.

Mehdi, whose surname remains unknown, received a second death sentence from Iran's Special Clerical Court on a charge of apostasy. HRANA provided no further details about the circumstances of that case or his previous service in the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

All three were arrested separately by security forces during the nationwide protests in January. They were transferred from Greater Tehran Prison to Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj on Wednesday.

The sentences come amid warnings from the United Nations that Iranian authorities have intensified executions and prosecutions linked to the protests during the war with the United States and Israel.

UN Special Rapporteur Mai Sato told the General Assembly on Wednesday that at least 34 people had been executed in connection with the nationwide protests.

Sato cited one case in which 34 defendants were tried in just five days, with 12 sentenced to death and seven already executed. She raised concerns about mass trials, forced confessions and the lack of due process in capital cases.

"The war has provided cover for the authorities to intensify their crackdown and tighten the repression," Sato said, adding that protesters had been portrayed as agents of foreign powers and peaceful dissent prosecuted as a national security threat.

https://www.dpa-international.com/politi.body:
Iran has reported shooting down two military drones amid heightened military tensions with the United States.

An MQ-1 Predator drone was intercepted and destroyed east of the Strait of Hormuz by a new advanced air defence system, the Tasnim news agency reported on Thursday, citing Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The US military did not initially confirm the report.

A second report said a smaller US drone had also been downed in Iran. This could not be independently verified either.

According to the Iranian report, the country's armed forces have destroyed 14 MQ-1 Predator drones and more than 50 MQ-9 Reaper drones since the outbreak of war in late February. Such claims generally cannot be independently verified.

Iranian forces have recently stepped up attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz. Oil exports through the waterway fell again last week, according to shipping data provider Kpler.

https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/29/pale.body:
Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas said on Thursday that he hoped the election of a new Israeli government would allow for the resumption of peace talks.

During a meeting with Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides in Nicosia, Abbas asked Cyprus to mediate the efforts.

"For many years now, we have been extending a hand to the Israeli side in order to achieve peace with them, so that Israel and Palestine may live in security, stability and peace," Abbas said.

"We hope that, immediately after a new Israeli government is formed, we will be able to engage in dialogue together," he added.

Christodoulides said Abbas' visit comes at an "important moment" for the region.

"How can we work together, always through a positive approach? To create conditions of security and stability in the region. Of course, we are also at Palestine’s disposal, so that we may play whatever role they deem necessary for the Republic of Cyprus, in order to achieve our common goals," Christodoulides said.

Later during a working lunch attended by delegations from both sides, Abbas' highlighted the importance of Cyprus' role.

"I will not dwell on the excellent relationship that exists between the Palestinian people and the Cypriot people and the Republic of Cyprus, but you also have excellent relations—and rightly so—with Israel," Abbas said.

"So you can play a role in mediating between the two sides, based on a political solution that is grounded in international law and the resolutions of the Security Council and the United Nations," he concluded.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2.heading: Palestinians injured, arrested in Israeli raids across West Bank | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2.body:
Israeli forces and settlers have escalated pogroms and raids across the occupied West Bank, attacking and injuring Palestinians, restricting their movement, carrying out arrests and demolishing homes.

This comes as a military offensive and siege on the Hebron governorate entered its seventh day – an operation that has displaced or besieged hundreds of Palestinian families and kept tens of thousands of students out of classrooms.

In the Qalandiya refugee camp just north of occupied East Jerusalem, Israeli forces carried out a raid that triggered clashes on Thursday. Two children were wounded, the Palestine Red Crescent Society said.

It said its teams treated a 15-year-old boy who was shot with live ammunition in both legs, and a child, aged 12, who was injured by live-bullet fragments. Both were taken to hospital.

In a separate incident, Israeli soldiers and settlers beat disabled Palestinian Mohammad Ahmad Ayesh Thawabta in the village of al-Maniya, southeast of Bethlehem, the official Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

In the northern West Bank, Israeli forces detained 13 Palestinians, including three brothers, in raids before dawn on Thursday, the Palestinian Prisoners Media Office and local sources said. Most of the raids were in the Nablus governorate, where soldiers searched homes and harassed families.

In Hebron, Israeli forces continued raids and closures that began last week after two Israeli soldiers were killed in a gun attack. Both Palestinian suspects were also killed.

Hebron Governor Khaled Dudin said on Thursday that 537 families, comprising 3,361 people, have been forced from their homes, Wafa reported.

They include 232 infants, 326 older people, 147 pregnant or breastfeeding women and 213 people with chronic illnesses. Municipal figures put the total number affected, including those under siege, at about 5,000 people from 780 families.

Dudin said the offensive has disrupted education for about 262,000 students across 589 schools in the governorate this week, forcing schools to move to remote learning. Officials estimated daily economic losses at 10 million to 12 million shekels ($3.2m to $3.9m).

The Palestinian Prisoner’s Society said Israeli forces detained 110 Palestinians in the governorate from Friday to Wednesday. Soldiers beat two men in Dura and Wad al-Saman and arrested two brothers while they were ploughing their land east of Yatta, it said. Israeli forces also raided homes in Taffuh and Halhul, and settlers attacked vehicles at the city’s closed northern entrance, it added.

In nearby Masafer Yatta, armed settlers attacked US journalist Jasper Nathaniel and two activists in the village of Umm al-Khair on Wednesday. Russian activist Adele Shoko said on X that the settlers beat and threatened them and stole their equipment and Nathaniel was pepper-sprayed and arrested.

The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said Israeli forces are still operating in Hebron, blocking access and imposing tight restrictions on movement across the governorate.

They are “disrupting Palestinians’ access to livelihoods, education and healthcare. Most displaced families are staying with relatives,” OCHA said, calling for the prevention of further forced displacements and demolitions.

Israeli forces also demolished memorials to Palestinians in several parts of the Hebron governorate on Thursday. In Dura, south of Hebron city, soldiers fired a heavy barrage of tear gas before bulldozing a mural bearing the images of several of the town’s dead, including Bajis Abu Atwan, who was killed in the 1970s.

The targeting of memorials “appears to be a new pattern recently adopted by Israeli forces across all West Bank governorates – though at a higher rate here in Hebron”, Al Jazeera’s Muntasir Nassar said, reporting from Dura.

Israeli military and settler attacks across the West Bank have intensified since Israel’s war on Gaza began in October 2023.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2.heading: Israel election result shows no overall majority as vote count complete | Israel Election 2026 News | Al Jazeera
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2.body:
Vote counting is complete in Israel’s elections with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition winning a majority in parliament, Israeli media have said.

As the provisional results were being published on Thursday, opposition politicians met to explore options for a coalition.

With more than 99 percent of Tuesday’s ballots tallied, Netanyahu’s bloc held 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset while the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot secured 48 seats, Israeli outlet Haaretz reported.

The Arab list parties, meanwhile, held a combined 19 seats, it added.

Both Netanyahu’s bloc and the opposition parties fell short of securing the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority.

The final results of the Knesset elections will be certified and announced by Wednesday. Until that date, the results are subject to change.

Tuesday’s elections – the first since the October 7, 2023, attacks on southern Israel and the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza – were widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s premiership.

On Thursday, Eisenkot, who heads the Yashar party, met former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the Together party, to discuss ways to form a new government 'as quickly as possible', according to a statement reported by Israel’s Ynet News outlet.

Eisenkot also met Democrats party chairman Yair Golan, the only member of the opposition alliance to support forming a coalition with parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, while all other political groups have rejected any such union.

Golan met separately with Mansour Abbas, who leads the United Arab list, or Ra’am, which is projected to win seven of the 19 Arab party seats.

Meanwhile, Netanyahu’s Likud party has continued to amplify unsubstantiated allegations that Arab-led parties had 'stolen' the election, potentially with foreign assistance – claims that have been rejected.

The head of the Central Elections Committee, Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, said 'serious suspicions' of foreign interference had been brought to him in a letter to the Shin Bet security agency.

Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of working to delegitimise the election results with his allegations.

https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-eas.heading: Netanyahu, at risk of losing power, steps up attacks on Israel's Arab parties | Reuters
https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-eas.body:
JERUSALEM, Oct 29 (Reuters) - Israeli ​Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu alleged on Thursday, without providing evidence, that Arab parties' record gains in an election this week were driven in part by voter fraud, a charge ‌rejected by Arab leaders who accused the premier of incitement.

The allegation represents an escalation of rhetoric against Arab parties by Netanyahu and his far-right partners after high Arab turnout in a national ballot on Tuesday effectively blocked a smooth path to power for either him or his main rivals.

The Reuters Iran Briefing newsletter keeps you informed with the latest developments and analysis of the Iran war. Sign up here.

Israeli officials said on Thursday that the authorities were probing fraud allegations, though the election's integrity was not systematically compromised.

Analysts and critics say that by stepping up attacks on Arab parties, Netanyahu may be ​trying to ensure his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, feels unable to even consider forming a minority government with Arab help that could oust him from power.

Netanyahu's goal is "delegitimising any Arab-Jewish cooperation", ​said Eytan Gilboa, professor of politics at Reichman University.

Tuesday's tightly fought election has produced no clear winner and is likely to be followed by weeks of ⁠protracted negotiations over a new government.

With nearly 99% of votes counted, Netanyahu's nationalist-religious bloc held a modest lead in seats over a bloc of right-wing and centre-left parties led by Eisenkot, with both men's ​coalitions short of the 61 seats needed for a majority in parliament.

Parties representing Israel's 21% Arab minority were projected to win an unprecedented 19 seats, leaving Eisenkot's bloc, which has 48 seats against Netanyahu's camp ​of 53, with no path to power without broad Arab backing.

Eisenkot has so far ruled out including the parties in government but his camp could try to form a minority government with Arab support from the outside.

Ahmad Tibi, one of the leaders of the Arab Joint List party, said Netanyahu has launched a "toxic campaign" meant to undermine the election results.

"This entire campaign is directed against Eisenkot, to prevent him, intimidate and scare him off forming ​a government that relies on external support from the Joint List or Ra'am," Tibi told Reuters.

During and after Tuesday's election, Netanyahu and his allies warned against rising Arab turnout and his right-wing Likud party issued ​statements accusing the Arab parties of "stealing the vote."

It demanded police and the Shin Bet domestic intelligence service investigate incidents of suspected election bribery and intimidation at ballot stations in Arab towns. It said it possessed evidence of such ‌activity but has ⁠not presented it to the public.

The police say they have arrested at least seven people since Tuesday in Israel's south, where many Arabs live, on suspicion of voter fraud.

On Thursday, the head of Israel's Central Election Committee, Supreme Court jurist Noam Sohlberg, said he had asked the Shin Bet to investigate suspicions that unidentified foreign players had tried to intervene in the election.

Likud seized on Sohlberg's request, alleging an attack on Israel's democracy, "an Islamisation of Israel and the toppling of the right-wing in order to bring about IDF withdrawal and defeat on all fronts, foremost Iran."

Likud said Qatar was behind the alleged election intervention, which Qatar denied.

Ra'am ​head Mansour Abbas said his party was not involved ​and urged a full investigation.

"We have one ⁠message in response to the campaign of incitement and delegitimization he (Netanyahu) is waging against Arab citizens: Nothing will come of it, because there is nothing there," Abbas said in a statement.

In a letter sent to a parliamentarian and published by the Central Election Committee, the committee said that there was "no base for claims ​that there was systematic harm to the election's integrity."

Shin Bet said that its investigation was focused only on those involved and should not cast ​aspersions on "an entire sector that ⁠went out to vote democratically and legally."

The coalition that last toppled Netanyahu, in 2021, for the first time in Israel's history relied on an Arab party — Ra'am, which has Islamist roots. But Eisenkot's camp would need backing from the Arab-dominated Joint List, which includes an explicitly anti-Zionist party.

Eisenkot said in a statement that the investigation into possible election meddling must be carried out without politicians intervening.

"Likud and ⁠Netanyahu have set ​out on an orchestrated organised campaign to delegitimise the election results," Eisenkot said.

After vote tallying is completed, President Isaac Herzog will ​consult with party chairs and choose a candidate who he thinks has the best chance to form a government.

On Thursday, he said the allegations must be investigated.

"But even at a moment like this, we must not tarnish an entire community that sought to ​exercise its right to vote and take an active part in democracy," Herzog said.
