https://www.kurdistan24.net/en/story/949.body:
“ We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome,” Qatar’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said.

ERBIL (Kurdistan24) – Qatar on Thursday rejected allegations that it had interfered in Israel’s parliamentary elections or funded activities to influence the results, describing the accusations as “ridiculous and dangerous.”

“ We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome,” Qatar’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said.

The accusations, made by politicians aligned with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and their media contacts, claim that Arab parties received funding from Qatar. However, no evidence was provided to support the allegations.

Partial election results showed two Arab lists securing a strong position in the new parliament, potentially giving them a decisive role in determining the governing majority.

Mansour Abbas, leader of the Arab-Israeli Raam party, also rejected the accusations, while Israeli President Isaac Herzog called for an investigation and warned against stigmatising the Arab Israeli community, which recorded unprecedented voter turnout.

Netanyahu has also faced scrutiny over alleged Qatari payments to two of his aides, who were arrested last year. For years, his government tacitly supported Qatari funding for Gaza, which was then governed by Hamas, in an effort to maintain stability.

“Qatar should not be used as a scapegoat for the political failures of certain Israeli politicians,” Al Ansari said in a post on X, adding that the allegations would not distract Doha from its mediation efforts.

Qatar has played a central role in negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians, including efforts to halt the war in Gaza. Doha is also leading mediation efforts between Washington and Tehran to end the Middle East war, which began in late February with Israeli and US attacks on Iran.

More than 10 American military transport aircraft landed at Israeli airbases in southern Israel over the past week, according to analysts monitoring open-source flight tracking data.

Most of the recent cargo flights took off from Biggs Army Airfield in El Paso, Texas. According to the data, the planes were destined for the Israeli Air Force’s Nevatim and Ovda airbases in the south.

There have also been a number of other American military cargo flights to US bases in other Middle East countries in recent days, including Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Kuwait.

The contents of the transport planes are unknown, but are thought to be related to efforts by the US to improve its air defenses in the region ahead of a new possible round of fighting with Iran.

On Wednesday, The Wall Street Journal reported that the US military was sending a Patriot battery from Texas to bolster its air defenses in the region.

A month after an Omani copilot tried to crash a flydubai plane full of Israeli passengers en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv, in a terror attack foiled by the plane’s Indian pilot and a small group of Israeli passengers who tackled the terrorist, Israeli authorities today finally issued new, stringent directives to both foreign and Israeli airlines requiring them to submit crew information 48 hours prior to departure, amid other steps to bolster security.

The new directives also require that any further updates regarding crew are submitted no later than two hours before takeoff, and that a final list is issued at takeoff. Bloomberg reports that the measures were ordered by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after a security review, and are intended to allow adequate time for background checks.

The directives were issued by the National Center for Passenger Data Analysis, which operates the Tax Authority, and apply to all incoming and outgoing flights operated by all airlines, foreign and Israeli.

According to Israel’s Channel 13 news, all non-Israelis flying in and out of Israel — pilots, cabin crew and passengers — will henceforth be required to complete an online form 48 hours before entry to Israel, which will be reviewed by the Population Authority.

Furthermore, the Mossad and Shin Bet have designated certain countries as “red” countries and will review entry forms and visa applications from would-be arrivals from these countries, Channel 13 reports.

The Shin Bet, which hitherto oversaw security relating to Israeli airlines and provided the “security blanket” for all flights departing Israel, will from now be responsible for airline security procedures relating to incoming foreign airlines and their overseas departure points.

The near-disaster about Flight 1073 on September 30 exposed major flaws in Israel’s security procedures, especially for incoming foreign flights, with no effective oversight of the airlines’ vetting of pilots, no Israeli vetting of the crews, and aircrew lists routinely submitted only after planes have taken off. Unconfirmed reports said that some 1,240 aircrew members from countries that do not have diplomatic relations with Israel have entered the country over the past year.

The terrorist copilot Hamam al-Hammami had been grounded by Oman Air after it was discovered he was in possession of extremist materials, was nonetheless hired by flydubai, and intermittently worked the Dubai-Tel Aviv route.

The Channel 13 report also noted that the two off-duty flydubai pilots who took over the controls after Hammami had been immobilized, and who performed an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, have been cleared of any suspicion of cooperation with the terrorist at any stage.

Patrick Stewart, the classically trained stage actor who scaled the Shakespearean canon and added gravitas to a “Star Trek” franchise and the “X-Men” films, has died. He was 86.

Stewart died yesterday in Los Angeles, following “a brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy Body Dementia, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak says.

While best known as Professor Charles Xavier and Captain Jean-Luc Picard from the “X-Men” and “Star Trek: The Next Generation” series and films, respectively, Stewart spent more of his career onstage than in the X-Mansion or on the USS Enterprise.

Besides playing everyone from Claudius to Macbeth, he often performed a one-man rendition of “A Christmas Carol” and did West End and Broadway runs of Harold Pinter’s “No Man’s Land” and Samuel Beckett’s “Waiting for Godot” in repertoire with buddy Ian McKellen.

Stewart starred in the 2013 Israeli film “Hunting Elephants” and spent time in Israel while filming the movie.

Times of Israel staff contributed to this report.

“Ambassador Huckabee, this is unreleased video of an American who was beaten almost to death last week by Israeli settlers. You know his name because he came to you for help, but you blew him off. That’s disgraceful. Do your job,” Carlson writes on X.

The official, certified results of Tuesday’s elections will be presented to President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday, November 4, as scheduled, unnamed sources in the Shin Bet tell Channel 12 News.

The sources reportedly add that nothing in the information the security agency is investigating could affect the election result, in what is described as its “limited and focused probe” into alleged foreign state attempts to influence the vote.

The agency is investigating allegations regarding Qatar and at least two other countries, the report says, and is seeking to ascertain the sources of money conveyed to try to influence the vote, the routes by which it was sent, how much money was involved, and whether any Arab Knesset members knew anything about it, the report says.

Channel 12 further quotes unnamed sources in the Central Elections Committee condemning false assertions of widespread or systematic election fraud. “The claims about systematic intervention or stolen elections constitute political manipulation of the allegations that are being probed,” the sources say.

Earlier this evening, Dean Livne, the Central Elections Committee’s Acting Director General, said: “I don’t see a likelihood that [the allegations of foreign influence] will influence the results of the elections.”

The TV report says Shin Bet director David Zini informed the Central Elections Committee chair, Justice Noam Sohlberg, and Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara several weeks ago that the agency was gathering material relating to possible foreign efforts to influence the election, and subsequently received Sohlberg’s permission to open an investigation under Sohlberg’s supervision.

It adds that Zini yesterday sought and received Sohlberg’s permission to update Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu about the probe, but that Zini had in fact already done so.

It appears that the arrests of three Ra’am activists on election day, who were found to have tens of thousands of shekels in cash, are not connected to the Shin Bet probe, Channel 12’s reporting indicates.

The three have had their remands extended and have provided explanations for the money, the TV outlet reports, citing law enforcement sources. It says their arrests were the result of calls to the police made by Netanyahu’s chief of staff, Ido Norden. The Prime Minister’s Office denies this.

Ra’am party leader Mansour Abbas believes the establishment of a minority government led by Yashar party chair Gadi Eisenkot, with the outside support of Arab parties, is weak or impossible, Channel 12 news reports.

Abbas reportedly expressed the feeling in a meeting with party members.

It comes after the Jewish-led bloc against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu failed to win a majority in its own right in the election.

Only The Democrats have expressed openness to including Arab-majority parties.

https://turkishminute.com/2026/10/29/ali.heading: Aliyev to skip Ankara summit despite Erdoğan's invitation amid Turkey-Azerbaijan tensions - Turkish Minute
https://turkishminute.com/2026/10/29/ali.body:
Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev will not attend Friday’s Organization of Turkic States (OTS) summit in Ankara, Azerbaijani media reported Thursday, amid tensions between the two close allies over Turkey’s criticism of restrictions on headscarves in Azerbaijani schools.

Aliyev will be represented by Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov at the October 30 summit, according to the Azerbaijani Report Information Agency, which attributed his absence to previously scheduled engagements and a busy work schedule.

The agency reported that Aliyev would attend the final and closing ceremony of the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival in Baku on Friday and present awards to the finalists. It said his participation in the ceremony had been arranged in advance.

The announcement comes despite Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’s personal invitation to Aliyev during an October 21 telephone conversation and the departure of Erdoğan’s chief presidential adviser, Oktay Saral, following a dispute over Azerbaijan’s restrictions on headscarves in schools.

Saral criticized the restrictions in an October 12 post on X, saying it was unacceptable to prevent students wearing headscarves from exercising their right to education.

Azerbaijan amended its school uniform regulations in September to prohibit clothing considered inconsistent with prescribed uniforms or secular education. Although the regulations do not explicitly mention headscarves, some students wearing them have reportedly been turned away from classes.

Saral’s remarks prompted a sharp response from Azerbaijan’s ruling New Azerbaijan Party, which accused Turkish political figures of interfering in the country’s domestic affairs.

In an October 25 interview with journalist Talat Atilla, Saral said he was leaving his position on Erdoğan’s instructions. Asked whether his departure was connected to his criticism of Azerbaijan, he replied, 'Yes, it seems so.'

Saral announced his resignation the following day.

Middle East Eye had reported that Azerbaijan demanded Saral’s dismissal and legal action against Turkish commentators accused of insulting Aliyev.

The dispute has also resulted in measures against Turkish citizens. Azerbaijan has barred 31 Turkish nationals, including journalists, political figures and religious commentators, from entering the country and issued arrest warrants for seven others over statements related to the controversy.

Tensions between Ankara and Baku predate the headscarf controversy, Azerbaijani political analyst Arastun Orujlu told Meydan TV, an independent Azerbaijani news outlet operating in exile.

He identified Azerbaijan’s increasingly close ties with Israel as a major source of friction, pointing to broader competition between Turkey and Israel for influence in the South Caucasus.

Despite the tensions, Aliyev sent Erdoğan a message Thursday congratulating Turkey on the 103rd anniversary of the founding of the republic.

He described Azerbaijan and Turkey as bound by genuine ties of friendship and brotherhood and said the 2021 Shusha Declaration had elevated their relationship to the level of an alliance.

The announcement of his absence from the summit came later that day.

Bayramov, who will represent Azerbaijan at the summit, attended Thursday’s meeting of the OTS Council of Foreign Ministers in Ankara and met with his Turkish counterpart, Hakan Fidan.

The ministers discussed bilateral relations and regional and international developments, according to the Azerbaijani Foreign Ministry.

Friday’s summit, hosted by Erdoğan, will mark Turkey’s taking over the organization’s rotating chairmanship from Azerbaijan.

The OTS, which brings together Turkey, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan, promotes political, economic and cultural cooperation among Turkic-speaking countries.

According to the organization’s official announcement, the leaders are expected to discuss trade, transportation, energy and institutional cooperation, appoint a new secretary-general and adopt the Ankara Declaration.

Turkey and Azerbaijan maintain close military, energy and transportation ties and frequently describe their relationship as 'one nation, two states.'

https://www.dailysabah.com/politics/turk.heading: Türkiye, Uzbekistan sign 5 deals after Erdoğan-Mirziyoyev talks | Daily Sabah
https://www.dailysabah.com/politics/turk.body:
Turkey and Uzbekistan signed five agreements on Thursday aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation in trade, social security and business development following a meeting between President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Ankara.

The agreements were signed at the Presidential Complex after Erdoğan held talks with Mirziyoyev, who arrived in the Turkish capital to attend the 13th Organization of Turkic States (OTS) summit.

Erdoğan invited Mirziyoyev to the COP31 Leaders Summit in Antalya during talks in Ankara focused on strengthening bilateral ties and expanding cooperation among Turkic states.

He reaffirmed Ankara's commitment to deepening its high-level strategic partnership with Tashkent, particularly in trade, investment, mining, transportation and the defense industry.

He also expressed confidence that the OTS would continue to grow stronger through new cooperation initiatives, voicing hope that the upcoming leaders' summit in Ankara would mark a significant milestone for the organization.

Erdoğan welcomed his Uzbek counterpart at the entrance of the Presidential Complex before their meeting.

The agreements included an additional protocol amending a 2022 arrangement on the advance exchange of information concerning vehicles and goods crossing national borders, signed by Turkish Trade Minister Ömer Bolat and Uzbek Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov.

A separate protocol amending the preferential trade agreement between the two countries was signed by Bolat and Uzbek Minister of Investment, Industry and Trade Laziz Kudratov.

Turkish Labor and Social Security Minister Vedat Işıkhan and Saidov signed a bilateral social security agreement, along with a separate administrative agreement governing its implementation.

Erdoğan and Mirziyoyev also signed an agreement establishing a high-level council to support the business community and strengthen economic cooperation between the two countries.

The agreements come as Ankara and Tashkent seek to expand bilateral trade, which reached $3.1 billion in 2025, toward their shared target of $5 billion.

Earlier Thursday, Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz welcomed Mirziyoyev, Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedov and Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov at the airport ahead of the OTS summit.

In a statement shared on the Turkish social media platform NSosyal, Yılmaz expressed hope that the gathering would strengthen solidarity and cooperation among Turkic states.

https://tass.com/world/2210355.heading: African nations seek to expand cooperation with Russia in multiple sectors — CAR President -  World - TASS
https://tass.com/world/2210355.body:
According to Faustin-Archange Touadera, African states intend to move away from an economic model where the continent serves primarily as a raw material supplier, while processing and value-added production take place abroad.

MOSCOW, October 29. /TASS/. African nations are looking to Russia for assistance in developing their industrial, agricultural, energy, and transport infrastructure sectors, Central African Republic (CAR) President Faustin-Archange Touadera announced at the plenary session of the third Russia-Africa summit.

"We wish to develop cooperation with Russia in a variety of areas," he said. In particular, the CAR President pointed to agriculture, the extraction and processing of mineral resources--including copper and uranium--solar and general energy development, and the creation of transport corridors to provide access to seaports.

He also underscored the importance of digital cooperation and technology transfer.

According to Touadera, African states intend to move away from an economic model where the continent serves primarily as a raw material supplier, while processing and value-added production take place abroad.

In this regard, he called for developing local manufacturing, attracting investment, training specialists, and expanding international market access for African products.

The CAR President also thanked Russia for its security assistance.

"Your support in technology and the assistance provided to our national armed forces enabled us to achieve stability and peacefully hold elections in December 2025," he noted, adding that the focus must now shift toward economic development.

"The time has come to translate the peace achieved into concrete projects."

He expressed confidence that the summit should serve as a starting point for concrete initiatives, including the construction of industrial facilities, roads, schools, and hospitals.

Such cooperation, he emphasized, must be based on respect for sovereignty, non-interference in internal affairs, equality, and transparency.

Touadera also noted Russia’s support for the African position on reforming international institutions to ensure broader representation for the continent.

https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/10/2.heading: State Duma Passes Record Defense Spending Budget in First Reading - The Moscow Times
https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/10/2.body:
Lawmakers in the lower house State Duma passed the first reading of a draft three-year federal budget on Thursday, approving record defense spending alongside a new wave of tax hikes designed to fund the rising costs of the war in Ukraine.

The proposed budget allocates 17.1 trillion rubles ($202.6 billion) to national defense, accounting for over a third of total federal expenditures. Combined with a 7.6% increase in national security and policing, security forces will account for 44% of total government spending, totaling 21.3 trillion rubles ($262.1 billion).

"All questions related to security, defense and providing everything necessary for participants of the special military operation and their families have been resolved," State Duma Speaker Vyacheslav Volodin said during a discussion of the bill.

To offset soaring military expenditures, the draft budget redirects funding away from civilian sectors. Spending on economic support and healthcare will each drop by 3%, while funding for social support falls by 6% and housing and utilities take an 8% cut.

Russia is relying on broad revenue extraction measures to cover its spending priorities. The draft proposal imposes a 22% value-added tax (VAT) on cross-border online retail, alongside a small customs fee on small international packages.

It also introduces a progressive tax scale reaching up to 22% on passive personal income, a 35% levy on dividend transfers to non-resident Type C accounts and a 30% tax on excess corporate profits in the mining and metallurgy sectors.

Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said the budget draft preserves the key priorities of "fulfilling social obligations to our citizens, addressing the tasks of the special military operation, ensuring victory… and achieving the president’s national development goals."

The draft bill passed with 372 votes in favor, 51 abstentions, and zero opposing votes. It now advances to its second reading before going to the upper-house Federation Council for a vote, after which it will require a final signature from President Vladimir Putin.

https://meduza.io/en/news/2026/10/29/est.body:
Estonia plans to build about 150 bunkers in Ida-Viru County, along the border with Russia, Defense Minister Martin Herem said during a question-and-answer session in the Riigikogu, the Estonian parliament, responding to a question from lawmaker Arvo Aller.

Aller asked what national defense measures are planned for Ida-Viru County and whether the state intends to acquire private land along the Narva River to plan its actions in the border zone.

“As part of the construction of the Baltic defense zone, for example, around 150 bunkers are planned in Ida-Viru County, 100 of which will be on state land and about 50 on municipal or private land,” Herem said.

He added that if private land is needed for the bunkers, possible solutions include compensating landowners for the inconvenience, leasing the land, or purchasing it.

The Baltic states have steadily strengthened their defenses in recent years amid fears of aggression from Russia. Estonia installed stationary drone detection and monitoring equipment along its border, while Finland completed a 200-kilometer (124-mile) fence along its border with Russia. Lithuania is also building a barrier along its border with the Kaliningrad region.

Finland’s Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen will meet U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Washington, D.C., on Thursday to discuss efforts to end Russia’s war in Ukraine.

The Finnish Ministry for Foreign Affairs announced the meeting in a statement released overnight.

“The meeting with U.S. Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, comes at a good time and provides an opportunity for a confidential discussion of the efforts to secure peace in Russia’s war of aggression in Ukraine,” Valtonen said.

“Finland supports Ukraine’s goal of a just and lasting peace,” she added.

The meeting follows Tuesday’s phone call between Finnish President Alexander Stubb, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

According to the Finnish President’s Office, the call aimed to communicate messages directly to Putin ahead of further peace negotiations.

However, the diplomatic initiative drew criticism from Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, of the Social Democrats, who accused the Nordic leaders of “going solo.”

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy subsequently expressed gratitude for their diplomatic efforts.

Speaking to Norwegian broadcaster NRK on Wednesday, Støre defended the conversation, arguing that European leaders must communicate their positions directly to Moscow rather than rely entirely on Washington.

The call, initially scheduled for 20 minutes, lasted 90 minutes.

American envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have played prominent roles in negotiations involving Russia.

Last week, Witkoff met Zelenskyy in Oslo before traveling to Saint Petersburg for talks with Putin.

The latest diplomatic efforts come ahead of planned negotiations in Abu Dhabi, where Ukrainian, Russian and American delegations are expected to meet in the first half of November.

Philippines-China tensions resurface at the close of ASEAN defence gathering

BEIJING/CEBU - Tensions between the Philippines and China resurfaced at the close of a two-day ASEAN defence gathering on Thursday (Oct 29), with Beijing accusing an unnamed Philippine politician of obstructing its participation and Manila saying China had been given an opportunity to state its position.

China's defence ministry said the "self-serving" politician had "imposed obstacles to China's participation" in the expanded ASEAN defence ministers' meeting in Cebu, without identifying the person.

Its spokesperson Zhang Xiaogang said at a press conference the actions ran counter to the meeting's open and inclusive spirit, violated diplomatic norms, and undermined China's rights as a dialogue partner.

China was represented at the meeting by a military attache in the absence of Defence Minister Dong Jun, who was likely attending a key Chinese Communist Party meeting in Beijing this week.

Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro, who chaired the meetings, did not directly address the Chinese allegation of obstruction but said Beijing had been given the opportunity to present its views and that no ASEAN member raised similar concerns.

"The important fact is they were able to articulate their position on regional maritime security with little additions," Teodoro said at his closing press conference. The Philippines has said its defence ministry sent notice to its Chinese counterpart with an invitation to join the forum.

"We allowed the exchange of views to be robust, and I think that was the important thing, the opportunity to be heard," Teodoro said.

Relations between Beijing and Manila have soured amid repeated confrontations in the disputed South China Sea and, more recently, Chinese sanctions imposed on Teodoro.

The exchange put the spotlight back on that increasingly fraught relationship after defence officials at the annual gathering stressed practical co-operation and sought to find areas of agreement despite differences over the South China Sea and other regional security issues.

Washington used the gathering to reaffirm its commitment to the region, with US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Wednesday pledging the US would defend its interests and those of allies and partners while proposing greater defence co-operation with the 11-member bloc.

China claims sovereignty over almost the entire South China Sea via a nine-dash line on its maps that cuts into parts of the exclusive economic zones of Malaysia, Vietnam, the Philippines, Brunei and Indonesia. An international arbitral tribunal ruled in 2016 that China's sweeping claims have no basis under international law, a decision Beijing rejects.

During bilateral meetings with several counterparts, including from other South China Sea claimant states, Teodoro stressed the importance of the 2016 ruling, arguing that its underlying principles were part of international law and not solely a Philippine matter.

In talks with Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi, the two expressed serious concerns over the increasing scale and frequency of what they described as China's coercive activities in disputed waters.

Teodoro also defended his country's growing network of defence partnerships and rejected suggestions they undermined regional stability, saying the Philippines faced "unilateral and illegal claims made by China over its maritime domain."

"If other ASEAN countries were subjected to the same kind of action in the magnitude the Philippines is experiencing, I am sure that they would resist this to the best of their ability," Teodoro said as he reiterated the country's commitment to peace and security.

https://english.news.cn/20261029/b8a6775.heading: China to take all necessary measures should EU impose discriminatory trade restrictions: commerce ministry
https://english.news.cn/20261029/b8a6775.body:
BEIJING, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- China will take all necessary measures to safeguard its interests and the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese enterprises if the European Union (EU) insists on imposing discriminatory restrictions on Chinese products, the Ministry of Commerce said Thursday.

Ministry spokesperson Huang Ling made the remarks at a regular news conference in response to media reports that the EU is considering extending the understanding reached between China and the EU on hybrid vehicle trade to other sectors such as chemicals.

Imposing artificial barriers to normal trade may violate World Trade Organization rules and would not help improve the competitiveness of EU industries. Instead, such measures would place a heavier burden on downstream industries, pushing up inflation in the EU and undermining the security and stability of global industrial and supply chains, Huang said.

Huang said the second meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism, held recently, made positive progress and yielded a number of agreed outcomes, showing that both sides have the willingness, ability and wisdom to properly manage their economic and trade differences through dialogue and consultation.

China has repeatedly stressed that it is a partner in addressing the problems facing the EU, rather than the source of those problems, Huang said, adding that China is willing to strengthen dialogue and consultation with the EU, continue exploring solutions to each other's economic and trade concerns, and promote upward balancing and forward progress in China-EU trade.

China firmly opposes any protectionist practices involving the abuse of trade defense instruments, Huang said. ■

https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/worl.heading: North Korea fires around 10 ballistic missiles toward sea, Seoul says
https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/worl.body:
SEOUL, Oct 29 (Reuters) - North Korea fired around 10 ballistic missiles toward the sea off its east coast on Thursday, South Korea's military said, as tensions run high ahead of Pyongyang's end-of-month deadline to activate propaganda loudspeakers along the heavily armed border.

The short-range missiles were launched at around 12:30 p.m. (0330 GMT) from around Wonsan on North Korea's eastern coast and flew about 250 km (155 miles), South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) said.

South Korea was strengthening surveillance and maintaining readiness for additional launches, while closely sharing information with the United States and Japan, it added.

Japan's Defence Ministry said North Korea had launched what could be a ballistic missile and that it did not appear to have landed within Japan's Exclusive Economic Zone.

South Korea's presidential National Security Office convened an emergency meeting to assess the security implications.

It urged North Korea to halt its repeated ballistic missile launches, calling them a "serious violation" of UN Security Council resolutions, a presidential statement said.

"The launch can be linked to the tensions along the border as part of a broader series of North Korean shows of force, although it is difficult to say the border situation directly prompted the missile launch," said Kim Yong-hyun, a professor of North Korean Studies at Seoul's Dongguk University.

Kim said the launch also appeared intended to demonstrate North Korea's increasingly advanced ballistic missile capabilities to the US, Japan and the broader international community.

The launch came as tensions along the inter-Korean border have risen sharply since two mine explosions in the Demilitarised Zone on September 21 wounded three South Korean soldiers.

Seoul says the mines were planted by North Korean forces and has called the incident an armistice violation and demanded an apology. Pyongyang has denied responsibility and accused Seoul of fabricating the incident.

Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, announced last week that Pyongyang would place loudspeakers capable of blasting anti-South Korean propaganda on standby across the border within days.

She had earlier said the broadcasts would operate along the entire border by the end of October, though analysts in Seoul questioned whether the devices would be activated.

"Rather than being a firm decision to begin broadcasts, North Korea seems to be saying it will have everything ready and watch how South Korea responds," said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University in Seoul.

North Korea's military has also deployed artillery batteries visible from across the border, which South Korea's military said earlier on Thursday appeared largely intended for show.

"We assess that North Korea has several intentions, but the exposure of older weapon systems should be understood as being for show," JCS spokesperson Jang Do-young told a briefing.

Defence Ministry spokesperson Chung Binna said placing artillery where it could be easily seen "makes little tactical or military sense".

Reuters witnesses this week saw three North Korean armoured vehicles, identified by South Korean experts as self-propelled 122-mm howitzers, positioned near the border with their gun barrels pointed south.

North Korean soldiers were also seen erecting fences inside the DMZ.

Jang said North Korean activity near the Military Demarcation Line bisecting the DMZ was continuing, while South Korean forces were issuing warning broadcasts and firing warning shots during incursions.

Seoul was awaiting a response to its two proposals for military talks and had urged North Korea to return to dialogue, the Defence Ministry said.

North Korea last fired ballistic missiles on October 12. Pyongyang has conducted missile tests on more than 10 occasions this year.

https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261029014.heading: S. Korean defense chief agrees to expand defense cooperation with Singapore, Vietnam | Yonhap News Agency
https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261029014.body:
SEOUL, Oct. 29 (Yonhap) -- South Korean Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul on Thursday met with his Singaporean and Vietnamese counterparts to discuss ways to expand defense cooperation with the two countries, his ministry said.

Kang met with Singapore's Defense Minister Chan Chun Sing on the sidelines of an extended defense ministers' meeting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in the Philippines, according to the ministry.

During the talks, the two sides positively assessed their efforts to expand cooperation in the defense sector after the two countries forged a strategic partnership during summit talks between their leaders in November last year.

The ministers also agreed to expand cooperation in various areas, including personnel exchanges, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence (AI).

Kang also met separately with Vietnamese Defense Minister Phan Van Giang, with the two sides agreeing to swiftly hold their annual senior-level defense talks in a bid to accelerate cooperation in the defense sector.

They also vowed to push for a revision to a bilateral memorandum of understanding on defense cooperation concluded in 2010 to better reflect the changing security landscape and the state of their relations.

South Korea and Vietnam agreed to establish a comprehensive and strategic partnership in 2022 on the occasion of the 30th anniversary of their diplomatic relations.

During the back-to-back meetings, Kang explained that North Korea's latest launch of short-range ballistic missiles toward the East Sea earlier in the day posed a security threat to the Korean Peninsula and the region.

He also requested cooperation from the international community regarding the recent explosion caused by North Korean mines planted south of the Military Demarcation Line, saying it was a "clear violation" of the Armistice Agreement that suspended the 1950-53 Korean War.

The Sept. 21 mine blast injured three South Korean soldiers, two of them seriously, but Pyongyang has denied its responsibility.

https://www.koreaherald.com/article/1091.heading: Korea, Germany forge ‘enhanced strategic partnership’ as global risks mount - The Korea Herald
https://www.koreaherald.com/article/1091.body:
South Korea and Germany agreed to elevate their ties to an 'enhanced strategic partnership,' pledging to expand the scope of cooperation to advanced industries and future growth sectors while strengthening defense and security ties.

President Lee Jae Myung and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz outlined the expanded partnership in a joint statement issued after their summit at Cheong Wa Dae in Seoul on Thursday.

The two leaders noted that their meeting came 'at a time of increased strategic convergence and mutual solidarity.'

They also agreed to 'significantly intensify their bilateral and multilateral cooperation, considering that the increase in global risks and challenges as well as shared opportunities necessitates concerted action.'

Speaking at a joint news conference, Lee underlined that “today's summit will be remembered as an important milestone in opening a new future for Korea-Germany relations.”

Chancellor Merz and I have agreed to establish an enhanced strategic partnership between our two countries based on deep trust and cooperation,” Lee said.

The joint statement adopted today reflects the firm and clear commitment of both countries to deepen cooperation across a wide range of areas, including politics, security, the economy, culture and people-to-people exchanges, and to strengthen future-oriented cooperation and strategic coordination.

On defense, Lee said the countries had agreed to deepen defense and security cooperation, and to expand 'practical, mutually beneficial cooperation' in the defense industry.

Seoul and Berlin also pledged to expedite an agreement on the exchange of classified military information.

Our two countries will strengthen strategic communication between our respective defense authorities and work to swiftly conclude an Agreement on the Protection of Classified Military Information, thereby reinforcing the institutional foundation for defense and security cooperation,” Lee said.

The joint statement called for regular military exchanges, closer cooperation on training and greater information sharing between the two countries. Lee highlighted growing interest among South Korean defense manufacturers in establishing long-term partnerships with German companies.

I also conveyed that Korean defense companies have a strong interest in establishing long-term partnerships with Germany, the world’s third-largest economy and Europe’s largest, through joint investments and joint development,” Lee said.

We will actively seek opportunities for mutually beneficial cooperation between defense companies, building on the advanced defense technologies and industrial capabilities of Korea and Germany,” he added.

Beyond bilateral defense ties, Lee said the two leaders agreed to 'strengthen strategic coordination on major issues amid growing global economic and security uncertainties.'

The two leaders acknowledged the increasingly close links between security in Northeast Asia and Europe and pledged to work together to promote peace and stability in both regions in the joint statement.

The two leaders discussed peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula, referring to the two countries' shared experience of national division.

Drawing on Germany’s own painful experience of division, Chancellor Merz has expressed a deep, unwavering understanding of our efforts to resume dialogue and establish a peace regime on the Korean Peninsula,” Lee said.

Moreover, our two nations have agreed to continue cooperating steadfastly to realize peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula.

Speaking at the joint press conference, Merz said he plans to visit the Demilitarized Zone separating the two Koreas on Friday, saying, “We know all too well how painful it is to live in a divided country.”

The two leaders additionally exchanged views on Russia's war in Ukraine, developments in the Middle East, the international free trade system and climate change, committing to closer cooperation in addressing shared global challenges, according to Lee.

Lee underlined that Seoul and Berlin had agreed to “strengthen strategic cooperation in the economic and industrial sectors and broaden the scope of cooperation to advanced industries and future growth engines.”

Through the Framework for an Economic and High-tech Partnership, bilateral cooperation, which has centered on trade and investment, will expand into the industrial and advanced technology sectors,” Lee said.

South Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources and Germany's Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy are set to sign the Joint Declaration of Intent on a Framework for an Economic and High-tech Partnership on Friday morning.

The agreement aims to strengthen bilateral cooperation in trade, industry, future technologies and innovation, including automobiles, batteries, industrial artificial intelligence, smart manufacturing, advanced energy systems and robotics.

In their joint statement, the leaders described the two countries as 'trusted partners with complementary strengths in the semiconductor industry,' pledging to deepen cooperation through a semiconductor ecosystem partnership that is expected to be concluded in the near future.

Speaking at the news conference, Lee said he had sought Germany's support to ensure that South Korean companies receive the same treatment as those in European Union member states under the bloc's proposed Industrial Accelerator Act.

The two sides agreed to renew their energy partnership agreement, expanding policy and technology exchanges on renewable energy and power grids, as well as joint research aimed at advancing the energy transition and ensuring a stable supply of clean energy.

They signed a protocol amending their double taxation agreement, which Lee said would provide a 'fairer and more transparent environment' for bilateral investment and economic cooperation.

The summit coincided with Merz's visit to Seoul for the 19th Asia-Pacific Conference of German Business, which is being held in the South Korean capital for the first time since 2007.

In their joint statement, the leaders called the conference 'a cornerstone of bilateral and regional engagement,' saying its location in Seoul reflected South Korea's 'geopolitical weight, technological edge and role as a trusted anchor for German industries in the Indo-Pacific.'

https://www.koreaherald.com/article/1091.heading: Seoul, US making progress on OPCON transfer talks despite concerns over delay: security chief - The Korea Herald
https://www.koreaherald.com/article/1091.body:
South Korea and the United States are making progress in discussions of wartime operational control, National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac said Thursday, amid concerns the postponement of a bilateral defense meeting and revised US military requirements could delay the transition.

Speaking during a parliamentary audit of the presidential office by the National Assembly Steering Committee, Wi said Seoul had been consulting with Washington with the goal of completing the OPCON transfer within President Lee Jae Myung's term.

"We will continue advancing the discussions and report back on the results," Wi told lawmakers.

Concerns over a potential delay have intensified after the annual South Korea-US Security Consultative Meeting was postponed to early next year, with some questioning whether the allies can maintain momentum and complete the transfer within President Lee Jae Myung's term.

The uncertainty also follows remarks from Gen. Xavier Brunson, commander of US Forces Korea, who indicated at a Washington seminar on Oct. 14 that changes in the security environment and military planning had created new benchmarks that must be met before the transition can proceed.

His comments raised questions about whether the allies would need to reassess the conditions governing the transfer, potentially complicating Seoul's efforts to accelerate the process.

Addressing those concerns, Wi said the allies had agreed to pursue an early OPCON transfer based on conditions established during the early years of the former Moon Jae-in administration.

"We are working to bring forward the timing of the transfer in accordance with that principle," Wi said.

He noted that discussions had continued recently, including talks between the South Korean and US defense chiefs in the Philippines.

"There has been a convergence of views on the conditions and timing," Wi said, adding that Seoul was currently focused on meeting the necessary requirements and determining the transfer timeline through consultations with Washington.

Meanwhile, Wi said Seoul was considering deploying a maritime patrol aircraft as part of international efforts to safeguard freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, but stressed that no decision had been made.

"We have reviewed the possibility of deploying a maritime patrol aircraft, but no decision has been made," Wi said, adding that Seoul was consulting with Washington on possible contributions while adhering to President Lee's directive not to participate in combat operations or warfare.

The remarks came as Seoul considers expanding the operational area of its Cheonghae anti-piracy naval unit, currently deployed in the Gulf of Aden, to the Gulf of Oman, which lies just outside the Strait of Hormuz.

Rep. Kim Joon-hyung of the Rebuilding Korea Party raised concerns that such an expansion could effectively amount to a new military mission, potentially exposing South Korean forces to attacks even without direct combat involvement. Wi rejected suggestions that the proposal was intended to accommodate US requests while avoiding a formal military deployment, citing Japan's maritime patrol operations in Djibouti as a precedent.

Wi also dismissed suggestions of a policy rift between Lee and his national security team over North Korea, particularly regarding possible adjustments to joint military exercises with the United States.

Describing the perceived differences as a "misunderstanding," Wi said Lee was outlining the administration's broader diplomatic objectives, while he was explaining the practical challenges involved in achieving them. He added that joint military exercises could be adjusted depending on circumstances but remained necessary.

In his opening remarks, Wi reaffirmed Seoul's commitment to serving as a "pacemaker" for renewed US-North Korea dialogue, citing US President Donald Trump's willingness to engage Pyongyang. He said the government would pursue a phased approach to denuclearization involving a freeze, reduction and eventual dismantlement of North Korea's nuclear capabilities.

Wi also pledged to strengthen South Korea's independent defense capabilities, including through the acquisition of nuclear-powered submarines, while supporting the defense industry's growth as a strategic national industry.

Separately, Wi defended the government's response to a September land mine explosion in the Demilitarized Zone that injured three South Korean soldiers, saying Seoul had raised the incident with the United Nations, including the Security Council.

Asked about apparent differences in North Korea policy between the Foreign Ministry and Unification Ministry, Wi acknowledged that agencies could hold differing views but said they were being coordinated through the National Security Council.

South Korean prosecutors are seeking the death penalty for former President Yoon Suk-yeol over his failed attempt to impose military rule.

The team led by special prosecutor Cho Eun-suk renewed the demand at an appeal hearing in Seoul on Thursday, arguing that Yoon’s actions threatened South Korea’s democracy.

He was sentenced to life imprisonment in February after being convicted of leading an insurrection.

Prosecutors had previously sought the death penalty at Yoon’s original trial in January, but the court sentenced him to life imprisonment the following month.

At Thursday’s hearing at the Seoul High Court, a prosecutor said there was “no reason to hesitate” over imposing the death penalty, according to South Korea’s Yonhap news agency.

South Korea retains the death penalty but has not carried out an execution since 1997.

Prosecutors argued that this long pause should not prevent judges from sentencing Yoon to death.

Yoon declared martial law on December 3, 2024, deploying soldiers and police to the National Assembly, South Korea’s parliament.

Lawmakers overcame a security blockade to vote down the measure, forcing the government to withdraw it about six hours after it was announced.

The lower court found that Yoon had tried to stop parliament from functioning, detain political opponents and remain in control of the country for an extended period.

Yoon’s lawyers told reporters on Thursday that he had intended to warn an opposition-controlled parliament against what he considered attempts to obstruct his government, not to establish authoritarian rule.

Speaking at the Seoul High Court on October 27, Yoon also denied seeking to establish a long-term dictatorship, according to the Hankyoreh newspaper.

The crisis led parliament to impeach Yoon in December 2024.

South Korea’s Constitutional Court, which decides whether to uphold impeachments, removed him from office in April 2025.

The appeals court plans two more hearings, including Yoon’s final statement on November 5.

https://news.az/news/canada-set-to-join-.heading: Canada set to join Europe’s advanced computing network | News.az
https://news.az/news/canada-set-to-join-.body:
The European Union and Canada are strengthening cooperation on computing capacity, a crucial resource for training AI models, with Canada set to become part of the EU’s supercomputing network.

European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen said on Thursday Canada "will now become part of this network", confirming a POLITICO report from earlier this week that both sides were discussing the country's entry into the European supercomputing network.

Canada joining "enables Canadian industry, startups and researchers to access European supercomputing," von der Leyen said. "Paired with Canada's pioneering AI industry, this would allow us to develop highly competitive, innovative and safe AI systems."

The EU's supercomputing network is run by the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking, an EU public-private vehicle with an €8.2 billion budget. The network consists of 14 supercomputers (some ranked in the global top 10), 19 AI-focused AI factories and 10 quantum computers.The vehicle will also run seven massive AI data center hubs, known as AI gigafactories, set to be built next year with a total investment cost of €30 billion.

Experts praised a possible EU-Canadian compute power team-up, but warned it's only the start.

“Compute cooperation is one of the most obvious short-term ‘middle power’ cooperation plays in AI,” said Anton Leicht, technology and international affairs fellow at Carnegie Endowment for International Peace.

But he added that for now “it doesn’t put a dent into the actual dependence" on the U.S.

“As long as the U.S. builds gigawatt-scale clusters, no amount of cooperation that doesn’t result in massive buildouts will help,” he said.

Canada's engagement in the EU's supercomputer network builds further on Canada's previous partial involvement in the EU's flagship research and development program, Horizon Europe.Horizon Europe partially funds EuroHPC.

To date, 38 countries have participated in the EU's supercomputing network: 27 EU member countries plus non-EU countries including Norway, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, Israel and Turkey.

https://www.thelocal.de/20261029/europea.heading: Europeans and Canadians set to get more opportunities to move across Atlantic
https://www.thelocal.de/20261029/europea.body:
The European Union and Canada are set to announce on Friday a new strategic alliance that will include more opportunities for Canadians and Europeans to live and study and work on the opposite side of the Atlantic.

The two-day EU-Canada summit in Montreal, on October 29th and 30th, will address a wide range of issues with the perspective of launching the Canada-EU “Alliance for the Future” in order to “create a common prosperity and economic security space.”

The EU and Canada have both faced US tariffs under President Trump, who has also threatened of annexation Canada and Greenland (which is part of Denmark but not of the EU).

The draft joint statement set to be published after the summit and reported on by Politico says: “Closer engagement at the highest political levels will allow us to exchange views, identify shared priorities and coordinate our responses to common challenges.”

The draft statement also says that “Canada and the EU will expand opportunities for Canadians and Europeans to study, work, conduct research and build lasting connections and cultural exchanges across the Atlantic.”

“Canada and the EU will launch negotiations toward deeper participation in Erasmus+”, the EU flagship programme for education, training, youth and sport, the draft continues.

Discussions should also be launched on “cooperating on skills development and enhancing labour and researcher mobility, and talent attraction, with a focus on reducing barriers for young people and facilitating mobility for highly skilled workers and researchers and promoting greater recognition of professional qualifications.”

In this regard, Canada and the EU will explore a “next-generation Youth Mobility Partnership that will further enable young Canadians and Europeans to access opportunities across the Atlantic through a more integrated mobility framework,” the statement is expected to say.

A joint press conference is planned at the end of the summit, on Friday evening, with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, EU Council President António Costa and Canada Prime Minister Mark Carney.

The new partnership builds on the EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), a free-trade pact signed in 2016 which is not fully implemented yet. Canadian officials have said businesses are pursuing new opportunities in Europe to offset US tariff-related losses, AFP reported.

Talks will also aim to align policies on climate, energy, artificial intelligence, critical minerals and infrastructure investment.

In September, President Ursula von der Leyen offered Canada to become the first EU associate member.

At an event on the sidelines of the summit, on Thursday, von der Leyen said: “It has become clear that there is more that we can do together bilaterally, Canada and the European Union. Canada cannot become a full-fledged member of the EU because of geography, but we both want to bring our relationship to the highest level possible. This is why we are discussing the idea of Canada becoming the first associate member of the European Union.”

Several EU countries, including Germany, France and Italy, however, have objected to the words “associate EU membership” in the final declaration because EU treaties do not include any provisions on such status.

https://breakingdefense.com/2026/10/cana.heading: Canada unveils first national security strategy in more than 20 years - Breaking Defense
https://breakingdefense.com/2026/10/cana.body:
Canada has released a national security strategy today focused on sovereignty — marking the first time Ottawa has released such a document in more than 20 years.

“Canada stands at a hinge moment in history,” Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a statement today. “The world is increasingly defined by contested borders, authoritarian aggression, and acute global threats. The long-held belief that the combination of our geography, interconnectedness, and a rules-based international order could substitute for Canadian sovereign capacity to protect ourselves is no longer tenable.”

The strategy drives home that Canada “controls its own destiny,” and comes amid tension between Canada and its North American neighbor, the US, over tense trade negotiations. Specifically, the national security policy underscores several key priorities, including a “cooperative, clear-eyed relationship” with the US, and an “innovative” Canadian economy.

“To bolster our sovereignty and national security, we will build long-term economic strength through generational domestic investments,” Carney said. “We will develop a dense web of trading relationships that bolster our strategic capabilities. We will focus our diplomatic efforts on practical cooperation and partnerships that will help us influence the course of global events to serve the interests of Canadians. We will rebuild, rearm, and reinvest in the Canadian Armed Forces.”

Likewise, the proposal emphasizes that Canada aims to foster stability with international partners though a “global system” of partnerships.

“We will broaden our options and build our resilience by diversifying our economic and security ties around the world, including with new partners in the Middle East, Africa and elsewhere,” Carney said in his message.

Canada last released a national security strategy in 2004.

https://apnews.com/article/hegseth-gener.heading: Hegseth fires the Pentagon's top military planner | AP News
https://apnews.com/article/hegseth-gener.body:
U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth attends the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Defence Ministers’ Informal Meeting in Cebu, central Philippines, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. (Jam Sta Rosa/Pool Photo via AP)

U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth attends the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Defence Ministers’ Informal Meeting in Cebu, central Philippines, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. (Jam Sta Rosa/Pool Photo via AP)

U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth attends the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Defence Ministers’ Informal Meeting in Cebu, central Philippines, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. (Jam Sta Rosa/Pool Photo via AP)

This photo provided by the U.S. Army shows Maj. Gen. Brett Sylvia, at a 101st Airborne Division change of command ceremony at Fort Campbell, Ky., May 30, 2025. (Sgt. Timothy Jackson/U.S Army via AP)

This photo provided by the U.S. Army shows Maj. Gen. Brett Sylvia, at a 101st Airborne Division change of command ceremony at Fort Campbell, Ky., May 30, 2025. (Sgt. Timothy Jackson/U.S Army via AP)

WASHINGTON (AP) — Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has fired the Pentagon’s top military planner, a defense official said Wednesday, the latest in a series of generals to be ousted and one that comes even as President Donald Trump is weighing renewed strikes on Iran in the eight-month-long war.

Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia was removed as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff. He is the second general to be ousted from the post, known in military circles as the “J5,” under Hegseth. His predecessor, Lt. Gen. Joseph McGee, was forced to retire last October.

The defense official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive personnel matters, said there is no immediate replacement for Sylvia and no reason has been given for the firing. The move was reported earlier by The Atlantic.

A spokesperson for the Joint Staff said “the Chairman, the Joint Staff, and the Joint Force extend our deepest gratitude to Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia and his family for their 32 years of distinguished service to our nation” and they “wish him and his family the best.”

Typically, the J5 director and their staff are responsible for generating and coordinating military plans with both the chairman of the Joint Chiefs and the president. Sylvia’s firing comes as Trump has repeatedly floated starting new military operations against Iran.

Trump has vowed to “finish the job” in Iran after launching the war with Israel eight months ago and said new strikes are an option after the midterm elections next week.

U.S. officials have told several Middle East countries and regional allies to be prepared for potential renewed military action after Tuesday’s elections as well as for the possibility that Iran will attempt to retaliate against them, two diplomats briefed on the matter said. They say Trump has not made a final decision on new strikes.

A third U.S. aircraft carrier and thousands of additional troops are making their way to the region.

Before arriving at the Joint Staff, Sylvia served as the commander of the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, until May 2025, according to his official biography, which has now been taken offline. He also previously served as the vice director for the J5.

He is the latest in nearly two dozen generals, admirals and other military leaders to be fired, forced to retire or otherwise depart under Hegseth’s tenure — almost all of which have not been publicly explained by the Pentagon. That includes the civilian secretaries of the Army and Navy as well as some top uniformed officers for the military services.

The Pentagon did not immediately respond to messages seeking comment late Wednesday.

Hegseth said last month that he ordered the military to double the cuts to the overall number of top officers to a 20% decrease to be completed by Jan. 1, 2027. There are currently roughly 800 flag and general officer positions.

“I call it accountability and long overdue,” Hegseth told junior officers and enlisted leaders at the Marine Corps Base Quantico on Sept. 30.

Some members of Congress have criticized cuts to the ranks of generals as a “purge” that will take years to rebuild.

“He’s got some kind of like deep-seated grievance about leadership in the military,” Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., a former Navy combat pilot who has been critical of Hegseth, said last month. “He’s purging a generation of great leaders of the military, and it’s going to take a generation to recover from it.”

Associated Press writers Aamer Madhani in Washington and Samy Magdy in New York contributed to this report.

https://breakingdefense.com/2026/10/us-j.heading: US, Japan reach agreements for AMRAAM assembly, SM-3 production boost: Japanese MoD - Breaking Defense
https://breakingdefense.com/2026/10/us-j.body:
WASHINGTON — The US and Japan have finalized a plan to assemble the Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile (AMRAAM) in Japan amid a crunch for munitions, according to Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi.

In remarks posted by the Japanese Defense Ministry, Koizumi confirmed the AMRAAM agreement covers “the establishment of a final assembly and inspection facility in Japan,” according to a Google translation. The weapon is “essential” for F-35 Joint Strike Fighters, Koizumi said, which are operated by Washington and Tokyo among other international partners.

“This is a groundbreaking agreement that will not only ensure the acquisition of equipment needed by both Japan and the United States, but will also strengthen Japan’s defense industry base,” Koizumi said Wednesday during a press conference on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Defense Ministers’ Meeting in the Philippines.

The defense minister did not share which Japanese industry partner was picked to assemble the missile. Koizumi additionally did not include a timeline for opening the facility, or its expected output.

Manufactured by RTX subsidiary Raytheon, the AMRAAM is a key air defense weapon that can be fired by aircraft and ground-based launchers. The missile is in high demand amid conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East, and ramping up its production is a key focus of military planners.

The AMRAAM agreement follows a September contract award to Raytheon worth up to over $20 billion under a five-year agreement, with options for an additional two years of production. That contract will “nearly” double the weapon’s production, the Pentagon said at the time — as long as US lawmakers provide the necessary funding.

Koizumi additionally disclosed that the US and Japan “agreed to share the necessary technical information to achieve increased production” of the Standard Missile-3 Block IIA, a primarily ship-based interceptor used to bat down ballistic missiles. The SM-3 Block IIA is a joint program between the US and Japan, though Koizumi did not share how much the agreement may raise the interceptor’s production rate.

A Tuesday readout of a meeting between Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth published by the Pentagon does not discuss the AMRAAM or SM-3 agreements. However it says Hegseth “welcomed Japan’s efforts to strengthen its defense industrial capacity, and both leaders committed to continue close coordination on critical munitions production.”

RTX deferred to the US Defense Department when asked to comment on the agreements. A Pentagon spokesperson did not respond to an inquiry by press time.

The AMRAAM and SM-3 agreements were both part of “Operation Supercharge,” a joint US-Japan effort to boost defense technology cooperation, according to Koizumi. The two countries are deepening defense ties amid a historic ramp up in defense spending in Japan as the threat of Chinese expansion looms large over the region.

Koizumi and Hegseth “shared a sense of crisis regarding the increasingly severe regional situation and agreed to strengthen the deterrence and response capabilities of the Japan-US alliance at an even faster and stronger pace,” Koizumi said during the Wednesday press conference, without explicitly referencing China.

https://www.thelocal.se/20261029/eu-and-.heading: EU and Canada to bring ties to 'highest' possible level at summit
https://www.thelocal.se/20261029/eu-and-.body:
EU and Canada want to bring their relationship to the "highest level possible" as they face a "world of growing rivalries," the 27-nation bloc's chief said Thursday ahead of a meeting with Canadian leader Mark Carney.

Brussels and Ottawa are to lay the groundwork for an ever-closer partnership at a two-day summit in Montreal, as they navigate uncertain ties with the United States and China.

"We both want to bring our relationship to the highest level possible," von der Leyen said, doubling down on the prospect of Canada becoming the European Union's "first associate member" despite an intra-EU squabble over the term.

Canada and the EU have both been rattled by US President Donald Trump's second term.

Prime Minister Mark Carney has warned relations will not return to a pre-Trump normal and told Canadians that reducing dependence on the United States is an urgent priority.

Ahead of the summit, he promised "a new, ambitious alliance" with the EU.

The EU has equally faced US tariffs, and Trump and his top allies have piled criticism on European political leaders.

China's growing economic heft has also unnerved Brussels, which has moved to protect its industry from what it views as unfair competition from rivals subsidized by Beijing and ease its dependencies on Chinese goods and raw materials.

Brussels and Ottawa could either "go it alone" or "take a more strategic approach with trusted partners that face the same challenges," von der Leyen said.

The EU and Canada already share a free-trade pact, but it has not been fully implemented, and Canadian officials have said businesses are pursuing new opportunities in Europe to offset US tariff-related losses.

An EU official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the new Canadian partnership would align policies in areas such as climate, energy and artificial intelligence, allowing Ottawa to participate in some EU programs.

Canada has huge stocks of the critical minerals needed for green technologies such as batteries and wind turbines that Europe sources mostly from China.

But Canada needs massive infrastructure investment to jump-start its mining industry. The summit could lead to an agreement allowing the European Investment Bank to back Canadian critical mineral projects.

A digital trade deal allowing faster and cheaper online transactions is expected to be unveiled in Montreal.

Ottawa and Brussels are also understood to be working to have Canada participate in the EU's Erasmus youth program, which allows university students to spend a semester abroad, among other things.

Carney said this week he wasn't concerned about associate-member status, or "specific names" to characterize the new alliance.

https://ukranews.com/en/news/1184163-nor.heading: Nord Stream will not resume operations after war: EU finally abandoning russian gas | Ukrainian News Agency
https://ukranews.com/en/news/1184163-nor.body:
The European Union has no plans to resume operations of the Nord Stream gas pipeline after the end of Russia’s war against Ukraine.

The ban on Russian gas will remain in effect regardless of any potential agreements between Moscow and Washington.

The European Commission emphasized that Europe has already recognized the risks of dependence on Russian energy resources, which the Kremlin has used as a tool for political pressure.

"We know far too well the hidden costs of being dependent on Russia for the purchase of fossil fuels.

They have been weaponized and we have been paying the price, so we do not forget that," said European Commission Chief Spokesperson Paula Pinho.

She also pointed out that it was Russia that was the first to cut off gas supplies to Europe.

The European Commission’s position is in line with the course of action outlined by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

Last week, she stated that sanctions against the Russian energy sector will remain in effect until Moscow ends the war.

At the same time, the phase-out of Russian gas is enshrined in separate EU legislation and does not depend solely on sanctions or the course of peace negotiations.

"The legislation in force is not tied to sanctions or any geopolitical events either.

So regardless of what happens, we are phasing out Russian gas and LNG from the European market.

The last shipments should be finished by the end of next year," said Anna-Kaisa Itkonen, the European Commission’s spokesperson on energy.

According to the EU’s plan, imports of Russian gas are to be phased out by the end of 2027.

Short-term contracts for the supply of liquefied natural gas (LNG) have already been terminated, and long-term LNG contracts are set to expire by January 2027.

The final phase involves ending contracts for pipeline gas supplies, particularly those previously linked to the Nord Stream pipeline.

These are scheduled to end by September 2027.

Reversing or altering this course would require a new proposal from the European Commission and the support of a qualified majority of EU member states.

Canadian and EU leaders, however, dropped the idea of associate EU membership from their joint declaration, seen by Reuters, ​agreeing instead to an "ever closer association."
